assessments.title: AC Requirements Of Anonymity And High Operational Security
assessments.description: Mandates anonymity and operational security for Alignment Conservers and defines penalties for breaches.
assessments.quote: The Alignment Conserver roles of Facilitator and Aligned Delegate require anonymity and high levels of operational security. Breaches of these anonymity and operational security requirements are considered serious misalignment. In the event of such breaches, the known identities of individuals holding these AC roles shall be promptly derecognized, and they will be barred from further participation as Alignment Conservers.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires 'anonymity' and 'high levels of operational security' without any quantifiable metrics, thresholds, or verifiable criteria. Compliance is entirely a matter of judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph states a consequence (derecognition and barring) but does not specify who enforces it or through what process. Only the generic misalignment reporting and adjudication backstops would apply, which are weak.

assessments.title: Signal Account Requirement
assessments.description: Requires Ranked Delegates to maintain active Signal accounts and mandates regular status verification by the Core Facilitator.
assessments.quote:
RDs are required to maintain an active Signal account to facilitate communications related to emergency / urgent situations. This requirement applies regardless of whether an RD has been appointed to the Emergency Response Group. See [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf). RDs must provide their Signal username to the Core Facilitator.

The Core Facilitator is responsible for maintaining an internal registry of RDs' Signal accounts. Because the ranked RDs are continually changing, the Core Facilitator must ensure that the internal registry is maintained on a frequent basis. The Core Facilitator must check the active status of the RDs' Signal accounts by sending test messages and confirming the RDs' timely response; this must be done regularly, on a schedule known only to the Core Facilitator. If an RD fails to timely respond to the test messages, the Core Facilitator must remove them from RD status.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes obligations on RDs and the Core Facilitator with qualitative terms like 'active', 'timely response', 'frequent basis', and 'regularly', making compliance arguable; no numeric thresholds or verifiable metrics are provided.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule states a direct consequence (removal from RD status) but no enforcement mechanism from the catalog or document UUIDs is cited; only the catch-all misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Tier 2 (Integrity) Breaches
assessments.description: Defines integrity breaches and immediate derecognition for Aligned Delegates to protect governance security.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule lists seven specific breach categories, but most rely on qualitative judgments (e.g., 'unsubstantiated', 'inflammatory', 'proven dishonesty', 'intended to manipulate'). Only item 6 provides an objectively verifiable condition. No numeric thresholds or metrics are given, making compliance arguable for most categories.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule states immediate derecognition as a consequence, but no specific enforcement mechanism from the rubric's catalog or the paragraph text reaches this rule. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Emergency Contact Mechanism
assessments.description: Requires Aligned Delegates to register for and follow approved emergency contact mechanism procedures.
assessments.quote:
Aligned Delegates must safeguard the security of the Sky Protocol through the Executive Vote process. To deal with emergencies related to Executive Votes, ADs are required to sign up for the approved emergency contact mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.3.2.2 - Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms](57006d4e-cd91-4565-97b5-5fab73fa94d5).

ADs must strictly adhere to all onboarding procedures and usage instructions associated with this emergency contact mechanism. ADs that fail to do so will be considered in misalignment and will be derecognized.

The high operational security requirements applicable to ADs extend to their use of the emergency contact mechanism.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires ADs to sign up for a specific emergency contact mechanism and adhere to its procedures, but the procedures themselves are defined externally, leaving the operative criteria delegated. No quantifiable metrics are provided.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The consequence of derecognition is stated, but enforcement relies solely on the generic misalignment/adjudication process, which is weak. No specific enforcement mechanism from the catalog reaches this rule.

assessments.title: Protocol Security Workstream Lead Requirements
assessments.description: Defines expertise and conflict of interest requirements for the Protocol Security Workstream Lead role.
assessments.quote: The Protocol Security Workstream Lead role must be held by an individual with demonstrated expertise in protocol security, smart contract security, and operational security practices. The individual must not have involvement in any business, political, or governance-related activities that could create a conflict of interest, either directly or indirectly.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes qualitative requirements ('demonstrated expertise', 'no involvement that could create a conflict of interest') with no metrics, thresholds, or verifiable criteria; compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is weak.

assessments.title: Emergency Response System
assessments.description: Defines a protocol for managing emergencies outside of standard governance cycles.
assessments.quote: This Article defines a general emergency response protocol for managing emergencies or urgent situations outside of the standard Weekly Governance Cycle and Monthly Governance Cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The text is a purely aspirational statement that an emergency response protocol is defined; it contains no metrics, thresholds, actors, deadlines, or verifiable conditions, and imposes no concrete obligations.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph imposes no specific obligations, so no enforcement mechanism applies beyond the generic misalignment backstop.

assessments.title: Definition Of Emergency Situations
assessments.description: Defines emergency situations and grants the Core Facilitator discretion to trigger expedited emergency response processes.
assessments.quote:
An emergency situation is any situation that would require immediate intervention to prevent initiation of Emergency Shutdown, severe peg divergence, or harm to members and users of the Ecosystem.

Pursuant to [A.0.1.2.1 - Core Council’s Broad Discretionary Capacity](f18229fe-fbc3-4dc8-ad84-4bca2915f6c4), the Core Facilitator has broad discretion to apply the emergency-situation processes defined in [A.1.9.1 - Emergency Response](20dcf582-8862-48b3-9ca9-c3703871bd14) to urgent situations. Urgent situations are defined as any situation that involves a time-sensitive matter that would need an expedited governance process, where following a standard governance cycle would be too slow, risk a larger problem, or constitute an important missed opportunity.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines emergency and urgent situations entirely in qualitative, judgment-based language ('immediate intervention', 'severe peg divergence', 'harm to members', 'time-sensitive matter', 'too slow', 'risk a larger problem', 'important missed opportunity') with no numeric thresholds, metrics, formulas, or verifiable conditions. Compliance is arguable either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is a definition and a grant of discretion to the Core Facilitator; it imposes no compliance obligation on any regulated party and creates no specific consequence for misuse of that discretion. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Group Membership Criteria
assessments.description: Defines the composition and required capabilities of the Emergency Response Group.
assessments.quote: The membership of the Emergency Response Group may change at the discretion of Core GovOps, and as circumstances require. Generally, the Emergency Response Group should contain domain-expert Ecosystem Actors as well as governance decision-makers. The group must be able to diagnose a situation, suggest a short-term mitigation and act on such mitigation. The group should also be able to define the path forward for a long-term solution to the problem and act on it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states qualitative obligations ('should contain domain-expert Ecosystem Actors', 'must be able to diagnose', 'should be able to define') with no numeric thresholds, metrics, cadence, or verifiable conditions. Compliance is entirely judgment-based.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this membership criteria rule. The catch-all misalignment/adjudication backstop is the only possible path, which is always weak. Core GovOps' discretion over membership is self-enforcement.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Group Membership
assessments.description: Defines the membership update process for the Emergency Response Group via Core GovOps.
assessments.quote:
The membership of the Emergency Response Group is defined as Active Data in [A.1.9.1.2.2.0.6.1 - Emergency Response Group Current Membership](e9807449-fdc3-4860-8d53-c56181311618).

The Active Data is updated as follows:

- The Responsible Party is Core GovOps.
- The Update Process must follow the protocol for ‘Direct Edit’.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a responsible party (Core GovOps) and a specific update process ('Direct Edit'), but the process itself is delegated to an external protocol with no quantified thresholds, metrics, or verifiable steps stated in the text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is weak.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Group Team Members
assessments.description: Defines staffing requirements and operational resilience standards for the Emergency Response Group.
assessments.quote:
Where an Emergency Response Group Member is a team, that team should assign two (2) of its own team members to be responsible for incident response.

A team may assign more than two (2) of its team members to be responsible for incident response at the discretion of Core GovOps.

To the extent possible, the selected team members should be in different timezones and jurisdictions for maximum operational and regulatory resilience.

The team members assigned to the Emergency Response Group should not be disclosed publicly under any circumstances as this could make them targets.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a numeric threshold (two team members) and a defined actor (team that is an Emergency Response Group Member), but uses 'should' instead of a mandatory term, making the obligation non-binding. The additional requirements (timezone/jurisdiction diversity, non-disclosure) are entirely qualitative and conditional ('to the extent possible').
metrics: two (2) of its own team members
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific consequence is defined for failing to assign two team members; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak. The rule uses 'should' indicating a recommendation rather than a mandatory requirement, further weakening enforceability.

assessments.title: Additional Emergency Response Team Members
assessments.description: Permits Soter Labs to assign more than two team members to emergency response communication channels and calls.
assessments.quote: Soter Labs is permitted to assign more than two (2) of its team members to the permissioned Emergency Response Communication Channels defined in [A.1.9.1.3 - Emergency Response Communication Channels](18418289-ada8-401d-a992-7e38b235c866), as well as any Emergency Response calls.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a specific actor (Soter Labs), a numeric threshold (more than two), and defined targets (Emergency Response Communication Channels and calls). A third party can verify whether Soter Labs has assigned more than two members to those channels.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is a permissive grant, not an obligation or prohibition; there is no violation to enforce, and no enforcement mechanism is needed or cited.

assessments.title: Aligned Delegate Membership In Emergency Response Group
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps approval for Aligned Delegates to join the Emergency Response Group.
assessments.quote:
Aligned Delegate membership in the Emergency Response Group is not automatic based on amount of delegated SKY or Ranked Delegate status. An Aligned Delegate seeking to participate in emergency response must be reviewed and approved by Core GovOps prior to joining the Emergency Response Group.

Core GovOps has discretion to approve or deny Aligned Delegate participation in the Emergency Response Group based on their assessment of the Aligned Delegate's competence and reliability.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires Core GovOps approval based on 'competence and reliability', which are entirely qualitative and undefined; no metrics, thresholds, or deadlines exist, making compliance arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is mentioned; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Signal Group
assessments.description: Defines the creation, administration, and usage requirements for the Emergency Response Signal Group.
assessments.quote:
A unique Signal "Emergency Response" Group will be used for all incident response coordination.

TechOps Services will create the Signal Group and assign its administrators.

Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead shall manage access to the Signal Group. All Emergency Response Members must be added to the Group.

Where an Emergency Response Group Member is a team, the two (2) team members responsible for incident response are required to join the Signal Group.

The Signal Group should not be used for any purpose except communications concerning a potential emergency situation. The Group must be configured to have a four-week message retention.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies exact actors (TechOps Services, Core GovOps, Protocol Security Workstream Lead), a numeric threshold for team members (two), and a quantified configuration (four-week message retention). A third party could verify compliance from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is weak.

assessments.title: Emergency Contact Mechanism
assessments.description: Requires Emergency Response Group members to use a validated emergency contact mechanism.
assessments.quote: Emergency Response Group Members must use an emergency contact mechanism to deal with emergencies. This emergency contact mechanism is selected and validated by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes a real obligation to use an emergency contact mechanism, but the mechanism is not defined; it is delegated to the Protocol Security Workstream Lead to select and validate. No metrics, thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable conditions are stated, making compliance arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific consequence attaches to violating this rule. The Emergency Response System (A.1.9) provides a general escalation protocol but does not define a penalty for failing to use the validated contact mechanism. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Emergency Contact Mechanism Selection Criteria
assessments.description: Defines technical and operational criteria for selecting emergency response communication mechanisms.
assessments.quote:
A suitable emergency contact mechanism should meet the following criteria:

- The mechanism should use enterprise grade infrastructure with correspondingly high levels of uptime.
- The mechanism should not require personal information or KYC from users.
- The mechanism should allow segmenting of target user groups, so that required individuals are only notified when necessary.
- The mechanism should be able to bypass silent / do not disturb mode on devices to achieve an immediate response any time of day.
- It is recommended, but not required, that the mechanism minimizes data tracking of individual users.
- It is recommended, but not required, that the mechanism is open source.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule lists qualitative criteria (e.g., 'enterprise grade infrastructure', 'high levels of uptime') without any numeric thresholds, metrics, or verifiable conditions. Compliance is arguable based on interpretation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism is specified for these selection criteria. Only the generic misalignment backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms
assessments.description: Designates PagerDuty as the approved mechanism for emergency response communications.
assessments.quote: The currently approved emergency contact mechanism is PagerDuty.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a specific, verifiable mechanism (PagerDuty), but it is phrased as a statement of fact rather than an explicit obligation, and no actor is defined; a third party could check compliance but the text lacks an operative command.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism from the catalog directly reaches this designation; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Changes To Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms
assessments.description: Defines the consultation and governance process for changing approved emergency contact mechanisms.
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator may recommend changing the approved emergency contact mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.3.2.2 - Approved Emergency Contact Mechanisms](57006d4e-cd91-4565-97b5-5fab73fa94d5), but they must do so in consultation with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. The Core Facilitator’s recommendation is subject to a poll through the Operational Weekly Governance Cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete actors (Core Facilitator, Protocol Security Workstream Lead) and a defined step (poll through Operational Weekly Governance Cycle), but lacks quantitative thresholds, criteria for when a change is warranted, or voting requirements, leaving the operative decision qualitative and delegated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or implied for this procedural rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Emergency Contact Mechanism Fire Drills
assessments.description: Allows security leads to conduct and publish results of emergency response preparedness drills.
assessments.quote: The Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core Facilitator may run firedrills to test the preparedness of individuals that have been added to the emergency contact mechanism. This will be done at the discretion of the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core Facilitator. The results of firedrills shall be published to maintain transparency.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule grants discretion to run drills and requires publication of results, but no thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or verifiable criteria are specified; compliance is qualitative and arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment backstop applies, which is weak.

assessments.title: Emergency Response Roles And Responsibilities
assessments.description: Defines the authority and responsibilities for declaring and coordinating emergency response processes.
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator is empowered to declare an emergency situation.

After an emergency situation has been declared, Core GovOps is responsible for coordinating emergency-situation processes to ensure they are civil, consistently applied and aligned. The Core Facilitator is responsible for publishing Polls and Executive Votes.

Any participant in the Sky Ecosystem, including Ecosystem Actors, Aligned Delegates or other community members, can request that the Core Facilitator declare an emergency. The Core Facilitator is granted broad discretion in handling such requests.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule assigns roles and a process but uses only qualitative language ('empowered to declare', 'broad discretion') with no metrics, thresholds, or verifiable conditions. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific consequence or enforcement mechanism is attached to these role assignments; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Incident Validation
assessments.description: Defines the Core Facilitator's responsibility for validating reported incidents as emergencies.
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator is responsible for determining whether a reported incident is a valid emergency; where possible, this can be done in consultation with relevant stakeholders.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule assigns a responsibility to the Core Facilitator to determine valid emergencies, but provides no criteria, thresholds, or verifiable conditions; it is a qualitative judgment call.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this validation duty; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is weak.

assessments.title: Incident Categorization
assessments.description: Assigns the Core Facilitator the responsibility of categorizing emergencies by severity and other criteria.
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator is responsible for categorizing emergencies according to their severity and other pertinent criteria.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule assigns a responsibility to the Core Facilitator but provides no quantifiable criteria, thresholds, metrics, or verifiable conditions for categorization. It is expressed entirely in judgment language ('according to their severity and other pertinent criteria'), making compliance arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism targets this duty. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop (c6c6f595, 560e1024) could apply, which alone is always weak. No on-chain automatic enforcement, capital at risk, or named penalty path reaches this rule.

assessments.title: Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger
assessments.description: Mandates TechOps to trigger emergency notifications and requires group members to acknowledge incidents via a specific mechanism.
assessments.quote: Upon receiving notification from the Core Facilitator of a validated and categorized emergency situation, TechOps Services must trigger a notification in the Emergency Contact Mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.3.2 - Emergency Contact Mechanism](3efb0238-aaae-4351-9ec9-31902f3a1394). All Emergency Response Group Members are required to acknowledge the incident in a timely manner through the Emergency Contact Mechanism. The notification must include a link to the official Emergency Response video call ("war room").
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names specific actors (TechOps Services, Emergency Response Group Members) and actions (trigger notification, acknowledge, include link), but the timing requirement 'in a timely manner' is qualitative and unquantified, leaving compliance arguable.

assessments.title: Emergency Declaration Procedure
assessments.description: Defines the Core Facilitator's authority and communication protocols for declaring and managing emergency situations.
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator is empowered to declare an emergency situation at their discretion, either on their own initiative or in response to a request from a community member.

When declaring an emergency, the Core Facilitator should create a formal post on the Sky Forum, providing sufficient detail regarding the issue and explaining why immediate action is required. If the situation allows, the Core Facilitator should post the emergency declaration on the Sky Forum before taking action. If the urgency of the situation requires immediate intervention without delay, the Core Facilitator should create the Forum post as soon as possible after, or simultaneously with, the emergency action.

There may be situations in which a public Emergency Declaration would be counterproductive to security objectives; the Core Facilitator is granted discretion in these matters.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names an actor (Core Facilitator) and a communication action (Sky Forum post), but all operative criteria are qualitative: 'at their discretion', 'sufficient detail', 'as soon as possible', and a discretionary exception for public declarations. No numeric thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable metrics exist; compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule's violation modes. The Core Facilitator's emergency declaration procedure is not backed by any named penalty, on-chain automatic enforcement, or distinct enforcer. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop (c6c6f595, 560e1024) would apply, which is always weak.

Core GovOps, in consultation with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, must regularly evaluate the emergency preparedness of the Emergency Response Group. This can be done through running fire drills or through extensive postmortems after an actual incident.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Accountability Measures for Ecosystem Actor Individuals And Teams
assessments.description: Defines the process for documenting and removing Emergency Response Group members for performance deficiencies.
assessments.quote:
For Ecosystem Actors appointed to the Emergency Response Group, fulfilling the responsibilities of this role is as critical to their overall performance evaluation as their customary deliverables.

Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead are required to document all instances of Emergency Response Group Members’ failure to meet emergency-preparedness requirements. Given their domain expertise and proximity to each emergency situation, Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead are granted the discretion to evaluate emergency-preparedness deficiencies. Generally, they are required to take swift action to address non-negligible emergency-preparedness deficiencies in the following manner.

If the deficient Emergency Response Group Member is an Ecosystem Actor individual, the individual should be removed from the Group.

If the deficient Emergency Response Group Member is part of an Ecosystem Actor team, the specific member who has failed to meet requirements should be removed from the Group.

If different Emergency Response Group Members from the same Ecosystem Actor team consistently fail to meet requirements, the Ecosystem Actor team as a whole should be removed from the Group.

The removal of a Member from the Group is done at the discretion of Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. However, Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead may not proceed with removal unless it is supported with clear documentation.

When an Ecosystem Actor is removed from the Emergency Response Group for deficient performance, Core GovOps must transparently announce this action via a post to the Sky Forum. Further, the removal must be incorporated into the evaluation of the Ecosystem Actor’s overall performance.

Core GovOps has the discretion to decide if documentation supporting the removal should be retained internally or publicly shared on the Forum (with redactions, if needed).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a process for documenting and removing members for performance deficiencies, but the core condition 'failure to meet emergency-preparedness requirements' is entirely qualitative and left to the discretion of Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. No metrics, thresholds, or objective criteria are provided, making compliance arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule relies on Core GovOps and the Workstream Lead to evaluate and remove members, which is self-enforcement. No external enforcement mechanism like on-chain automatic action, capital at risk, or a named penalty process reaches this rule. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop exists, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Accountability Measures For Alignment Conservers
assessments.description: Defines the process for documenting and executing the removal of emergency response group members for performance deficiencies.
assessments.quote:
For an Alignment Conserver who has been appointed to the Emergency Response Group, the requirements of this role become as critical to the assessment of their overall performance as their customary obligations.

Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead are required to document all instances of Emergency Response Group Members’ failure to meet emergency-preparedness requirements. Given their domain expertise and proximity to each emergency situation, Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead are granted the discretion to evaluate emergency-preparedness deficiencies. Generally, they are required to take swift action to address non-negligible emergency-preparedness deficiencies in the following manner.

Where the deficient Member is an Alignment Conserver, that Member should be derecognized pursuant to [A.1.5.9 - Adjudication Process](560e1024-0897-4f1e-ae71-3ba31e29ed57).

Where the deficient Alignment Conserver is the Core Facilitator, the Protocol Security Workstream Lead and Core GovOps must reach consensus in order to initiate a derecognition proceeding against the Core Facilitator. Once this threshold is met, the procedure defined in [A.1.5.9 - Adjudication Process](560e1024-0897-4f1e-ae71-3ba31e29ed57) should be followed. In the interim, Core GovOps selects an Operational Facilitator to step in temporarily and assist with coordinating emergency response.

The initiation of derecognition is done at the discretion of the Core Facilitator (or Core GovOps) and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. However, the Core Facilitator and Protocol Security Workstream Lead may not proceed with removal unless it is supported with clear documentation.

When an Alignment Conserver is removed from the Emergency Response Group and derecognized for deficient performance, the Core Facilitator must transparently announce this action pursuant to [A.1.5.10.1 - Derecognition Notice](9c05207d-5e11-43ae-a8a3-1b61734d6ef9).

The Core Facilitator has the discretion to decide if documentation supporting the Alignment Conserver’s derecognition and removal should be retained internally or publicly shared on the Forum (with redactions, if needed).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a process for documenting and derecognizing Alignment Conservers for emergency-preparedness deficiencies, but the criteria for 'deficiencies' and 'non-negligible' are entirely qualitative and left to the discretion of Core GovOps and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead. No metrics, thresholds, or deadlines are provided, making compliance arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule relies solely on the Adjudication Process (A.1.5.9), a catch-all mechanism, to derecognize a member. No automatic, on-chain, or quantified penalty mechanism is specified; the consequence is entirely dependent on discretionary initiation by the same actors evaluating performance.

assessments.title: Chainlog
assessments.description: Defines the process for updating the on-chain registry of core smart contract addresses via Executive Votes.
assessments.quote: The Chainlog is an on-chain, governance-managed registry that records the official addresses of Sky’s core smart contracts. Each contract entry in the Chainlog is identified by a unique key ("Chainlog key"), which is used to reference the contract in documentation, governance actions, and integrations. It serves as the single source of truth for contract addresses in the protocol. The Chainlog is available at [https://chainlog.skyeco.com/](https://chainlog.skyeco.com/). Updates to the Chainlog are defined as housekeeping items (see [A.1.11.1.5.1.1 - Definition Of Housekeeping Items](7648bf12-d600-4e0d-807b-5eb18e8d0f4f)) and can be included directly in an Executive Vote (see [A.1.11.1.5.1.2 - Process for Adding Housekeeping Item In Executive Vote](2d165c27-5daf-4a84-af8c-7c36f5de03d2)).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete process: Chainlog updates are classified as housekeeping items and can be included directly in an Executive Vote, with referenced process docs. However, it provides no quantified thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or qualifying criteria; operative details are delegated to the referenced documents.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism from the rubric catalog or the paragraph reaches this update-classification rule. The Chainlog is described as governance-managed, but no penalty, emergency, artifact-review, or on-chain enforcement path is specified; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would remain, which is weak.

assessments.title: Executive Vote

assessments.quote: Executive Vote refers to the voting process of approving governance proposals within Sky Governance. These votes are conducted onchain and are used to implement technical changes to the Sky Protocol. For an Executive Vote to be executed, it must accumulate more SKY token support than any other active proposal, including the current leading proposal, ensuring it reflects the highest level of community backing at the time of approval.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a fully quantified, objectively verifiable condition: an Executive Vote must accumulate more SKY token support than any other active proposal. This is a numeric comparison that can be checked on-chain by any third party.

assessments.title: Spell Team
assessments.description: Defines the required composition and separation of duties for Spell Teams during the Executive Vote process.
assessments.quote: Each Executive Vote has a dedicated Spell Team, made up of Spell Crafters and Spell Reviewers. The Spell Team must include one Crafter, who is responsible for crafting the Spells. The Spell Team must also include at least two Reviewers, responsible for reviewing and confirming that the Spells are ready for the Executive Vote, at least one of whom should be a member of a different Ecosystem Actor than the Spell Crafter. A Crafter cannot serve as a Reviewer for the same Spell. The Spell Team is a set of technical contributors working on developing all technical and smart-contract-related aspects of a particular Executive Vote, based on instructions set out by the Governance Point.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies exact numbers (one Crafter, at least two Reviewers) and a clear prohibition (Crafter cannot be Reviewer). The requirement for a Reviewer from a different Ecosystem Actor uses 'should' rather than 'must', creating a minor ambiguity, but the core obligations are quantified and verifiable.
metrics: at least one Reviewer from a different Ecosystem Actor (should)
Crafter cannot serve as a Reviewer

assessments.title: Spell Crafter

assessments.quote: The Spell Crafter (the Crafter) is the person or entity who parses the written instruction set of a proposed Executive to Solidity code in order to develop the Spell in the first instance. Every addition, modification, or removal of code or content within the Spell must be performed by the Crafter. The designated Spell Crafter must be rotated, such that the same person does not craft the Spells for two consecutive Executive Votes. The Spell Crafter is a member of the Spell Team for a particular Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a clear, binary condition: the same person must not craft spells for two consecutive Executive Votes. This is objectively verifiable by checking the identity of the crafter for each vote.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or implied; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Governance Point And Governance Backup
assessments.description: Defines the roles and responsibilities of the Governance Point and Backup during the executive process.
assessments.quote:
The Governance Point is the Core Facilitator. Currently, the only Core Facilitator is JanSky. Each Spell also has a designated Governance Backup. The Governance Backup is required to assume the responsibilities of the Governance Point if the original Governance Point becomes unavailable, effectively stepping into the role as needed. The Governance Point is responsible for coordinating the Executive Vote and ensuring that the information in the Executive Sheet accurately reflects the progress of the Spell.

The Technical Point has domain expertise as the crafter of the smart contracts, but the Governance Point also has crucial context and should serve as a cross-check to the extent they can. The Governance Point is expected to ask questions where needed.

assessments.quote: The role of Governance Point and Governance Backup alternates from within the Core Facilitator. The positions rotate, following an internal schedule.

assessments.title: Responsibilities For Governance Point
assessments.description: Defines the Governance Point's duties for preparing, verifying, and publishing Executive Votes and code.
assessments.quote:
The Governance Point has the following responsibilities in the Executive process:

- Gather the proposed content for the Executive sheet and prepare a draft of the Executive Vote.
- Align on Executive Vote contents with the relevant teams, and coordinate technical details.
- Ensure the contents of each Executive Vote are justified by processes or structures ratified by Sky Governance.
- Produce the text (Executive Document) that accompanies each Executive Vote and verify that the delivered code matches the code reviewed and approved on GitHub and that it contains all expected actions from the sheet.
- Publish the Executive Vote on the official Voting Portal.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule lists concrete responsibilities, including a verifiable condition (code matches GitHub and sheet), but lacks any numeric thresholds, deadlines, or defined verification process. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment reporting and adjudication backstops apply, which are weak. No on-chain automatic enforcement, capital at risk, or named penalty path is tied to these duties.

assessments.title: Technical Point
assessments.description: Defines the roles and communication hierarchy for the Spell Team during the technical development process.
assessments.quote:
The Technical Point role is filled by the Spell Team or the Spell Crafter from that group. For each Executive Vote, a Spell Team is selected from the Spell Roster to steward the Spell development process.

Within the Spell Team, the Spell Crafter serves as the primary point of contact for the Governance Point and any external parties. If the Spell Crafter is unavailable or if disagreements arise, the Governance Point’s secondary point of contact is the Spell Reviewers.

Input or opinions from external parties on technical details should be treated as informational and should not influence the Spell decision-making process.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines roles and a communication hierarchy but contains no quantified metrics, thresholds, or verifiable conditions; compliance is entirely qualitative and arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Spell Team Configuration
assessments.description: Defines the mandatory rotation and composition of the Spell Team for crafting and reviewing spells.
assessments.quote:
The Spell Team consists of the Crafter(s) and Reviewers for a designated Spell.

Currently, Sky has two teams of technical contributors for Spell development, Dewiz, and Sidestream. They rotate the responsibility of crafting and reviewing as follows:

- When Dewiz is crafting:
    - Crafting: one Dewiz member
    - Reviewing: one Dewiz member, one Sidestream member
- When Sidestream is crafting:
    - Crafting: one Sidestream member
    - Reviewing: one Sidestream member, one Dewiz member.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies exact team composition and rotation: when Dewiz crafts, one Dewiz member crafts and one Dewiz plus one Sidestream review; the symmetric for Sidestream. A third party can verify compliance from the text alone.
metrics: Crafting: one Dewiz member; Reviewing: one Dewiz member, one Sidestream member
Crafting: one Sidestream member; Reviewing: one Sidestream member, one Dewiz member

A Prime Agent's spell items are the onchain changes that require a Spell to execute. assessments.title: Office Hours
assessments.description: Defines conditions and execution timeframes for the Office Hours modifier during Spell execution.
assessments.quote:
Office hours are set to "Yes" if a Spell introduces major changes that can affect external parties, or if a stakeholder makes a specific request for the office-hours modifier to be switched on. Typical examples include collateral offboarding, onboarding new modules, oracle changes, and other actions that may have a significant impact on the protocol or its users.

While stakeholders can request that Office Hours be switched on, the final decision and responsibility for setting this parameter rests with the Spell Crafter. If the office hours modifier is on, the Spell can only be executed between 14:00 and 21:00 UTC, Monday - Friday. The purpose of this modifier is to ensure that Ecosystem Actors are available to address any issues that may arise during or shortly after the execution of the Spell. The Spell will have an extra restriction on top of the GSM Pause Delay, meaning it can only be cast during that timeframe, regardless of when it was approved.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a concrete execution window (14:00-21:00 UTC, Mon-Fri) but the condition for activating the modifier is qualitative ('major changes', 'significant impact', 'specific request'), leaving the trigger to judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Spell Crafter's decision to set office hours could be reviewed under Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7), which can lead to findings and penalty assessment, providing a general mechanism that reaches this rule, though no consequence is quantified for this specific rule.

- (optional) Authority is given to the protocol owner: `MCD_PAUSE_PROXY` in the case of SKY and denied from the deployer address.
- Include instructions to be added to the Executive Sheet, such as adding the module to the chainlog, defining parameters for the module (provided by the Risk Advisor), further authorization that needs to be done to different module elements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule enumerates specific, objectively verifiable items that must be present in a forum post. A third party can check compliance by inspecting the post for each listed element; no judgment is required.
metrics: link to the audit reports as specified in A.1.10.2.7.6, hosted on the auditor's website or another independently verifiable source
confirmation that the deployed code matches the commit hash that was sent for audit
constructor arguments are as expected in the Init script
instructions to be added to the Executive Sheet
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Neither cited mechanism reaches this rule: Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) governs standing Agent Artifacts, not a per-spell executive-process forum post, and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) apply to Primes' Risk Capital shortfalls — wrong actor and violation mode. Only the generic misalignment backstop remains, so weak.

assessments.title: Core Facilitator Approve Inclusion In Executive Vote
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to approve technical scope inclusion via a forum reply for Executive Votes.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is identified; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Governance Point Includes Module Deployment In The Executive Sheet
assessments.description: Mandates specific documentation and linking requirements for module deployment within the governance executive sheet.

The Reasoning URL for the "Input Action" should contain a link to the Atlas Edit Proposal Forum post specified in [A.1.10.2.3.2.1.2.1.2 - Technical Scope Forum Post](ef6d73e5-cdcb-48dd-873c-264c07af80bf) and the Authority URL for the "Input Action" should contain a link to Atlas documents. The "Derived Action" is more specific for deployment address and other necessary information. The Reasoning URL for the "Derived Action" should contain a link to the Technical Scope Forum post specified in [A.1.10.2.3.2.1.2.1.2 - Technical Scope Forum Post](ef6d73e5-cdcb-48dd-873c-264c07af80bf) and the Authority URL for the "Derived Action" should contain a link to the approval of the Core Facilitator as specified in [A.1.10.2.3.2.1.2.1.3 - Core Facilitator Approve Inclusion In Executive Vote](d0c4f880-902e-4d32-ac55-f05725753ac1).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies exact fields (Input Action, Derived Action, Reasoning URL, Authority URL) and the required content for each (links to specific documents), but the obligation is expressed as 'should' rather than 'must', making compliance arguable. A third party could verify the presence of the links, but the non-mandatory language introduces ambiguity.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or implied. The rule is a procedural documentation requirement; failure to include the links would at most result in the proposal being rejected by governance, which is self-enforcement and not a defined consequence. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Confirmation Of Module Deployment In The Executive Sheet
assessments.description: Requires the Forum post author to confirm module deployment in the Executive Sheet.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states that the author 'usually acts as Content Liaison and confirms in the Executive Sheet' — 'usually' is non-mandatory, and no metric, threshold, deadline, or verifiable condition is provided. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific consequence attaches to this confirmation step; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, which is always weak. No on-chain, capital-at-risk, or named enforcement mechanism reaches this rule.

assessments.title: Core Facilitator Includes Module Deployment In The Executive Document
assessments.description: Mandates specific documentation requirements for module deployment within the Executive Document.

The Core Facilitator must include the module deployment in the Executive Document. The format for this content should be as specified below:

assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or implicitly reaches this documentation requirement; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is weak.

assessments.title: Prime Spells
assessments.description: The protocol promises to define the Prime Spell specification in a future Atlas iteration.
assessments.quote: This process will be further specified in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule explicitly defers specification to a future iteration, containing only a placeholder with no operative obligation; a third party cannot verify compliance from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule currently imposes no verifiable duty, so no enforcement mechanism applies; it is a stub.

assessments.title: Purpose
assessments.description: Establishes binding enforcement and recordkeeping for Prime Agent Spell security during framework codification.
assessments.quote: Prime Spell Security Enforcement establishes binding enforcement and formal recordkeeping for Prime Agent Spell security during the period when the Prime Spell Security Framework is progressively codified and operationalized in the Atlas. Its objective is to protect the Executive Process by ensuring that Prime Agents adhere to all applicable security requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a purpose statement with no quantifiable metrics, thresholds, formulas, or verifiable conditions. It declares an objective but provides no operative text that a third party could use to check compliance.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is referenced; the paragraph only states an intent to establish enforcement. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Obligation To Comply With Prime Spell Security Guidelines
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to follow security guidelines to participate in Executive Votes.
assessments.quote: Prime Agents must adhere to all Prime Spell Security Guidelines as a condition of inclusion in an Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names an actor (Prime Agents) and a condition (inclusion in an Executive Vote), but the actual requirements are entirely delegated to 'Prime Spell Security Guidelines' which are not defined in this paragraph. A third party cannot verify compliance from this text alone; the obligation is qualitative and unquantified.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule states exclusion from the Executive Vote as a consequence, but no mechanism doc from the rubric's catalog or appearing in the text enforces this gatekeeping. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Determination Of Occurrence Of Prime Spell Security Incident And Penalties
assessments.description: Grants Core Facilitator and GovOps discretion to identify security incidents and impose penalties.
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator and Core GovOps, in consultation with other appropriate stakeholders, have full discretion to determine whether a Prime Spell Security Incident has occurred and to impose appropriate penalties.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule grants full discretion to named actors to determine an incident and impose penalties, but provides no quantitative thresholds, metrics, or verifiable criteria; compliance is entirely judgment-based.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism ensures the Core Facilitator or GovOps exercise their discretion; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Penalties
assessments.description: Defines potential penalties for Primes following a security incident during the executive spell process.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule enumerates categories of penalties but provides no quantified thresholds, criteria for application, or defined process. It is entirely qualitative and leaves compliance arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule merely lists possible penalties without specifying any automatic or defined enforcement path. Imposition depends on discretionary governance action, and no specific mechanism ensures these penalties are applied; only the generic misalignment backstop exists.

assessments.title: Prime Agent And Operational Executor Agent Produce Prime Spell Security Incident Report
assessments.description: Requires Prime and Operational Executor Agents to produce a security incident report after a Prime Spell incident.
assessments.quote: After a Prime Spell Security Incident has occurred, the Prime and its Operational Executor Agent must promptly produce a Prime Spell Security Incident Report using the designated template.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes a real obligation to produce a report after an incident, but 'promptly' is a qualitative judgment with no deadline, making compliance arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Failure to produce the incident report would be a security practice deficiency, directly triggering higher insurance fees under the Risk-Based Pricing Of Insurance mechanism (fd1f682c), a priced incentive that is strong.

assessments.title: Delay In Submitting Or Failure To Thoroughly And Accurately Complete Report
assessments.description: Defines reporting failures as security incidents subject to Core Council determination and penalties.
assessments.quote: Unreasonable delay in submitting the Report, or failure to thoroughly and accurately complete it (including omission of relevant facts), as determined by the Core Council, constitutes a separate Prime Spell Security Incident and may result in additional penalties.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule relies entirely on qualitative judgment ('unreasonable delay', 'thoroughly and accurately', 'as determined by the Core Council') with no numeric thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable criteria. Compliance is arguable on the same facts, so it is at most preciseness 2.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule defines a reporting failure as a separate Prime Spell Security Incident. The Risk-Based Pricing Of Insurance via the Prime Spell Security Registry (fd1f682c) directly links such incidents to higher insurance fees for the Prime, creating a concrete, priced consequence with a defined path from Core Council determination through incident recording to fee adjustment.

assessments.title: Core Spell Teams Review Prime Spell Security Incident Report
assessments.description: Requires Core Spell Teams to review Incident Reports for completeness and accuracy.
assessments.quote: The relevant Core Spell Team, on behalf of the Core Council, must review this Incident Report for completeness and accuracy.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is qualitative: 'review ... for completeness and accuracy' with no numeric thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or cadence. The actor is defined, but the review criteria are entirely judgment-based; a third party could not objectively verify compliance.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No automatic or institutional consequence attaches to a failure to review. The generic misalignment/adjudication backstops (A.1.3.2.4, A.1.5.9) alone are always weak, and no capital-at-risk, on-chain, or named penalty mechanism reaches this specific duty.

assessments.title: Core Facilitator Records Prime Spell Security Incident Report In Prime Spell Security Incident Registry
assessments.description: Requires Core Facilitators to record all Prime Spell Security Incidents in a specific registry with detailed metadata.
assessments.quote: All Prime Spell Security Incidents must be recorded by the Core Facilitator in the Incident Registry at [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.5.0.6.1 - Prime Spell Security Incidents](7bcaaa37-c914-41a4-b61b-cf3a7eb5438f). Each Registry entry must identify the Prime Agent and its Operational Executor Agent, the incident date(s), a short description of the violation, the penalties imposed, and a link to the corresponding Prime Spell Security Incident Report.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes a concrete, objectively checkable duty on the Core Facilitator to record all Prime Spell Security Incidents in the designated registry, and specifies exactly what metadata each entry must contain. The sole gap is the absence of a deadline or timeframe for recording.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Core Facilitator's registry entries are artifacts subject to scheduled review under the Agent Artifact Review mechanism (d4bf73e7), which includes penalties assessed by Core GovOps, a distinct enforcer. This general oversight plausibly reaches a failure to record incidents, though no specific penalty is quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Use Of Prime Spell Security Registry In Prime Agent Credit Rating System
assessments.description: The Registry determines Prime Agent Credit Line Borrow Rates within the credit rating system.
assessments.quote: The Registry shall serve as a critical input to the Prime Agent Credit Rating system and will determine Primes’ Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate when variable pricing is activated pursuant to [A.3.1.2.5.1 - Relationship To Base Rate](4659cbf0-78c2-469b-8432-883e5c931dd1).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states the Registry will serve as a critical input and determine the borrow rate, but provides no numeric thresholds, formulas, or verifiable metrics. Compliance would be arguable because the mechanism for translating Registry data into a rate is unspecified.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific consequence attaches to non-compliance; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop exists, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Use Of Prime Spell Security Registry In Risk-Based Pricing Of Insurance
assessments.description: Requires insurance fees to be calculated using risk-based pricing informed by the security incident registry.
assessments.quote: Insurance‑related fees charged by a Prime’s Operational Executor shall also be calculated using risk‑based pricing informed by the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry, including the severity, frequency, and recency of incidents.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete parameters (the registry, severity, frequency, recency) and an obligation (risk-based pricing), but the operative magnitudes and exact formula are qualitative; a third party could not verify compliance from the text alone, as the link between incidents and fees is not quantified.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Artifact review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) could plausibly evaluate whether insurance fees comply with the risk-based pricing requirement, and the penalty machinery (b8ee2d12) could be triggered on non-compliance, but no quantified consequence is tied specifically to this rule.

assessments.title: Review Of Prime Spell Security Registry By Prime Agents
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to review the security incident registry and incorporate mitigations into spell development processes.
assessments.quote: Prime Agents are expected to review the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry on an ongoing basis and to independently incorporate mitigations and controls based on relevant prior incidents into their Spell-development related processes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule is entirely qualitative, with no numeric thresholds, metrics, or defined cadence beyond 'ongoing basis'. Compliance is a matter of judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Risk-Based Pricing Of Insurance mechanism (fd1f682c) ties insurance fees to security practices; failure to review the registry and incorporate mitigations would be poor security practice, directly increasing a Prime's insurance costs, a specific financial consequence.

assessments.title: Escalated Penalties For Similar Prime Spell Security Incidents
assessments.description: Applies an escalation multiplier to financial penalties for recurring Prime Spell Security Incidents.
assessments.quote: Where a new Prime Spell Security Incident reflects the same or a substantially similar circumstance as a previous Incident in the Registry, the new Incident shall be subject to an escalation multiplier applied to its financial penalty, as determined by the Core Council. This applies regardless of whether the earlier Incident involved the same Prime.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a condition (similar incident in Registry) and a consequence (escalation multiplier), but the multiplier magnitude is entirely delegated to the Core Council with no numeric threshold or formula, making it a mixed rule.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The escalation multiplier increases the financial penalty for similar incidents, which directly feeds into the risk-based insurance pricing mechanism (fd1f682c), creating a priced incentive for Primes to avoid repeat incidents.

assessments.title: Prime Spell Security Incident Registry
assessments.description: Defines the process and responsible party for updating the Prime Spell Security Incidents registry.
assessments.quote:
Prime Spell Security Incidents are recorded as Active Data in [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.5.0.6.1 - Prime Spell Security Incidents](7bcaaa37-c914-41a4-b61b-cf3a7eb5438f).

The Active Data is updated as follows:

- The Update Process must follow the protocol for ‘Direct Edit’.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a responsible party (Core Facilitator) and a process ('Direct Edit') but provides no metrics, thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable criteria for what constitutes an incident or when updates must occur. Compliance is a matter of following an undefined protocol, making it qualitative only.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or implied. The rule merely assigns a process duty; failure to update the registry would only be reachable through the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Interim Deployments
assessments.description: Allows Prime Agents to deploy new Allocation Instances under constrained testing conditions via the Executive Spell process.
assessments.quote: Prime Agents are allowed to deploy a new Allocation Instance on-chain and allocate capital through it under constrained testing conditions, prior to completing a full risk assessment. Such deployments are termed "Interim Deployments". Interim Deployments are otherwise subject to the customary requirements of the Sky Core Executive Spell and Prime Proxy Spell process.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule permits deployments under 'constrained testing conditions' but provides no metrics, thresholds, or verifiable criteria for what constitutes constrained testing. Compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is mentioned; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Forum Post By Prime Agent
assessments.description: Requires interim deployments to complete all specified external audits before posting a proposal to the Forum.
assessments.quote: The technical implementation of Interim Deployments must successfully complete all required external audits as specified in [A.1.10.2.7 - Audit Process](a8334e19-fedb-48fb-a38c-f18666ccc8e6) before the Prime can post its Interim Deployment proposal to the Forum.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes a concrete obligation (complete all required external audits before posting) but delegates the specifics of what constitutes 'required' and 'successfully complete' to an external document (A.1.10.2.7). No numeric thresholds, formulas, or deadlines are stated in the rule text itself.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this procedural gate. The rule does not specify any consequence for non-compliance, and only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Specification Of Testing Parameters By Core Council Risk Advisor
assessments.description: Requires Risk Advisor to specify testing parameters and mandates 100% Instance Capital Ratio for interim deployments.
assessments.quote: Once posted to the Forum, the Core Council Risk Advisor must respond on the Forum thread specifying testing parameters that will govern the Interim Deployment, including maximum exposure and rate limits. The Prime must maintain 100% Instance Capital Ratio Requirement for all Interim Deployments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes a clear numeric threshold (100% Instance Capital Ratio) but delegates specification of maximum exposure and rate limits to the Core Council Risk Advisor, leaving those parameters unquantified.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Breach of the 100% Instance Capital Ratio Requirement triggers the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and can escalate to Conservatorship (5c3dd35a), providing a defined enforcement path with concrete remedies.

assessments.title: Submission Of Artifact Edit Proposal By Governance Actor
assessments.description: Requires Governance Actors to submit Artifact Edit Proposals incorporating approved testing parameters into Prime Artifacts.
assessments.quote: Subsequently, the appropriate Governance Actor must submit an Artifact Edit Proposal incorporating the approved testing parameters into the Prime’s Artifact.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes a clear obligation on a Governance Actor to submit an Artifact Edit Proposal, but provides no quantified thresholds, deadlines, or metrics; compliance is binary but timing is unspecified, making it arguable when violation occurs.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism in the catalog reaches this procedural step; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Artifact Update
assessments.description: Updates the Prime's Agent Artifact with approved interim testing parameters following a successful poll.
assessments.quote: Upon successful conclusion of the Artifact Edit Poll, the Prime's Agent Artifact is updated with a new Instance Configuration Document codifying the Deployment’s approved interim testing parameters and other basic data.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a procedural obligation (update the artifact with a new Instance Configuration Document) but the content to be codified ('approved interim testing parameters and other basic data') is entirely qualitative and undefined; no metrics, thresholds, or verifiable criteria are provided, making compliance arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or implied; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Creation Of Public Information Dashboard
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to maintain a public dashboard showing current exposure to the Interim Deployment.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent must create a publicly available information dashboard through a platform such as Dune showing, at a minimum, the current exposure to the Interim Deployment. This requirement is waived if the Core Council Risk Advisor has already included the Interim Deployment in the publicly available information dashboard at https://info.skyeco.com.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the Prime Agent, the required dashboard, and the minimum content ('current exposure to the Interim Deployment'), but it does not define how exposure is computed or updated, sets no update cadence or deadline, and 'platform such as Dune' is only an example.
metrics: current exposure to the Interim Deployment
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The public dashboard is plausibly an agent artifact subject to Core GovOps Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7), which provides scheduled review, published findings, and penalty assessment; however, no quantified consequence for missing or non-compliant dashboards is specified for this rule.

assessments.title: Prime Agent Usage Of Interim Deployment
assessments.description: Permits Prime Agent use of interim deployments following requirement satisfaction and approved testing.
assessments.quote: Once the Interim Deployment has been deployed and all requirements above have been satisfied, the Prime Agent may begin using it subject to the approved testing parameters.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule is entirely qualitative, referencing 'approved testing parameters' without defining them, and provides no metrics, thresholds, or verifiable conditions; compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Violation of this security rule could trigger Emergency Spells (b8266c11), a general mechanism that plausibly reaches this rule, though the consequence is unquantified for this specific violation.

assessments.title: Completion Of Full Risk Assessment
assessments.description: Requires a full risk assessment and capital ratio calculation before lifting deployment testing constraints.
assessments.quote: Following the Interim Deployment, the Prime will work with the Core Council Risk Advisor to complete a full risk assessment. Once the means to calculate an official Capital Ratio Requirement for the deployment has been determined, the Prime can request that Core GovOps propose a subsequent Atlas Edit Proposal to lift the testing constraints and reduce the RRC to the Atlas-calculated value.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires a 'full risk assessment' and determination of 'means to calculate an official Capital Ratio Requirement', but provides no metrics, thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable criteria. Compliance is qualitative and arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited; the only consequence is that the Prime cannot request the subsequent proposal without completing the assessment, which is a self-enforcing condition, not a penalty or external enforcement. The catch-all misalignment backstop is weak.

assessments.title: Prime Spell Process Breakdown
assessments.description: Defines the four-week governance and execution procedure for Prime Spells via two distinct governance paths.
assessments.quote:
The documents herein define the Prime Spell Process, the end-to-end procedure through which Prime Agents bring proposed actions through governance and into Sky Core Spells for on-chain execution. The Prime Spell Process spans four (4) weeks, from initial proposal through publication of the Sky Core Spell that includes the Prime Spell payload.

Two governance paths are accommodated. The Sky Governance path applies to Prime Agents whose Root Edit Primitive is not yet operational; in this state, Prime Spell content is ratified through the Sky Core Atlas Edit Proposal process as specified in [A.2.2.6.2.3.2 - Atlas Edit Proposal Process For Prime Agents](364e52eb-4529-46a9-9852-edaaab88baeb). The Independent Governance path applies to Prime Agents whose Root Edit Primitive is operational; in this state, Prime Spell content is ratified through the voting process defined in the Prime Agent's [A.2.2.6.2 - Root Edit Primitive](78488c6b-d77f-4344-b954-476e415a2c7d). Any divergences between the governance paths are specified in the relevant sections.

The Prime Spell Process is organized into four (4) phases, one per week, specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete parameters (four-week timeline, four phases, two governance paths) and a defined actor (Prime Agents), but the operative details of each phase are delegated to subdocuments, making compliance verification dependent on external specifications.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph defines a procedural prerequisite for Prime Agents to have their proposals included in Sky Core Spells; failure to follow the process simply means the proposal is not executed, which is a self-enforcing condition rather than an external penalty. No specific enforcement mechanism is referenced or implied beyond the generic misalignment backstop.

assessments.title: Step 1: Propose And Prioritize (Week 0)
assessments.description: Defines the submission and approval process for Prime Spell content during week 0 of the governance cycle.
assessments.quote: During week 0 of the Prime Spell Process, the Prime Agent's proposed Prime Spell content for the upcoming Executive Vote cycle is submitted, prioritized, and approved, as specified in the subdocuments herein.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a process step (submission, prioritization, approval) and a timeframe (week 0) but delegates all operative criteria to 'subdocuments herein'. No thresholds, metrics, or verifiable conditions appear in the text itself; compliance is not determinable from this paragraph alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or implied for this procedural step. The natural consequence of non-compliance is exclusion from the Executive Vote, which is self-enforcement and weak. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Prime Agent Submits Prime Spell Form
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to submit spell forms with complexity scores and completed audits for new code.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent submits a Prime Spell Form to the Executive Process Liaison by Monday, 16:00 UTC of week 0. The Prime Spell Form initiates the Prime Spell Process for the upcoming Executive Vote cycle and specifies the proposed Prime Spell content. The Prime Agent must include the complexity score calculation for the proposed Prime Spell content in the Prime Spell Form. Items that introduce new code must have a completed audit as specified in [A.1.10.2.7 - Audit Process](a8334e19-fedb-48fb-a38c-f18666ccc8e6) before submission.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a specific actor (Prime Agent), a recipient (Executive Process Liaison), a precise deadline (Monday, 16:00 UTC of week 0), and verifiable content requirements (include complexity score calculation; for new code, a completed audit). A third party could check compliance from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this procedural submission rule. The only consequence of non-compliance is that the Prime Spell may not be included in the Executive Vote cycle, which is self-enforcement and therefore weak. The catch-all misalignment/adjudication backstop alone is also weak.

assessments.title: Delivery And Pre-Risk Review
assessments.description: Defines the timeline and responsibilities for pre-risk review of proposed Prime Spell items.
assessments.quote: During Wednesday of week 0, the Executive Process Liaison delivers proposed Prime Spell items to the Core Council Tracker and the Core Council Risk Advisor conducts a pre-risk review of the items submitted on Monday. Both must be completed by Wednesday, 16:00 UTC of week 0 so that the Strategic Team's scope approval that follows is informed by the Core Council Risk Advisor's findings.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies actors (Executive Process Liaison, Core Council Risk Advisor), actions (deliver items, conduct pre-risk review), and a precise deadline (Wednesday 16:00 UTC week 0). However, the 'pre-risk review' is a qualitative obligation with no defined criteria, metrics, or output requirements, making the review's content unquantified.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is mentioned or implied for missing this procedural deadline or failing to conduct the review. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstops (c6c6f595, 560e1024) could apply, which are weak. No on-chain, capital-at-risk, or named penalty path reaches this rule.

assessments.title: Executive Process Liaison Delivers Items To Core Council Tracker
assessments.description: Defines the Liaison's duties for reviewing Prime Spell forms and delivering verified complexity scores to the Core Council.
assessments.quote: The Executive Process Liaison reviews the submitted Prime Spell Form for completeness and clarity, and discusses possible Prime Spell content and potential blockers with the Prime Agent. The Executive Process Liaison must verify the Prime Agent's complexity score calculation. The Executive Process Liaison must deliver the items, including the verified complexity score, to the Core Council Tracker by Wednesday, 16:00 UTC of week 0.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a clear actor (Executive Process Liaison), a verifiable action (deliver items including verified complexity score), and a precise deadline (Wednesday, 16:00 UTC of week 0). A third party could objectively check compliance.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this process duty; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is weak. No on-chain automatic enforcement, capital at risk, or priced incentive.

assessments.title: Core Council Risk Advisor Conducts Pre-Risk Review
assessments.description: Requires the Risk Advisor to complete a pre-risk review of Prime Spells by a specific weekly deadline.

assessments.title: Validation Checks By StarGuard
assessments.description: The contract enforces single-use spells, bytecode validation, execution requirements, and StarGuard access control.
assessments.quote:
The following checks are enabled by the contract:

- Verifies that the whitelisted Spell is executable only once, enforcing single-use to prevent replay attacks or unauthorized repeats.
- Verifies that the whitelisted bytecode codehash is valid, protecting against tampering or malicious alterations.
- Verifies that the Spell meets custom requirements (e.g., office hours) by confirming the `spell.isExecutable()` view function returns true.
- Verifies that StarGuard retains access to the SubProxy, ensuring no loss of control during the Agent Spell execution.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule lists four specific, boolean checks that a contract performs: single-use enforcement, bytecode codehash validation, spell.isExecutable() return value, and StarGuard access retention. Each is objectively verifiable by inspecting the contract code, with no vague terms or missing parameters.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The contract itself enforces these checks automatically on-chain, but no mechanism UUID from the rubric's catalog or the paragraph text describes this specific on-chain validation. Without a citable mechanism, enforcement is rated weak per rubric rules.
