assessments.title: Report Review And Acceptance
assessments.description: Prohibits deployment or governance votes until audit reports are verified and findings are remediated.
assessments.quote:
Upon delivery of the interim audit report, the team responsible for the audited code reviews the report and confirms that the audited scope and commit hash match the audit request. The audited artifact must not proceed to deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote until the team has accepted the report.

An audit is considered complete when the final audit report is published at the independently verifiable hosting location specified in [A.1.10.2.7.3 - Audit Execution And Report Delivery](31544b57-28e8-4cee-b4ae-f73c2cacabad).

If the interim audit report identifies findings, the artifact must not proceed to deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote until the remediation process specified in [A.1.10.2.7.5 - Findings Remediation](80eab9dd-3833-4418-9845-b648e19fb72f) is completed.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a concrete, binary condition (matching audit scope and commit hash) and a clear gate (no deployment until team acceptance and, if findings exist, remediation). However, it does not define how acceptance is recorded or made externally verifiable, leaving a gap in objective third‐party compliance checking.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Deploying unaudited code in contravention of this rule is a violation of a security rule. The pre-authorized Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11) specifically provides for freezes and pauses when security rules are breached, giving a defined executive intervention path with concrete remedies distinct from the actor.

assessments.title: Findings Remediation
assessments.description: Mandates remediation of audit findings based on severity before code deployment or governance action.
assessments.quote:
If the interim audit report contains findings, the team responsible for the audited code must address each finding based on its severity:

- Findings of low severity or below may be fixed or acknowledged. An acknowledged response must explain why the finding is accepted as-is, including the rationale and any mitigating factors.
- Findings of medium severity or higher must be fixed. The updated code must be re-audited through a new audit request as specified in [A.1.10.2.7.2 - Audit Request And Intake](fcc17c4e-b1cd-4e62-bb2b-0aea02ee72d5), and the re-audit must be completed as specified in [A.1.10.2.7.4 - Report Review And Acceptance](252e0d85-55ca-4fb5-8f44-a38b6ac65e81) before the audited artifact can proceed to deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote. Where the code was submitted by a Prime Agent, the Prime Agent is responsible for the cost of the re-audit.

All findings must be resolved or acknowledged before the audited artifact can proceed to deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote. The resolution status of each finding must be recorded in the final audit report or in a supplementary document referenced from the final audit report.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies discrete actions for each severity category (acknowledge/fix, re-audit) and a gate condition (cannot proceed to deployment/vote). The severity categories are not defined here, but the actions are objectively verifiable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) would check that audit findings are resolved before an artifact can proceed; unresolved findings would block the artifact from deployment or governance vote, creating a concrete procedural consequence.

assessments.title: Audit Recordkeeping
assessments.description: Requires Forum posts and Technical Scopes to include audit reports and verified commit hashes for deployments.
assessments.quote: The Forum post for the associated Spell or deployment must include a link to each applicable final audit report, the audited commit hash, and confirmation that the deployed code matches the audited commit, as specified in [A.1.10.2.3.2.1.2.1.2.1 - Requirements For Forum Post](3d031b7c-1b1f-4f84-8668-1cdf43cb2ab2). Where a Technical Scope is submitted for the deployment, the final audit report and audited commit hash must also be included in the Technical Scope as specified in the same requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule explicitly lists required items: a link to the final audit report, the audited commit hash, and confirmation of match. A third party can verify compliance directly from the text.
metrics: link to each applicable final audit report
confirmation that the deployed code matches the audited commit
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) is a scheduled process that evaluates agent submissions like Forum posts, with published findings and penalty assessment; it plausibly covers missing audit recordkeeping, though no quantified penalty is specified.

assessments.title: Pause Delay
assessments.description: Mandates a minimum time delay between Executive Vote passage and the implementation of protocol changes.
assessments.quote:
The GSM (Governance Security Module) Pause Delay parameter sets the minimum amount of time after an Executive Vote has passed before changes will come into effect in the Sky Protocol.

Once an Executive Vote passes, the GSM Pause Delay must pass before the changes within that Executive Vote can affect the Sky Protocol. The Sky Protocol only has one GSM Pause Delay, and all parameter changes are subject to it. The GSM Pause Delay is usually expressed in terms of hours.

It is possible to move functionality outside of the GSM Pause Delay; however, this requires additional engineering work. A list of exceptional functionality can be found in [A.1.10.3.2 - Exceptions](6781594b-5dff-45ec-89a4-1c9684c4eed8).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the concrete parameter 'GSM Pause Delay' and specifies that it must pass before changes take effect, but the actual duration (numeric threshold expressed in hours) is not stated; it is delegated to an external parameter setting.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No mechanism UUID from the catalog or paragraph text reaches this rule. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which alone is always weak; no on-chain automatic enforcement doc is provided.

assessments.title: Pause Delay Adjustment
assessments.description: Requires an Executive Vote and a pre-change delay period to adjust the GSM Pause Delay parameter.
assessments.quote:
Adjusting the GSM Pause Delay parameter is a manual process that requires an Executive Vote. Changes to the GSM Pause Delay are subject to the pre-change GSM Pause Delay.

An increase to the GSM Pause Delay parameter should be considered if the risk of governance attack is considered especially high for whatever reason. In the past, the GSM Pause Delay has been increased due to the risk from flash loans combined with increased liquidity of the SKY token on the open market.

A decrease should be considered if time-critical governance actions are projected to be needed in the near future. For example, if extreme market volatility is expected, it may be beneficial to reduce the GSM Pause Delay temporarily to allow Governance to better react to changing conditions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The process for adjusting the GSM Pause Delay is precisely defined: an Executive Vote is required, and the change is subject to the pre-change delay. The guidance on when to increase or decrease is qualitative, but the core binding rule (how changes happen) is quantified procedurally.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The on-chain delay enforces the change timing automatically, but no mechanism UUID in the catalog represents this specific timelock, so no citable enforcement mechanism; thus weak.

assessments.title: Executive Drop Exception
assessments.description: Allows successful governance proposals to cancel pending proposals before the GSM Pause Delay expires.
assessments.quote:
The MCD_PAUSE contract manages the general governance timelock of the GSM Pause Delay; however, it also contains an in-built exception to its own rule.

The executive drop functionality allows a successful governance proposal to cancel a previous governance proposal that has not yet passed the GSM Pause Delay period and been executed. As in any other situation, the new Executive proposal must be the hat proposal, meaning more SKY is voting for it than is voting for any other Executive proposal.

This functionality allows Sky Governance to prevent a malicious attack on the protocol if they are able to exceed the attacker’s SKY weight before the GSM Pause Delay expires.

The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is that a malicious attacker may be able to delay or permanently block a legitimate governance proposal.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines the executive drop functionality with a clear condition: the new proposal must be the hat (more SKY voting for it than any other Executive proposal). This condition is objectively verifiable. However, it lacks a quantified threshold, measurement cadence, or deadlines; the rule is descriptive rather than prescriptive, but the condition is precise enough for compliance verification.
metrics: new Executive proposal must be the hat proposal, meaning more SKY is voting for it than is voting for any other Executive proposal
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The executive drop is built into the MCD_PAUSE contract and automatically enforced on-chain, but no catalog enforcement mechanism (such as those listed for liquidation or peg stability) specifically covers this governance exception, and no UUID appears in the paragraph. Without a cited mechanism, the rating defaults to weak.

assessments.title: Oracle Freeze Exception
assessments.description: Defines the OSM_MOM contract's ability to freeze oracle prices via governance and the required GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.quote:
The OSM_MOM contract manages the freezing of Sky’s oracles. The freeze functionality allows a successful governance proposal to immediately freeze the oracle price for any or all of the vault types in the Sky Protocol. Once frozen, the oracle price will remain at its current value.

The oracle cannot be unfrozen without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay as part of a regular governance proposal.

The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is that the oracles may be frozen by an attacker in order to either:

- Prevent an expensive liquidation.
- Take advantage of a significant drop in collateral prices to mint unbacked USDS.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is purely descriptive of the OSM_MOM contract's functionality and associated risks. It does not impose any obligation, threshold, metric, or verifiable condition on any actor; no regulated party has a duty to act or refrain from acting. It is essentially a background explanation, not an operative rule.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No rule exists to enforce. The paragraph describes a contract feature but does not set any compliance obligation. No mechanism applies.

assessments.title: Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception
assessments.description: Allows governance to bypass pause delays to zero out specific vault debt ceilings via the LINE_MOM contract.
assessments.quote:
The LINE_MOM contract manages the breaker for the Debt Ceilings of a configurable subset of the vault types in the Sky Protocol. This Debt Ceiling Breaker allows a successful governance proposal to reduce the debt ceilings of a pre-configured whitelist of vault types to zero without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay to expire.

The Debt Ceiling Breaker affects both the Debt Ceiling and the Maximum Debt Ceiling of a given vault type when activated, disabling the Dynamic Debt Ceiling functionality for that vault type if enabled. To reverse the effect, parameters of affected vault types must be reconfigured with an Executive Vote which is subject to the GSM Pause Delay.

The whitelist may be configured via a successful governance proposal, but must wait for the GSM Pause Delay before changes come into effect. The whitelist is defined in [A.1.10.3.2.3.1 - Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception Whitelist](4937205a-5be0-4def-9b7f-00f9f3bff421) and can be changed via the Weekly Governance Cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes a deterministic mechanism: a successful governance proposal zeroes debt ceilings for whitelisted vaults without the GSM Pause Delay, and whitelist changes are subject to the delay. The steps and actors are concrete, but the operative criteria for whitelist inclusion are delegated to another document and no numeric thresholds appear.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Debt Ceiling Breaker is enforced on-chain: the LINE_MOM contract automatically bypasses the GSM Pause Delay for debt ceiling reductions to zero, and any whitelist changes are subject to the GSM Pause Delay via the governance contract. This pre-authorized executive intervention is analogous to Emergency Spells (b8266c11) in its immediate, code-enforced action.

assessments.title: Liquidations Circuit Breaker Exception
assessments.description: Defines liquidation circuit breaker levels and permissionless activation triggers based on collateral price volatility.
assessments.quote:
The CLIPPER_MOM contract manages the circuit breaker for vault types using Liquidations 2.0. The circuit breaker functionality allows a successful governance proposal to impose Sky Governance’s choice of limitations on liquidations for any or all of the vault types in the Sky Protocol.

- Level 0 - Liquidations Enabled - The breaker is not tripped, new vaults can be liquidated and old liquidations can proceed.
- Level 1 - New Liquidations Disabled - No new liquidations can take place.
- Level 2 - New Liquidations and Resets Disabled - No new liquidations can take place. No existing auctions can be reset if they expire.
- Level 3 - All Liquidations Disabled - No new liquidations, no resets, no bidding in active auctions.

This functionality is exceptional because liquidations at non-market prices have the potential to be irreversibly damaging to both users and the Sky Protocol. The circuit breaker allows Sky Governance to attempt to limit the damage in the event of an issue affecting liquidations without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay.

Additionally, the contract allows for permissionless activation of the circuit breaker, if the price decrease in a collateral exceeds a preset percentage value between oracle price updates. The permissionless activation triggers the circuit breaker at Level 2 because both new auctions and resets reference the current oracle price.

When Level (0, 1, 2, 3) of liquidations circuit breaker is altered via Executive Vote, Sky Governance has the ability to set locked time, which is a specified duration which needs to pass before the liquidations circuit breaker can be triggered again via permissionless activation.

The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is that liquidations may be halted by an attacker in order to either:

- Prevent an expensive liquidation.
- Take advantage of a significant drop in collateral prices to mint unbacked USDS.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule clearly defines four operational breaker levels (0-3) and the exact operations disabled at each, but the triggering condition for permissionless activation ('a preset percentage value') and the governance-set 'locked time' are delegated parameters without numeric thresholds, leaving the operative magnitudes qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph describes a system feature (the CLIPPER_MOM contract) and its operational states; it imposes no obligation on any regulated party. No enforcement mechanism from the catalog is cited, and the descriptive nature means there is nothing to enforce beyond the catch-all misalignment backstop, which is insufficient alone.

assessments.title: Liquidations Circuit Breaker Exception Price Tolerance
assessments.description: Defines the Breaker Price Tolerance parameter and the governance process for its adjustment.
assessments.quote:
Breaker Price Tolerance is a parameter which determines the condition for the permissionless activation of circuit breaker. Adjusting the Breaker Price Tolerance requires an Executive Vote, which is subject to GSM Pause Delay.

The Breaker Price Tolerance is expressed as a number between zero and one, and works with the following equation: `next_oracle_price < current_oracle_price * breaker_price_tolerance`.

In instances where the price oracle model does not support the price delay function, the permissionless activation of the liquidation circuit breaker ceases to function, since there is no next oracle price.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule provides a precise activation formula (next_oracle_price < current_oracle_price * breaker_price_tolerance) and a governance process for adjustment. However, the actual numeric value of the Breaker Price Tolerance is not specified; it is defined only as a number between zero and one, leaving a minor gap for independent verification.
metrics: Breaker Price Tolerance is expressed as a number between zero and one
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism from the catalog reaches this rule. The liquidation circuit breaker's permissionless activation is an automatic on-chain effect, but it enforces the trigger logic, not the rule's parameter definition. The requirement that adjustments go through an Executive Vote with GSM Pause Delay is an on-chain governance constraint, but no catalogued mechanism explicitly penalizes non-compliance with this adjustment rule.

assessments.title: Direct Deposit Breaker Exception
assessments.description: Governance can disable Direct Deposit Modules by setting the debt ceiling parameter to zero via the DIRECT_MOM contract.
assessments.quote:
The DIRECT_MOM contract manages the breaker for Direct Deposit Modules (D3Ms). The breaker functionality allows a successful governance proposal to disable any or all of the active D3Ms. In practice, this will set the bar parameter to zero, which (contrary to intuition) disables the module by setting the allowed Debt Ceiling to zero. At this point, no further USDS can be minted through the Direct Deposit Module. To reverse the effect, parameters of affected Direct Deposit Modules must be reconfigured with an Executive Vote which is subject to GSM Pause Delay.

The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is that a given line of USDS credit is unexpectedly shut down. This has the potential to disrupt the protocol in question, which may impact Sky indirectly.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph describes a governance tool (DIRECT_MOM) and its effect on D3Ms, but imposes no obligation, metric, threshold, or verifiable condition on any regulated party. It is purely descriptive and aspirational regarding risk.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No rule with a violation mode; there is no consequence for non-compliance because there is no prohibition. The described functionality is contract-level, but that does not constitute enforcement of a behavioral rule.

assessments.title: SparkLend Freezer Mom Exception
assessments.description: Allows Sky Governance to bypass pause delays to freeze or pause SparkLend markets during emergencies.
assessments.quote:
The SparkLend FREEZER_MOM contract allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay to either freeze or pause any markets in SparkLend. The contract also allows the undoing of such actions for any market in SparkLend.

This functionality allows Sky Governance to react faster in an emergency. Freezing markets does not allow for new supplies or borrows, while pause restricts all market functionality, including deposits/withdrawals/borrows/repays and liquidations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the FREEZER_MOM contract, the actor (Sky Governance), the bypassed GSM Pause Delay, and the exact actions (freeze, pause, undo), but the triggering circumstances are qualitative ('react faster in an emergency') with no definition of emergency or threshold.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is mentioned; the rule is a permission, not a prohibition with penalties. The contract itself provides the functionality but does not enforce appropriate use. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception
assessments.description: Allows disabling the Smart Burn Engine and USDS staking rewards without the standard GSM pause delay.
assessments.quote:
The SPLITTER_MOM contract allows for the disabling of the Smart Burn Engine without the GSM Pause Delay.

This functionality is available so that Sky Governance can react to emergencies regarding the Smart Burn Engine.

Since the Splitter contract also allocates USDS from the Surplus Buffer to USDS Staking Rewards, the activation of SPLITTER_MOM also disables these rewards until the activation is reversed by Sky Governance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a concrete action (SPLITTER_MOM disabling Smart Burn Engine and USDS staking rewards without the usual GSM Pause Delay) and a defined actor (Sky Governance), but the condition for use is qualitative ('react to emergencies') with no threshold or criteria.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches misuse of this exception; only the general misalignment and adjudication catch-alls would apply, which are weak.

assessments.title: Bounded External Access Modules
assessments.description: BEAMs allow whitelisted operators to bypass GSM delays within predefined risk parameter limits.
assessments.quote:
Bounded External Access Modules (BEAMs) are contracts that allow whitelisted operators to manage parameters in the Sky Ecosystem without needing to use the standard Executive Vote process. Thus, parameter changes enacted via these modules are not subject to the GSM Pause Delay.

The actions of BEAMs are limited by risk parameters, which are set by Sky Core Governance and require an Executive Vote to change.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the concept of risk parameters that limit BEAM actions and states they are set by Sky Core Governance via Executive Vote, but it provides no specific numeric thresholds, formulas, or values. A third party would know what is regulated (actions must stay within parameters) but cannot verify compliance from the text alone because the actual limits are delegated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism document from the catalog corresponds to the on-chain bounding of a BEAM contract's parameters, and no UUID appears in the paragraph. The only conceivable enforcement is the contract's own logic, which is not a cited mechanism. Therefore, enforcement is rated weak.

assessments.title: Bounded External Access Module Risk Disclosure
assessments.description: Requires BEAMs to have MOM contracts for deactivation and limits modification frequency and size.
assessments.quote:
BEAMs allow whitelisted operators greater flexibility to respond to market movements when setting parameters in the Sky Ecosystem. This flexibility introduces additional risk since operators are able to bypass the Executive Vote process when changing the parameters relevant to the BEAM that they operate.

This risk can be mitigated by limiting the frequency and size of modifications that can be made by operators in parameters controlled by Sky Core. All BEAMs should also have a related MOM contract that can deactivate the relevant BEAM in the event of an operator acting in a misaligned manner.

Any operator that fails to follow the defined procedures for a BEAM they are operating should be considered misaligned.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule is entirely qualitative: it urges 'limiting the frequency and size of modifications' without any numeric thresholds, refers to 'defined procedures' that are not specified, and uses 'should' for the MOM contract, making compliance arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The only consequence stated is that an operator failing to follow undefined procedures 'should be considered misaligned,' triggering the generic misalignment reporting and adjudication backstops. No specific penalty, automated mechanism, or capital-at-risk incentive applies directly to this rule.

assessments.title: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Exception
assessments.description: Whitelisted operators may modify vault and savings rates within specified parameters without waiting for governance delays.
assessments.quote:
The Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module (SP-BEAM) MCD_SPBEAM contract manages the rates applied to Sky Protocol’s native vaults as well as the savings rates. Whitelisted operators can use the SP-BEAM to modify rates without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The SP-BEAM modifies rates up or down within specified parameters. See [A.3.7.1.3 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module](47b8b035-8abd-42e6-86b8-33f852fa953a).

This functionality allows the Sky Protocol to react to changes in market rates more quickly than waiting for an Executive Vote and the GSM Pause Delay.

The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by whitelisted operators setting rates to undesirable values. This risk can be mitigated through the SP-BEAM parameters and the SPBEAM_MOM.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states that the SP-BEAM contract modifies rates within specified parameters, but those parameters are not enumerated in this text. A regulated party cannot determine compliance solely from this paragraph; the obligation exists but lacks quantified bounds.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The SP-BEAM contract enforces rate change limits on-chain; the whitelisted operator cannot set rates beyond the parameters defined in the referenced document (47b8b035-8abd-42e6-86b8-33f852fa953a). Violation is impossible at the contract level, providing automatic enforcement.

assessments.title: stUSDS Bounded External Access Module Exception
assessments.description: Whitelisted operators may modify stUSDS parameters within specified ranges without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.quote:
The stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (stUSDS BEAM) manages the parameters of the stUSDS system. Whitelisted operators can use the stUSDS BEAM to modify certain stUSDS parameters without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The stUSDS BEAM modifies stUSDS parameters within specified ranges. See [A.4.4.1.3.8 - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module](37f8f82e-7239-4cfb-8f95-d2cc40515cd9).

This functionality allows the Sky Protocol to update stUSDS parameters more quickly than waiting for an Executive Vote and the GSM Pause Delay.

The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by whitelisted operators setting stUSDS parameters to undesirable values. This risk can be mitigated through the stUSDS BEAM parameters and the STUSDS_MOM.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states that whitelisted operators may modify certain stUSDS parameters within specified ranges without delay, but does not enumerate the parameters, the concrete ranges, or the operator identities. The operative details are delegated to a linked document, making it a mixed rule: the regulated action is clear but the bounds are not quantified here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The stUSDS BEAM is an on-chain contract that enforces the specified parameter ranges automatically; any attempt to set a value outside the bounds would be rejected by the contract code. This is on-chain self-executing enforcement, cited via the BEAM's UUID from the paragraph.

assessments.title: Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module Exception
assessments.description: Allows whitelisted operators to modify specific Smart Burn Engine parameters within defined bounds without GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.quote:
The Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module (SBE-BEAM) manages certain parameters of the Smart Burn Engine. See [A.3.5.2 - Smart Burn Engine Parameters](ddb90fee-2851-4bf0-b924-f1d73e30ce7a). Whitelisted operators can use the SBE-BEAM to modify the `kbump`, `burn`, and `hop` parameters without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The SBE-BEAM modifies these parameters, up or down, within specified bounds. See [A.3.5.2.4 - Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module](b57ac61b-f6b1-4025-bd44-569d0f2afe2f).

This functionality allows the Sky Protocol to update Smart Burn Engine parameters more quickly than waiting for an Executive Vote and the GSM Pause Delay.

The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by whitelisted operators setting Smart Burn Engine parameters to undesirable values. This risk can be mitigated through the SBE-BEAM parameters and the SPLITTER_MOM, as specified in [A.1.10.3.2.8 - Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception](5247c795-7f9d-4d3f-a040-6bc9b070e2d4).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the specific parameters (kbump, burn, hop) and the actors (whitelisted operators), and states that modifications must be within specified bounds. However, the actual bounds are not provided in this paragraph; they are delegated to a referenced document (A.3.5.2.4). Thus, the operative magnitudes are absent, making it a mixed case.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The SBE-BEAM contract itself enforces the parameter bounds on-chain, preventing any modification outside the specified bounds. This is automatic, contract-level enforcement, making violation impossible. The referenced document (b57ac61b) describes the bounded module.

assessments.title: Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception
assessments.description: Allows Sky Governance to bypass pause delays and disable the stability parameter module during emergencies.
assessments.quote:
The SPBEAM_MOM contract allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay and disable the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module.

This functionality allows Sky Governance to react more quickly in an emergency, e.g., if an operator of the SP-BEAM is hacked or is a malicious actor. Once the SPBEAM_MOM is activated, the SP-BEAM will not be able to change any rates in the system. If the SPBEAM_MOM has been triggered, it will still be possible to modify rates through the usual Executive Vote process, subject to the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph describes a contract capability ('allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay and disable the SP-BEAM') but imposes no obligations, metrics, thresholds, or verifiable conditions on any actor. It is a permissive description, not a rule to be complied with.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No rule is violated by any party, so no enforcement mechanism is triggered. Only catch-all misalignment reporting (c6c6f595) could theoretically apply, but that is weak and the text does not create a duty to misalign.

assessments.title: stUSDS Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception
assessments.description: Allows Sky Governance to bypass pause delays to disable the stUSDS Bounded External Access Module during emergencies.
assessments.quote:
The STUSDS_MOM contract allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay and disable the stUSDS Bounded External Access Module or set the `cap` or `line` stUSDS parameters to zero.

This functionality allows Sky Governance to react more quickly in an emergency, e.g., if an operator of the stUSDS BEAM is hacked or is a malicious actor. Once the STUSDS_MOM is activated to disable the stUSDS BEAM, the stUSDS BEAM will not be able to change any stUSDS parameters in the system. If the STUSDS_MOM has been triggered, it will still be possible to modify stUSDS parameters through the usual Executive Vote process, subject to the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule gives Sky Governance a qualitative permission ('in an emergency'), with only illustrative examples ('operator hacked or malicious actor') and no quantitative thresholds, metrics, or verifiable conditions that would allow a third party to determine objectively when the exception applies.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph describes an on‑chain bypass capability, not an obligation with a defined penalty for misuse. No catalogued enforcement mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, or otherwise) reaches a violation of this permission; only the generic misalignment backstop could apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Linear Interpolation Module Features
assessments.description: Defines the operational mechanism for permissionless linear interpolation of governance parameters via the tick function.
assessments.quote: The `lerp` must be activated in an Executive Vote but can thereafter change the value of the designated parameter without additional Executive Votes. Each `lerp` instance is defined in terms of a `start` value, representing the desired starting value, an `end` value, representing the desired ending value, and a `duration` over which the parameter will be adjusted between the starting value and the ending value. Any user can then permissionlessly call `tick` to set the governance parameter to the appropriate value based on the time elapsed.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule enumerates a concrete process: activation must be via an Executive Vote, then parameters (start, end, duration) are defined, and any user can call tick to interpolate. The requirement is binary (an Executive Vote occurred or not) but lacks numeric thresholds, formulas, or a measurement cadence.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is implicitly enforced on-chain by the lerp contract's code, making violation impossible. However, no mechanism UUID from the catalog or the text covers this on-chain governance enforcement, so under the strict citation requirement, the rating falls to weak.

assessments.title: Linear Interpolation Module Authorization

assessments.title: Governance Process For Linear Interpolation Module
assessments.description: Requires parameter adjustments via the Linear Interpolation Module to follow the original parameter's governance process.
assessments.quote: The process to utilize the Linear Interpolation Module to adjust a parameter must follow the same governance process required to modify the designated parameter. If the parameter can be updated directly through an Executive Vote, then utilizing the Linear Interpolation Module to adjust it may also be included directly in an Executive Vote. If modifying the parameter requires a prior Governance Poll, then utilizing the Linear Interpolation Module for that parameter must also be preceded by a Governance Poll.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies that the process for using the Linear Interpolation Module must match the original parameter's governance process, with enumerated conditional steps (Executive Vote if direct, Governance Poll if required), but no quantification, thresholds, or deadlines; compliance is verifiable only by referencing another process definition.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Enforcement likely relies on artifact review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7), which can detect non-compliance with governance process for LPM usage during scheduled reviews; no automatic on-chain enforcement is indicated, and no quantified penalty for this rule exists.

assessments.title: Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig
assessments.description: Allows the SkyLink Freezer Multisig to bypass standard governance votes to freeze SkyLink bridges.

The Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig (see [A.4.2.2.1 - Ethereum SkyLink Freezer Multisig](21fa6749-6209-4280-9b5f-b2a73d400421)) can freeze SkyLink bridges deployed in the Sky Ecosystem without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process.

The Solana SkyLink Freezer Multisig (see [A.4.2.2.2.3.1.1 - Solana SkyLink Freezer Multisig](8e618196-257a-49d8-834d-665dba345fcd)) can freeze the Solana SkyLink Bridge without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process.

assessments.title: Standby Spells
assessments.description: Defines Standby Spells as emergency mechanisms to bypass pause delays for critical protocol actions.
assessments.quote:
A subset of Emergency Spells is Standby Spells.

Standby Spells allow Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay and directly perform crucial actions such as stopping an oracle, setting a debt ceiling to zero, disabling a D3M integration, or stopping liquidations for a collateral. Standby Spells or the factory contracts used to deploy them are reusable, meaning they can be executed several times if needed, or voted on again on a later date to be executed again.

The subdocuments herein specify the authorized use of Standby Spells.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph lists enumerated actions (stop oracle, set debt ceiling to zero, etc.) but provides no quantitative thresholds, formulas, deadlines, or verifiable criteria. Compliance hinges on judgment of 'crucial actions', and exact authorized uses are deferred to subdocuments, making it arguable whether a given use violates the rule.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule defines a capability for governance, not an obligation with consequences. No on-chain automatic enforcement, no named enforcer, and no defined penalty for misuse beyond the generic misalignment catch-all, which alone is weak.

assessments.title: Standby Spells Definition
assessments.description: Defines Standby Spells as mechanisms to trigger MOM circuit-breakers while bypassing the GSM Pause Delay.
assessments.quote:
Sky Protocol uses circuit-breakers to mitigate undesired scenarios, which circuit-breakers are called MOM contracts. MOM contracts must first be triggered through a Spell, after which they bypass the GSM Pause Delay and can immediately act on the Protocol. See [A.1.10.3.2 - Exceptions](6781594b-5dff-45ec-89a4-1c9684c4eed8).

In emergency scenarios, time is a scarce resource. Therefore, Standby Spells are used in validated emergency scenarios to trigger a MOM contract. In an emergency situation, Spell teams can then focus on crafting an ad hoc Emergency Spell to solve the root cause of an issue, if appropriate. Due to Standby Spells, it is no longer necessary in an emergency for Spell teams to spend time crafting and reviewing a Spell whose sole purpose is to trigger a mitigation of the issue, i.e., the MOM contract.

Standby Spells open new attack vectors that must be mitigated pursuant to [A.1.10.5.2.3.3 - ADs' Role In Standby Spells](53cea69b-45cc-4f9c-b863-9bf259e37deb).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines Standby Spells and states they are used in 'validated emergency scenarios', but provides no quantitative thresholds, metrics, or criteria for validation; the obligation is entirely qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement consequence is attached to the rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop (catch-all) would apply, which is always weak.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states the spell can be used if 'collaterals fail' with examples like 'stablecoin depegs' or 'protocol hacked', but no measurable thresholds (e.g., depeg magnitude, duration) or objective triggers are provided. Compliance with the described conditions is a matter of judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is a descriptive specification of a standby spell's function, not a binding obligation on any party. No mechanism enforces the rule; the catch-all misalignment path alone would be the only backstop, which is weak.

assessments.title: GroupedClipBreakerSpell

assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph describes a spell's function, not a rule that can be violated. No enforcement mechanism reaches it; the catch-all misalignment process would be the only backstop, which is weak.

assessments.title: MultiLineWipeSpell

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a concrete on-chain action: setting all collateral debt ceilings to zero. 'Zero' is a numeric threshold, and 'all collaterals' makes the scope fully defined and objectively verifiable.
metrics: debt ceilings set to zero for all collaterals
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule describes a Standby Spell, which is an emergency spell that executes on-chain. Once triggered, it automatically enforces the zero debt ceiling, preventing new debt creation. This is self-executing on-chain enforcement via the Emergency Spells mechanism.

While it defines a process (disabling SP-BEAM, freezing rates), it contains no quantitative thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or verifiable conditions that a regulated party must satisfy.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is purely permissive; it does not impose an obligation that can be violated, and therefore no specific enforcement mechanism is directed at it. Only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: The Core Facilitator Role In Standby Spells
assessments.description: Defines the Core Facilitator's responsibilities and communication protocols for initiating and executing Standby Spells during emergencies.
assessments.quote:
The role of the Core Facilitator in the Standby Spell process is as follows:

- Standby Spells can only be used in response to a properly validated and categorized emergency scenario, for which the Core Facilitator is responsible. See [A.1.9.1.5.1 - Incident Validation](97020aa2-9492-4fa4-8eee-d860d6f33618) and [A.1.9.1.5.2 - Incident Categorization](f3a647b2-8083-41f1-b67a-66bd322ccc16).

The decision to initiate the process to use a Standby Spell is reserved for the Core Facilitator; where possible, the Core Facilitator should consult with any relevant Scope Advisor(s). See [A.1.9.1.4 - Emergency Response Roles And Responsibilities](c9c32f24-cf6c-43d5-ac4c-bd2b4d02032b).

- The Core Facilitator must explicitly communicate the decision to use a Standby Spell in the secure, private communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf) or on a "war room" video call.

- After the decision to use a Standby Spell is first reached on a video call, the Core Facilitator is required thereafter to promptly document their decision in the secure, private communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).

- After the Core Facilitator decides to use a Standby Spell, TechOps Services must promptly trigger an incident to the Emergency Response Group as specified in [A.1.9.1.5.3 - Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger](34a3d273-ce49-4147-adf3-6d52b4a2fad5).

- The Core Facilitator is responsible for actioning the Standby Spell and liaising with the Ranked Delegates (and other Aligned Delegates as needed) to gather the necessary support for it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule lists enumerated steps (communication, documentation, trigger) and references specific channels by document UUID, but the core obligation to act only in 'properly validated and categorized' emergencies delegates criteria to other documents, and terms like 'where possible' and 'promptly' leave room for judgment without numeric thresholds.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None of the named enforcement mechanisms reach this procedural duty; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Core GovOps Role In Standby Spells
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps to promptly acknowledge Standby Spell decisions via a specific communication channel.
assessments.quote: Core GovOps must promptly acknowledge receipt of the Core Facilitator's decision to use a Standby Spell. This acknowledgment must take place in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a concrete action (acknowledge receipt of a Standby Spell decision) and the exact communication channel (via reference to A.1.9.1.3.1). However, the timing requirement 'promptly' is qualitative, leaving no objective threshold for compliance verification.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism is specified for failure to acknowledge. The catch-all adjudication or misalignment processes would apply only generally, and no on-chain, capital-at-risk, or named escalation path directly reaches this acknowledgment duty.

assessments.title: Requirement To Validate Authenticity Of Standby Spell
assessments.description: Requires two Core GovOps representatives to validate Standby Spell authenticity via secure written communication before AD voting.
assessments.quote:
Two Authorized Representatives, as defined in the subdocument below, from Core GovOps must validate the authenticity of the Standby Spell.

This validation must be in the form of a written communication in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf). Only the entities specified in [A.1.10.5.2.3.2.1.1 - Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Standby Spell](4cf98145-079f-44e0-9a2b-1d7b16037f4a) are authorized to provide the validation of authenticity.

Pursuant to [A.1.10.5.2.3.3 - ADs' Role In Standby Spells](53cea69b-45cc-4f9c-b863-9bf259e37deb), ADs are prohibited from voting for a Standby Spell without this validation of authenticity.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies concrete parameters: the number of representatives (two), the form (written communication), and the channel (secure group). However, the core obligation 'validate the authenticity' is qualitative with no defined criteria, making compliance partly a judgment call. Mixed precision.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: If an AD votes for a Standby Spell without this validation, the action likely constitutes a security rule violation. The Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11) enables pre-authorized executive intervention (freezes, pauses) for security violations, plausibly reaching this rule. No quantified penalty is specified for this specific act.

assessments.title: Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Standby Spell
assessments.description: Designates specific individuals and entities authorized to validate the authenticity of Standby Spells.
assessments.quote:
This document defines the term "Authorized Representative" as used in [A.1.10.5.2.3.2.1 - Requirement To Validate Authenticity Of Standby Spell](82393e1d-1021-4f48-ac4e-a98d2328f2e7).

The entities listed below are authorized to validate the authenticity of a Standby Spell on behalf of Core GovOps:

- Retro on behalf of Core GovOps team Soter Labs
- Adam Fraser on behalf of Core GovOps team Soter Labs
- Lex on behalf of Core GovOps team Soter Labs

The Authorized Representatives listed are synonymous with the Sky Forum account holders with the following handles:

- retro
- adamfraser
- Lex
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule provides an exhaustive, verifiable list of specific individuals and their associated Sky Forum handles authorized to perform the validation action. A third party can definitively check compliance against this list.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule defines actors for the Standby Spell process under Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5). An invalid validation could render a spell unauthorized, triggering the Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11-3a84-4bbe-abe2-de9474f74ffd) which allows for pre-authorized executive intervention to pause or freeze actions, providing a specific path for consequence.

assessments.title: Custom Spell Voting For Standby Spells
assessments.description: Restricts the Core Facilitator to using custom spell voting only upon documented recommendation from the Emergency Response Group.
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator may use the Custom Spell Voting Page when it is beneficial to coordinate voting without using the standard Spell process. The Core Facilitator must not use this method unless domain expert Ecosystem Actors in the Emergency Response Group have recommended this approach; such a recommendation must be explicitly documented in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a clear prohibition: the Core Facilitator must not use the Custom Spell Voting Page unless the Emergency Response Group has recommended it and the recommendation is documented in a specified channel. The condition is verifiable (documentation exists or not), but the rule lacks a defined cadence for repeated uses or a formal definition of what constitutes a valid recommendation from the group, leaving a minor gap.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is provided. Violation would rely on the general misalignment reporting (A.1.3.2.4) and adjudication (A.1.5.9) processes, which are catch-all and therefore weak.

assessments.title: ADs' Role In Standby Spells
assessments.description: Prohibits ADs from voting on Standby Spells without specific notification and authenticity validation requirements.
assessments.quote:
ADs are strictly prohibited from voting to use a Standby Spell unless they have first confirmed all of the following requirements:

- Receipt of the Core Facilitator's official notification of the emergency scenario in the Emergency Contact Mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.5.3 - Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger](34a3d273-ce49-4147-adf3-6d52b4a2fad5).
- Receipt of the Core Facilitator's announcement of the decision to use a Standby Spell in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf); and
- Core GovOps has validated the authenticity of the Standby Spell. This validation must fulfill two requirements: (1) the validation must be in the form of a written communication in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf); and (2) the validation must be provided by the Authorized Representatives listed in [A.1.10.5.2.3.2.1.1 - Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Standby Spell](4cf98145-079f-44e0-9a2b-1d7b16037f4a).

After ADs have confirmed all requirements are met, they must either (1) promptly vote to approve the Standby Spell, or (2) communicate any concerns to the Core Facilitator and collaborate with the latter for a speedy resolution.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule enumerates specific verifiable steps (receipt of notifications via named channels, validation from listed Authorized Representatives) that must be confirmed before voting. The conditions are objectively checkable, but the deadline 'promptly' and subsequent 'collaborate for a speedy resolution' are qualitative, leaving minor gaps.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No explicit penalty or enforcement path is stated for an AD violating the voting restriction. The only recourse would be a report of misalignment under the generic backstop (c6c6f595), which is weak enforcement.

assessments.title: AD Reliance On Core GovOps In Standby Spell Process Where Core GovOps Is Nonresponsive
assessments.description: Allows a Core Facilitator to grant sole validation authority to an Operational Facilitator during emergency nonresponsiveness.
assessments.quote: There is an exception to the requirement that two Authorized Representatives from Core GovOps must validate the authenticity of a Standby Spell. In situations where the Authorized Representatives have failed to respond to the emergency situation, the Core Facilitator may temporarily grant an Operational Facilitator the sole authority to validate the authenticity of the Emergency Spell pursuant to [A.1.10.5.2.3.3 - ADs' Role In Standby Spells](53cea69b-45cc-4f9c-b863-9bf259e37deb). The Core Facilitator must communicate this in writing in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule's trigger ('failed to respond') is entirely qualitative with no time threshold or objective criteria for nonresponse, making compliance arguable. The communication requirement is concrete but the core obligation lacks metrics.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication catch-alls would apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Misalignment To Vote For Unvalidated Standby Spell
assessments.description: Mandates immediate derecognition and buffer confiscation for delegates voting for unvalidated standby spells.
assessments.quote: It is severe misalignment for an Aligned Delegate to vote for a Standby Spell whose authenticity has not been validated pursuant to [A.1.10.5.2.3.3 - ADs' Role In Standby Spells](53cea69b-45cc-4f9c-b863-9bf259e37deb). Aligned Delegates in breach of this requirement must be immediately derecognized and their full AD Buffer should be confiscated.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a specific, verifiable action (voting for an unvalidated standby spell) and an immediate concrete consequence (derecognition and buffer confiscation). A third party can check compliance by verifying the spell's validation status and the delegate's vote.
metrics: Vote for a Standby Spell whose authenticity has not been validated pursuant to A.1.10.5.2.3.3
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule states a direct penalty (derecognition, buffer confiscation) but provides no distinct enforcement mechanism UUID or documented process to execute it; only the generic catch‑all misalignment/adjudication backstops are available, which alone are weak.

assessments.title: Accountability
assessments.description: Mandates accountability procedures for any breach of Emergency Spell requirements.
assessments.quote: Breach of any requirement concerning Emergency Spells - including Standby Spells - constitutes misalignment and must be addressed pursuant to [A.1.9.1.6 - Accountability For Emergency Response Preparedness](8df982ee-754c-4cd9-a5f9-ce1c30e06cf8).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule declares that breach of unspecified Emergency Spell requirements constitutes misalignment and must be addressed per a referenced procedure. No metrics, thresholds, or actor-defined obligations are present; the rule's operative effect depends entirely on content outside this paragraph, making compliance arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule explicitly invokes the accountability procedure defined in A.1.9.1.6 (UUID 8df982ee...), which likely includes a defined escalation path and consequences for emergency preparedness breaches, though not on-chain automatic; thus mid.

assessments.title: Emergency Drop Spells
assessments.description: Allows authorized governance to cancel pending actions via the Protego contract during emergency periods.
assessments.quote: The Protego contract can be used to deploy an Emergency Drop Spell. Once authorized by Sky Governance, the Emergency Drop Spell can cancel any planned governance action that is awaiting GSM Pause Delay expiration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a clear, binary condition: the Emergency Drop Spell can cancel pending actions only after authorization by Sky Governance. A third party could verify compliance by checking governance votes, though the exact authorization process is not detailed here.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Protego contract enforces the authorization requirement on‑chain, making unauthorized execution impossible. This on‑chain self‑enforcement falls under the Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11).

assessments.title: Deployment Of Emergency Drop Spells
assessments.description: Allows users to permissionlessly deploy emergency spells to cancel planned governance actions via the Protego contract.
assessments.quote:
Any user can permissionlessly deploy an Emergency Drop Spell by invoking the `deploy` function on the Protego contract with parameters identifying the planned governance action to be canceled:

`deploy(address _usr, bytes32 _tag, bytes memory _fax, uint256 _eta)(address)`

The parameters of the `deploy` function are defined in [A.1.10.5.3.1.3 - Protego Parameters](55195cdc-90c3-4133-a0e4-792444b60ed8).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule gives an exact function signature ('deploy(address _usr, bytes32 _tag, bytes memory _fax, uint256 _eta)') with permissionless invocation; a third party could verify the contract call without ambiguity.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The deployment is an on-chain smart-contract function, automatically enforced by the Protego contract; the emergency-spells framework (b8266c11) ensures the cancellation capability is natively enforced without human intervention.

assessments.title: Execution Of Emergency Drop Spells
assessments.description: Defines the mechanism and authority requirements for invoking the Emergency Drop Spell function to cancel governance actions.
assessments.quote: Once an Emergency Drop Spell has been deployed, it can be used to cancel the execution of the planned governance action by invoking its `drop` function. This function can only be invoked if the Emergency Drop Spell has been granted authority by Sky Governance by giving the Emergency Drop Spell the `hat` in the Chief contract.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a clear on-chain condition for invocation (holding the hat in the Chief contract) which is objectively verifiable. However, it does not define the actor who can call the drop function, leaving a minor gap.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The hat requirement is enforced automatically by the Chief contract: calling drop without the hat reverts. This falls under the pre-authorized executive intervention of the Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11), providing on-chain self-enforcement.

assessments.title: Allowing Permissionless Cancellation Of Planned Governance Actions
assessments.description: Allows any user to permissionlessly cancel planned governance actions via the Protego contract.
assessments.quote: The Protego contract can be granted authority by Sky Governance to allow any user to permissionlessly cancel any planned governance action. This is done by giving the Protego contract the `hat` in the Chief contract. Once the Protego contract has been granted authority, any user can cancel either a single planned governance action or a set of planned governance actions as specified herein.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph describes a feature (granting the Protego contract the hat to allow user cancellations) but contains no numeric thresholds, deadlines, measurable metrics, or defined obligations. The phrase 'as specified herein' is not further detailed in the given text, leaving the operative criteria qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The ability for any user to cancel planned governance actions is enforced on-chain by the Protego contract once it holds the hat; the code makes violation impossible while the authority is active, constituting a self-executing mechanism under the Emergency Spells framework (A.1.10.5).

assessments.title: Permissionless Cancellation Of Single Planned Governance Action
assessments.description: Allows any user to permissionlessly cancel a planned governance spell via the Protego contract drop function.
assessments.quote:
If the Protego contract has authority from Sky Governance, any user can permissionlessly invoke the `drop` function to cancel a specified Spell:

```
/// @notice Permissionlessly drop anything that has been planned on the pause.
drop(address _usr, bytes32 _tag, bytes memory _fax, uint256 _eta)
```

The parameters of the `drop` function are defined in [A.1.10.5.3.1.3 - Protego Parameters](55195cdc-90c3-4133-a0e4-792444b60ed8).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states an on-chain capability: any user can call the `drop` function to cancel a spell if the Protego contract has authority. This is fully quantified by the function signature and the verifiable on-chain state; compliance is objectively checkable from the contract code.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule imposes a functional requirement (the drop function must be permissionlessly callable). Violation would be a code defect, detectable in scheduled Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7), which could trigger Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12). No on-chain automatic enforcement exists for the absence of the function itself.

assessments.title: Permissionless Cancellation Of Multiple Planned Governance Actions
assessments.description: Allows any user to permissionlessly cancel specified sets of planned governance Spells via the Protego contract.
assessments.quote:
If the Protego contract has authority from Sky Governance, any user can permissionlessly invoke the `drop` function to cancel a specified set of Spells:

```
/// @notice Drop multiple plans in a single call.
drop(Plan[] calldata plans)
```

The parameter of the `drop` function is defined in [A.1.10.5.3.1.3 - Protego Parameters](55195cdc-90c3-4133-a0e4-792444b60ed8).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a precise, verifiable capability: any user may invoke the `drop` function, specified with its exact function signature, and the only condition is that the Protego contract holds authority from Sky Governance. This is objectively checkable against contract code; no measurement cadence or discretionary thresholds are needed.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The cancellation action is executed directly by the Protego smart contract on-chain, with no human intervention required—any user can permissionlessly call `drop` and the contract enforces the outcome. This self-execution is part of the Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11), making violation impossible and ensuring the rule is automatically enforced.

assessments.title: Determining Protego Parameters
assessments.description: Mandates using Pause contract logs rather than Spell functions to determine parameters for canceling scheduled Spells.
assessments.quote: The parameters for the scheduled Spell to be canceled, as specified in [A.1.10.5.3.1.3 - Protego Parameters](55195cdc-90c3-4133-a0e4-792444b60ed8), should always be determined by inspecting the logs emitted from the `plot` function of the Pause contract. The parameters should never be determined by calling functions on the Spell to be canceled, because these functions may not return the correct values in the case of a malicious Spell.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule mandates a specific, verifiable technical method: parameters must be determined by inspecting Pause contract `plot` logs and must never be derived from Spell function calls. A third party can check compliance by inspecting the implementation, so the obligation is objectively verifiable without quantitative thresholds.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) includes scheduled reviews with findings and penalty assessments for non-compliant artifacts, plausibly reaching violations of this implementation rule. No automatic on-chain enforcement or quantified penalty specific to this rule is present.

assessments.title: The Core Facilitator Role In Protego Usage
assessments.description: Defines the Core Facilitator's responsibilities and communication protocols for initiating Protego emergency spells.
assessments.quote:
The role of the Core Facilitator in the usage of Protego is as follows:

- Protego can only be used in response to a properly validated and categorized emergency scenario, for which the Core Facilitator is responsible. See [A.1.9.1.5.1 - Incident Validation](97020aa2-9492-4fa4-8eee-d860d6f33618) and [A.1.9.1.5.2 - Incident Categorization](f3a647b2-8083-41f1-b67a-66bd322ccc16).
- The decision to initiate the process to use Protego is reserved for the Core Facilitator; where possible, the Core Facilitator should consult with any relevant Scope Advisor(s). See [A.1.9.1.4 - Emergency Response Roles And Responsibilities](c9c32f24-cf6c-43d5-ac4c-bd2b4d02032b).
- The Core Facilitator must explicitly communicate the decision to use Protego in the secure, private communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf) or on a "war room" video call.
- If the decision to use Protego is first reached on a video call, the Core Facilitator is required thereafter to promptly document their decision in the secure, private communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
- After the Core Facilitator decides to use Protego, TechOps Services must promptly trigger an incident to the Emergency Response Group as specified in [A.1.9.1.5.3 - Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger](34a3d273-ce49-4147-adf3-6d52b4a2fad5).
- The Core Facilitator is responsible for actioning the usage of Protego and liaising with the Ranked Delegates (and other Aligned Delegates as needed) to gather the necessary support for it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule lists specific communication channels and a decision reserved for a named actor, but the operative condition ('properly validated and categorized emergency scenario') is delegated to referenced documents, and no quantitative thresholds, deadlines, or metrics are stated. Compliance is verifiable only as process steps, not by measurable magnitude or timing.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific consequence attaches to violation of these facilitator responsibilities. Only the general misalignment/adjudication catch-all could be invoked, which alone is weak. No on-chain automatic enforcement, capital at risk, or named penalty mechanism reaches this process rule.

assessments.title: Core GovOps Role In Protego Usage
assessments.description: Requires Core GovOps to acknowledge Protego emergency usage decisions via a specified communication channel.
assessments.quote: Core GovOps must promptly acknowledge receipt of the Core Facilitator's decision to use Protego. This acknowledgment must take place in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The duty to 'promptly acknowledge receipt' contains a qualitative adverb ('promptly') with no specified time frame, making compliance arguable and unverifiable. The communication channel is referenced but no metric or deadline is provided.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism is specified for a delayed or missing acknowledgment; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Requirement To Validate Authenticity Of Emergency Drop Spell
assessments.description: Requires two Core GovOps representatives to validate Emergency Drop Spells via secure written communication before voting.
assessments.quote:
Two Authorized Representatives, as defined in the subdocument below, from Core GovOps must validate the authenticity of the Emergency Drop Spell, if applicable.

This validation must be in the form of a written communication in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf). Only the entities specified in [A.1.10.5.3.2.2.1.1 - Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Emergency Drop Spell](a15e7cd9-ea93-48ac-b53a-afc476ca2d05) are authorized to provide the validation of authenticity.

Pursuant to [A.1.10.5.3.2.3 - ADs' Role In Protego Usage](0cec9b17-ef83-4d25-9b6e-dbba11587d52), ADs are prohibited from voting for an Emergency Drop Spell without this validation of authenticity.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: Rule specifies two Authorized Representatives, written communication in a secure channel, and prohibits AD voting without validation. However, 'if applicable' and the qualitative nature of authenticity validation leave some ambiguity.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism applies; only the generic misalignment backstop. No catalog mechanism cited in text or implicitly reaches this rule.

assessments.title: Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Emergency Drop Spell
assessments.description: Lists specific entities and handles authorized to validate the authenticity of Emergency Drop Spells.
assessments.quote:
This document defines the term "Authorized Representative" as used in [A.1.10.5.3.2.2.1 - Requirement To Validate Authenticity Of Emergency Drop Spell](44b9503d-bc11-427e-8deb-47feed07eba2).

The entities listed below are authorized to validate the authenticity of an Emergency Drop Spell on behalf of Core GovOps:

- Retro on behalf of Core GovOps team Soter Labs
- Adam Fraser on behalf of Core GovOps team Soter Labs
- Lex on behalf of Core GovOps team Soter Labs

The Authorized Representatives listed are synonymous with the Sky Forum account holders with the following handles:

- retro
- adamfraser
- Lex
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names exact authorized entities and exact Sky Forum handles — Retro, Adam Fraser, and Lex on behalf of Soter Labs, with handles retro, adamfraser, and Lex. A third party can verify from the text alone whether a given validator is authorized.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph only defines and lists authorized validators; it states no consequence, penalty, invalidation, or automatic check for unauthorized validation. No cited enforcement mechanism from the catalog reaches this authorization list, leaving only the generic backstop.

assessments.title: Custom Spell Voting For Protego Usage
assessments.description: Restricts Custom Spell Voting to cases recommended and documented by the Emergency Response Group.
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator may use the Custom Spell Voting Page when it is beneficial to coordinate voting without using the standard Spell process. The Core Facilitator must not use this method unless domain expert Ecosystem Actors in the Emergency Response Group have recommended this approach; such a recommendation must be explicitly documented in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a clear, verifiable condition: the Core Facilitator must not use Custom Spell Voting unless the ERG has recommended it and documented the recommendation in the specified channel. 'Beneficial' is a subjective qualifier, but the operative restriction is concrete. No numeric thresholds, but compliance can be objectively checked.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) plausibly reaches procedural compliance rules like this one; a review could flag undocumented usage, leading to penalty assessment. The consequence is unquantified for this specific rule, making enforcement mid.

assessments.title: ADs' Role In Protego Usage
assessments.description: Prohibits ADs from voting on emergency spells without specific notification and validation requirements.
assessments.quote:
ADs are strictly prohibited from voting to use an Emergency Drop Spell, or to give authority to the Protego contract, unless they have first confirmed all of the following requirements:

- Receipt of the Core Facilitator's official notification of the emergency scenario in the Emergency Contact Mechanism specified in [A.1.9.1.5.3 - Emergency-Contact Mechanism Trigger](34a3d273-ce49-4147-adf3-6d52b4a2fad5);
- Receipt of the Core Facilitator's announcement of the decision to use Protego or an Emergency Drop Spell in the communication channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf); and
- Core GovOps has validated the authenticity of the Emergency Drop Spell, if applicable. This validation must fulfill two requirements: (1) the validation must be in the form of a written communication in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf); and (2) the validation must be provided by the Authorized Representatives listed in [A.1.10.5.3.2.2.1.1 - Current Entities Authorized To Validate Authenticity of Emergency Drop Spell](a15e7cd9-ea93-48ac-b53a-afc476ca2d05).

After ADs have confirmed all requirements are met, they must either (1) promptly vote to approve the usage of Protego or the Emergency Drop Spell, or (2) communicate any concerns to the Core Facilitator and collaborate with the latter for a speedy resolution.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule lists specific, verifiable events (notification via defined mechanism, announcement in signal group, validation communication from authorized entities) that must precede AD voting. However, the requirement that ADs 'confirmed' receipt of the notification introduces a subjective element; while the events themselves can be externally checked, the AD's internal confirmation is not fully objective, leaving a minor gap.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No explicit enforcement mechanism is attached to this rule. Only the generic misalignment reporting (c6c6f595) and adjudication (560e1024) backstops apply, which are always weak.

assessments.title: AD Reliance On Core GovOps In Emergency Drop Spell Process Where Core GovOps Is Nonresponsive
assessments.description: Allows a Core Facilitator to grant sole emergency spell validation authority if Authorized Representatives are nonresponsive.
assessments.quote: There is an exception to the requirement that two Authorized Representatives from Core GovOps must validate the authenticity of an Emergency Drop Spell. In situations where the Authorized Representatives have failed to respond to the emergency situation, the Core Facilitator may temporarily grant an Operational Facilitator the sole authority to validate the authenticity of the Emergency Drop Spell pursuant to [A.1.10.5.3.2.3 - ADs' Role In Protego Usage](0cec9b17-ef83-4d25-9b6e-dbba11587d52). The Core Facilitator must communicate this in writing in the secure channel specified in [A.1.9.1.3.1 - Emergency Response Signal Group](45a7ccff-09fa-4d95-b3d8-e3f34f7917cf).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule is entirely qualitative: 'failed to respond' lacks any time window or threshold, and the grant of sole authority is permissive ('may'). Compliance depends on subjective judgment, not verifiable metrics.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism targets this procedural exception rule. Only the generic misalignment backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Misalignment To Vote For Unvalidated Emergency Drop Spell
assessments.description: Mandates immediate derecognition and buffer confiscation for delegates voting for unvalidated emergency spells.
assessments.quote: It is severe misalignment for an Aligned Delegate to vote for an Emergency Drop Spell whose authenticity has not been validated pursuant to [A.1.10.5.3.2.3 - ADs' Role In Protego Usage](0cec9b17-ef83-4d25-9b6e-dbba11587d52). Aligned Delegates in breach of this requirement must be immediately derecognized and their full AD Buffer should be confiscated.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a binary, objectively verifiable condition (voting for an unvalidated spell) and attaches immediate, concrete consequences (derecognition and full AD Buffer confiscation). A third party can check compliance solely from the paragraph and the referenced validation definition.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Emergency Spells (b8266c11) execute freezes/pauses but do not carry out the delegate derecognition or buffer confiscation this rule contemplates, and the text says the buffer 'should' be confiscated — no automatic path or named enforcer. A general mechanism reaching the rule without a defined path is mid.

assessments.title: Protego Usage Accountability
assessments.description: Mandates accountability procedures for any breach of emergency spell or Protego usage requirements.
assessments.quote: Breach of any requirement concerning Emergency Spells - including usage of Protego - constitutes misalignment and must be addressed pursuant to [A.1.9.1.6 - Accountability For Emergency Response Preparedness](8df982ee-754c-4cd9-a5f9-ce1c30e06cf8).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a real obligation (misalignment must be addressed via a specific section) but no thresholds, metrics, or deadlines are provided; the triggering requirements are entirely undefined in this paragraph, making compliance arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The reference to A.1.9.1.6 is not a known mechanism in the rubric catalog and no details indicate a specific consequence beyond misalignment; only the generic misalignment backstop (A.1.3.2.4, A.1.5.9) would apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Emergency Process For Misaligned Agent Artifacts
assessments.description: Sky Core may immediately suspend Agent Artifact functions during emergencies to mitigate significant system-level risks.
assessments.quote: In an emergency situation (see [A.1.9.1.1 - Definition Of Emergency Situations](5eafb29e-84a0-4a53-a798-3f958c880225)), Sky Core has the discretion to immediately suspend an Agent Artifact provision or function if it reasonably suspects that the Artifact is contributing towards a significant or system-level risk. Sky Core must act in good faith when exercising its discretion in emergency situations.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule relies entirely on qualitative judgment language ('reasonably suspects', 'significant or system-level risk') with no numeric thresholds, metrics, or deadlines. Compliance is arguable either way on the same facts because the operative criteria are subjective.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Sky Core's discretion to suspend an Agent Artifact during an emergency is enforceable through pre-authorized Emergency Spells (A.1.10.5), which allow immediate freezes or pauses. This provides a specific consequence executed by a named enforcer distinct from the agent, with a defined escalation pathway outside standard governance.

assessments.title: Sky Executive Vote Override
assessments.description: Sky Core may override Agent decisions to protect ecosystem safety or solvency.
assessments.quote: A Sky Executive Vote will override any Agent Artifact or decision by an Executor Agent if there is a determination by Sky Core that the Prime Agent or Executor Agent is acting misaligned, or if the Sky ecosystem's safety or solvency is at risk.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule relies entirely on subjective determinations ('acting misaligned', 'safety or solvency is at risk') with no quantitative thresholds, metrics, or verifiable criteria. Compliance is a matter of judgment, making the condition arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism applies to the rule itself; the override action is the rule's operative procedure, not a consequence for breaching it. The catch-all misalignment/adjudication would be circular. No mechanism from the catalog reaches this rule.

assessments.title: Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response
