assessments.description: Requires all Agent Artifacts to include a document specifying emergency response protocols for ecosystem-wide impacts.
assessments.quote: All Agent Artifacts must contain a `Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response` document as a direct child of the `Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive` document. This document and its subdocuments must specify the Agent’s emergency response protocol applicable in situations that impact the entire Sky Ecosystem.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies an exact document name ('Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response') and placement (direct child of 'Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive'), which is verifiable, but the requirement to 'specify the Agent’s emergency response protocol' is entirely qualitative with no metrics, thresholds, or content criteria.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Agent Artifact Review process (d4bf73e7) includes scheduled review of Agent Artifacts, with findings and penalty assessments; missing a required Omni document could be flagged as non-compliance and lead to penalties.

assessments.title: Agent Emergency Response
assessments.description: Requires all Agent Artifacts to include a specific emergency response protocol document.
assessments.quote: All Agent Artifacts must contain an `Agent-Specific Emergency Response` document as a direct child of the `Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive` document. This document and its subdocuments must specify the Agent’s emergency response protocol applicable in situations solely impacting the Agent, versus the broader Sky Ecosystem.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes a concrete, verifiable structural obligation (a named document, 'Agent-Specific Emergency Response', must exist as a direct child of a specified parent document). The content obligation to 'specify the Agent’s emergency response protocol' is qualitative, making overall compliance only partially objective.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is enforced through the Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7), which can detect a missing or deficient document and assess penalties. The consequence is unquantified for this specific documentation requirement, but the review mechanism provides a plausible path to enforcement.

assessments.title: Executor Agent Facilitators
assessments.description: Mandates that Facilitators hold privileged smart contract access and perform artifact interpretations for Executor Agents.
assessments.quote: Executor Agent Facilitators are Facilitators that carry out specific activities on behalf of Executor Agents. Whenever an Executor Agent must interpret an Artifact, that interpretation must be done by the Facilitator. Whenever an Executor Agent has privileged access to smart contracts of Sky or an Agent, that access must be held by the Facilitator. Facilitators use this access to carry out the Executor Agent’s operational responsibilities as directed by GovOps, unless the Facilitator believes that GovOps is misaligned.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule mandates that Facilitators perform artifact interpretations and hold privileged smart contract access, with operational responsibilities carried out unless misalignment is suspected. No numeric thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or verifiable criteria are provided; compliance is purely based on qualitative actions, making it arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) could plausibly examine whether Executor Agents' artifact interpretations are performed by Facilitators and whether operational responsibilities are carried out as directed, providing a general oversight mechanism with penalty assessment, though no specific penalty is quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Demand Side Buffer
assessments.description: The Demand Side Buffer is controlled by a multisig and topped up via Executive Vote.
assessments.quote: The Demand Side Buffer is the account used for disbursement of Distribution Reward and Integration Boost payments. The Demand Side Buffer is controlled by a multisig as specified in the documents herein. The balance of this account may be topped up through an Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is purely descriptive, stating the account's purpose, its multisig control, and topping-up mechanism, without imposing any obligation, threshold, or verifiable condition on any regulated party.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No operative rule exists to trigger any enforcement; only the generic misalignment backstop (always weak) could apply, with no defined consequence for this paragraph.

assessments.title: Demand Side Buffer Multisig Required Number Of Signers
assessments.description: The Demand Side Buffer Multisig requires a minimum of two out of three signers.
assessments.quote: The Demand Side Buffer Multisig has a 2/3 signing requirement.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states an exact numeric threshold (2 out of 3 signers) for a named multisig; a third party can check compliance from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism doc cited in the paragraph or catalog directly reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment backstop is available, which is weak.

assessments.title: Demand Side Buffer Multisig Signers
assessments.description: Defines the three specific addresses controlled by Soter Labs that serve as Demand Side Buffer Multisig signers.
assessments.quote: The signers of the Demand Side Buffer Multisig are three (3) addresses controlled by Operational GovOps Soter Labs.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a numeric requirement (three signers) and a qualitative condition (controlled by Operational GovOps Soter Labs), but does not list the actual addresses, making compliance verifiable only by judgment — the text is qualitative overall.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule. The on-chain multisig enforces signer addresses but not the controller's identity; only the generic misalignment catch-all (c6c6f595) could apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Demand Side Buffer Multisig Usage Standards
assessments.description: Requires Demand Side Buffer Multisig signers to disburse specific payments according to the Atlas.
assessments.quote: The signers of the Demand Side Buffer Multisig must use the Multisig to disburse Distribution Reward and Integration Boost payments in accordance with the Atlas.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes a real obligation on named actors (signers) but uses qualitative language ('in accordance with the Atlas') with no numeric thresholds, formulas, or deadlines. Compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific consequence attaches to violation. Only the generic misalignment catch-all could apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Demand Side Buffer Multisig Modification
assessments.description: Specifies the minimum signer count and threshold required for Demand Side Buffer Multisig modifications.
assessments.quote: Operational GovOps Soter Labs can change the signers of the Demand Side Buffer Multisig at any time, so long as there are at least three (3) signers and at least two-thirds of signers are required to execute transactions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states exact numeric thresholds (at least 3 signers, at least two-thirds threshold) and names the permitted actor; a third party can verify compliance by inspecting the multisig configuration.
metrics: at least two-thirds of signers are required to execute transactions
assessments.enforcementReasoning: A violation would be detectable via Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) by Core GovOps, which can lead to penalties under the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12). The consequence is unquantified for this rule, and there is no on-chain automatic enforcement, making the enforcement path mid-level.

assessments.title: Demand Side Buffer Auxiliary Accounts
assessments.description: Requires auxiliary accounts to use a three-signer multisig with a two-thirds quorum controlled by Soter Labs.
assessments.quote:
Operational GovOps Soter Labs may establish auxiliary accounts on other blockchains to facilitate efficient distribution of Distribution Reward and Integration Boost payments to Integrators operating on those blockchains. Operational GovOps Soter Labs may move funds from the Demand Side Buffer Multisig to auxiliary accounts as necessary to facilitate such payments. Each auxiliary account must conform to the same standards as the Demand Side Buffer Multisig, specifically:

- a minimum of three (3) signers;
- at least two-thirds of signers are required to execute transactions; and
- all signers are controlled by Operational GovOps Soter Labs.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states explicit, verifiable quantitative standards: minimum 3 signers and a two‑thirds quorum requirement, with all signers controlled by a named actor. A third party could inspect the multisig configuration and verify compliance from the text alone.
metrics: at least two-thirds of signers are required to execute transactions
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No direct penalty is specified for this operational security rule. However, Soter Labs' auxiliary accounts fall within the scope of scheduled artifact review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7), which can detect non‑conformance and lead to published findings and penalty assessment—a plausible but unquantified path, making enforcement mid.

assessments.title: Agent Token Emissions
assessments.description: Defines irreversible emission disabling and governance override capabilities for Agent Token emissions.
assessments.quote: The Agent Token Primitive must specify whether token emissions beyond the current supply have been irreversibly disabled. Once Disabled is set to `True`, the action cannot be undone by the Agent. Sky Governance retains the ability to revert the Disabled setting where the Agent is in violation of Risk Capital requirements and emissions are required by the Risk Framework.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a clear boolean condition ('Disabled' set to True), assigns obligations to specific actors (Agent, Sky Governance), and gives a precise, binary override condition (violation of Risk Capital requirements). The only gap is that the violation threshold is external, but the rule is still objectively verifiable given reference documentation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Non‑compliance (e.g., allowing the Agent to reverse the Disabled flag) would be identified during scheduled artifact review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7), which leads to formal penalty assessment under the penalty mechanisms (b8ee2d12). This provides a specific, institutional enforcement path with a distinct enforcer and defined consequences.

assessments.title: Token SkyLink Setup Target Chain Identification And Feasibility Analysis
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to evaluate bridging security and audit costs before deploying to new target chains.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent researches potential target blockchains for token bridging, including evaluation of user base, DeFi ecosystem, and bridging security requirements. The Prime Agent confirms that the target chain supports LayerZero or can be integrated easily with the LayerZero Omnichain Fungible Token standard. The Prime Agent also estimates potential use of the token on the target chain to justify the bridge deployment and audit costs. The output of this step is a preliminary decision to proceed with deploying a bridge to the target chain including a scope of work for the bridge deployment and estimated audit costs.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes a process with purely qualitative obligations (researching, evaluating, confirming, estimating) and no numeric thresholds, metrics, or verifiable criteria. Compliance would be arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism specific to this rule is present; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstops would apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Token SkyLink Setup Initial Alignment With Operational GovOps
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to present bridging plans and technical summaries to Operational GovOps for review and feedback.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent presents the bridging plan to Operational GovOps, including a technical summary, proposed timeline, and estimate of audit costs. The Prime Agent and Operational GovOps also discuss any guidelines in the Atlas or the Agent Artifact that may affect bridging. The Prime Agent receives early feedback on the plan and modifies it accordingly. The output of this step is an informal agreement to proceed with developing a bridge deployment along with any documented conditions or feedback from Operational GovOps.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule enumerates three concrete deliverables (technical summary, proposed timeline, estimate of audit costs) the Prime Agent must present, making the obligation identifiable, but it provides no quantitative thresholds or criteria for those items—compliance is verifiable only that the documents exist, not that they meet any measurable standard.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific consequence or mechanism enforces this procedural step. Failure would only stall the informal agreement; no capital at risk, on‑chain enforcement, or named penalty path reaches this rule. Only the generic misalignment backstop applies, which is weak.

assessments.title: Token SkyLink Setup Audit Preparation And Proposal Of Costs
assessments.description: Requires the Prime Agent to secure a third-party audit for the bridge implementation and document costs.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent contacts a reputable third-party security audit firm for reviewing the bridge implementation. The Prime Agent negotiates audit scope, timeline, and fees with the audit firm. The Prime Agent documents the projected cost for the bridge, including development, audit, and deployment costs, for future reimbursement. The outcome of this step is a formal agreement with the audit firm and a detailed cost breakdown for bridge deployment and auditing.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires contacting a 'reputable' audit firm, negotiating scope/timeline/fees, and documenting costs, but provides no quantitative metrics, thresholds, deadlines, or objectively verifiable criteria beyond the existence of an agreement and cost breakdown. Compliance is arguable based on qualitative judgments.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) can review the required audit agreement and cost breakdown as artifacts, with staged findings and penalty assessment possible for non-compliance; however, consequences are unquantified for this specific rule.

assessments.title: Token SkyLink Setup Bridge Deployment And Initial Audit
assessments.description: Defines the deployment process and audit verification requirements for the Token SkyLink bridge contract.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent, through Operational GovOps, deploys the Token SkyLink contract on the target chain. The Prime Agent shares the Token SkyLink contract’s final address with the audit firm for verification. Operational GovOps confirms that the bridge contract address and references match the updated Prime Agent Artifact. The audit firm completes and updates the bridging audit registry with the results of the audit. The output of this step is a deployed bridge contract with audit results uploaded to the bridging audit registry.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes a sequence of actions by named actors (Prime Agent, Operational GovOps, audit firm) but contains no numeric thresholds, deadlines, or objectively verifiable metrics. The confirmation step ('confirms that the bridge contract address and references match') uses a qualitative matching criterion with no specified method or cadence, making compliance arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) covers the verification of the Prime Agent Artifact, and a failure to ensure the bridge address matches could be detected during that periodic review. However, no quantified penalty or specific escalation for missing this deployment step is stated, so enforcement is mid.

assessments.title: Token SkyLink Setup Activation On New Chain
assessments.description: Requires an Executive Vote on audit results to activate bridging and updates reward tracking modules.
assessments.quote: Core GovOps formalizes the audit results with a Sky Core Executive Vote to fully activate bridging functionality. Operational GovOps updates the Prime Agent Reimbursement Module to begin counting any bridged tokens toward the incremental reward. The output of this step is fully enabled bridging on the target chain with the Prime Agent Reimbursement Module updated to track bridging based rewards.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete actors (Core GovOps, Operational GovOps) and specific actions (Executive Vote, updating the Prime Agent Reimbursement Module), making compliance verifiable. However, it lacks any quantitative thresholds, deadlines, or measurable criteria; the operative step ('formalizes the audit results') is qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is mentioned. Failure to execute the step would leave bridging inactive, but there is no penalty or automatic consequence for the responsible actors beyond the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop, which alone is weak.

assessments.title: List of Active Token SkyLink Deployments
assessments.description: Requires Token SkyLink deployments to list bridge contract addresses and associated audit documentation.
assessments.quote: The Token SkyLink Primitive must list each active Token SkyLink deployment. The listing must include the following information: (1), the token being bridged, (2) the target chain of the bridge, (3) the address of the bridge contract on the Ethereum Mainnet, (4) the address of the bridge contract on the target chain, (5) the audit of the bridge contract, (6) the bridge parameters, (7) the total bridge deployment and audit costs, and (8) the amount of bridge deployment and audit costs that have been reimbursed to date.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule mandates an exhaustive listing with eight named information items, allowing third-party verification. However, it lacks a required update frequency or criteria for completeness, creating a minor gap.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No dedicated enforcement mechanism is referenced; only the generic misalignment and adjudication processes (e.g., Reports of Misalignment, Adjudication Process) could potentially apply, which alone are considered weak.

assessments.title: Base Tracking Methodology
assessments.description: Specifies the Reward Code parameter and deposit calculation methodology for the Base PSM contract.
assessments.quote: The Tracking Methodology for Base is to specify the Reward Code as a parameter in calls to the Base PSM contract. Conversions from USDS or USDC to sUSDS are considered "deposits" and net deposits are calculated using an approach similar to that on Ethereum Mainnet.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states an actionable instruction (specify Reward Code as parameter) and defines deposits, but the net deposit calculation is described as 'similar to that on Ethereum Mainnet' without quantifying the approach, no thresholds or metrics. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism reaches this methodology rule; only the generic misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Sky Direct Exposures
assessments.description: Defines the rules governing exposures held directly by Sky through Prime Agent allocation systems.
assessments.quote: Sky Direct Exposures are exposures that are held directly by Sky but implemented through the Allocation System of a Prime Agent. The documents herein define the rules for Sky Direct Exposures.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph merely defines Sky Direct Exposures and states that rules are defined elsewhere; it contains no operative obligation, thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or verifiable conditions.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforceable obligation is stated; the paragraph imposes nothing that could be violated, so no enforcement mechanism applies.

assessments.title: Designation Process
assessments.description: Defines the process for designating Sky Direct Exposures and assigning responsible Prime Agents.
assessments.quote: Sky Direct Exposures are designated by the Core Facilitator in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor via posts to the Sky Forum under the "Sky Core" category. Sky Direct Exposures are recorded in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.1.2.0.6.1 - List Of Current Sky Direct Exposures](5f368e33-7a82-4244-a9ba-f285193ec043) and must specify the asset that is being designated as a Sky Direct Exposure and the Prime Agent responsible for implementing the exposure.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names specific actors (Core Facilitator, Core Council Risk Advisor), a defined communication channel (Sky Forum, 'Sky Core' category), and required content (asset, responsible Prime Agent). A third party could verify compliance by checking the posted record, though the 'consultation' step is qualitative and no deadline is given.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism is mentioned or implicit for this designation process; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak by rubric standard and no explicit mechanism UUID is cited.

assessments.title: Current Sky Direct Exposures
assessments.description: Defines the responsible party and update process for maintaining the list of current Sky Direct Exposures.
assessments.quote:
The list of current Sky Direct Exposures is defined as Active Data in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.1.2.0.6.1 - List Of Current Sky Direct Exposures](5f368e33-7a82-4244-a9ba-f285193ec043).

The Active Data is updated as follows:

- The Responsible Party is the Core Facilitator.
- The Update Process must follow the protocol for ‘Direct Edit’.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a responsible party (Core Facilitator) and a process reference ('Direct Edit') for updating a data list, but contains no quantitative thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or verifiable compliance criteria. It is purely a qualitative obligation expressed in procedural language; compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is identified or reaches this rule. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop (A.1.3.2.4, A.1.5.9) might apply, which alone is always weak. No on-chain enforcement, capital at risk, or named artifact review covers this administrative update duty.

assessments.title: Parameters For Sky Direct Exposures
assessments.description: The Core Facilitator sets and publishes rate and aggregate exposure limits for Sky Direct Exposures.
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator sets the following parameters for Sky Direct Exposures in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor:

- Rate limits; and
- Aggregate exposure limits.

The Core Facilitator must post the initial values for these parameters and any updates to them to the Sky Forum under the "Sky Core" category. The values for the parameters for Sky Direct Exposures are set by the Core Facilitator and supersede any values for these parameters specified in the Risk Framework.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete parameters (rate limits, aggregate exposure limits) and a posting obligation, but the actual magnitudes are entirely delegated to the Core Facilitator without quantitative criteria, thresholds, or deadlines. Compliance with the posting can be checked, but the substance of the limits is not verifiable from the rule text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is referenced or implicitly reaches this delegation duty. Failure to set or post parameters would only trigger the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop, which is weak.

assessments.title: Previous Sky Direct Exposures
assessments.description: Defines the update process and responsible party for maintaining the list of previous Sky Direct Exposures.
assessments.quote:
The list of previous Sky Direct Exposures is defined as Active Data in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.1.3.0.6.1 - List Of Previous Sky Direct Exposures](86fce840-f7f3-4617-bb58-d04db8731c9d).

The Active Data is updated as follows:

- The Responsible Party is the Core Facilitator.
- The Update Process must follow the protocol for ‘Direct Edit’.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a responsible party (Core Facilitator) and a process ('Direct Edit'), but provides no metrics, thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable criteria for what constitutes a correct update or when it must occur. Compliance is entirely qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or implied for this update process. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstops could apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Treatment Of Exposures In Excess Of Aggregate Exposure Limit
assessments.description: Exposures exceeding aggregate limits are reclassified and subject to monthly settlement and Risk Capital requirements.
assessments.quote: Any investments in assets that would otherwise qualify as Sky Direct Exposures by a Prime Agent in excess of the aggregate exposure limit are not Sky Direct Exposures and are subject to the customary requirements pursuant to [A.2.4 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle](6f8d5065-d6ff-4add-9a28-eadeffa7ed1a) and [A.3.2 - Risk Capital](55999acf-75fe-4adf-8584-9746ef50d3e4).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a condition (excess of aggregate exposure limit) and a classification consequence (not Sky Direct Exposures) with a requirement to follow two referenced processes, but it does not specify the numeric limit or the exact requirements; those are delegated to other documents. The phrase 'customary requirements' is qualitative, but the references provide a clear path for compliance checking.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule subjects excess exposures to the Risk Capital requirements (A.3.2). Failure to meet those requirements would trigger the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Conservatorship (5c3dd35a), providing a defined escalation path with concrete remedies. No automatic on-chain enforcement for the classification itself, but the indirect link to Risk Capital enforcement is sufficient for a mid rating.

assessments.title: Revenue Sharing For Sky Direct Exposures
assessments.description: Exempts Prime Agents from borrowing rates and yield retention for Sky Direct Exposures via settlement adjustments.
assessments.quote: Because Sky Direct Exposures are held by Sky rather than the Prime Agent implementing the exposure through its Allocation System, Prime Agents are not required to pay the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate with respect to funds borrowed to finance Sky Direct Exposures. All yield on Sky Direct Exposures is also due exclusively to Sky and is not retained by the Prime Agent. This is implemented as an adjustment to the Monthly Settlement Cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names the actor (Prime Agents), specifies the exemption from the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate on funds borrowed for Sky Direct Exposures, and states yield goes exclusively to Sky, with implementation via the Monthly Settlement Cycle. The term 'Sky Direct Exposures' is defined elsewhere but not in the paragraph, creating a minor gap in stand‑alone verifiability. No numeric thresholds or deadlines are present.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Artifact review (d4bf73e7) can detect a Prime Agent failing to implement the settlement adjustment or improperly retaining yield, and the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach such a violation, though the specific financial penalty is unquantified for this rule.

assessments.title: No Risk Capital Requirements With Respect To Sky Direct Exposures
assessments.description: Exempts Prime Agents from holding Risk Capital for Sky Direct Exposures.
assessments.quote: Because Sky Direct Exposures are held by Sky rather than the Prime Agent implementing the exposure through its Allocation System, Prime Agents are not required to hold any Risk Capital with respect to Sky Direct Exposures.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states an absolute exemption: 'Prime Agents are not required to hold any Risk Capital with respect to Sky Direct Exposures.' This is a binary, objectively verifiable directive once the term 'Sky Direct Exposures' is defined. No numeric thresholds are needed because it is a complete removal of obligation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This rule grants an exemption rather than imposing a duty. There is no violation possible, and therefore no penalty, conservatorship, emergency spell, or other consequence attaches to compliance or non-compliance. On-chain allocation system design might implement this implicitly, but no mechanism UUID is available to cite. Only the generic misalignment backstop exists, which is weak.

assessments.title: No Actively Stabilizing Collateral Requirements With Respect To Sky Direct Exposures
assessments.description: Exempts Prime Agents from holding Actively Stabilizing Collateral for Sky Direct Exposures and excludes them from requirement calculations.
assessments.quote: Because Sky Direct Exposures are held by Sky rather than the Prime Agent implementing the exposure through its Allocation System, Prime Agents are not required to hold any Actively Stabilizing Collateral with respect to Sky Direct Exposures. Sky Direct Exposures also do not count towards satisfying a Prime Agent’s Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule sets a clear, verifiable condition: Prime Agents must hold 0% ASC for Sky Direct Exposures, and such exposures are excluded from ASC requirement calculations. The exemption is fully quantified (zero requirement) and directly checkable from portfolio data and exposure classification.
metrics: 0% ASC requirement for Sky Direct Exposures
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This rule defines how the ASC requirement is computed; misapplication would cause a violation of the overall ASC requirement. The enforcement machinery for ASC requirements — Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) — implicitly reaches this definitional rule, as a Prime's failure to correctly exclude Sky Direct Exposures could lead to under-collateralization and trigger those mechanisms.

assessments.title: Rate Limits
assessments.description: Defines the mathematical formula and governance-controlled parameters for rate-limiting token allocation operations.
assessments.quote:
Rate limits set the maximum allowable amount of tokens that can be processed for specific operations within a given time period. Each rate limit contains the rate limit data: `maxAmount`, `slope`, `lastAmount` and `lastUpdated`. The current rate limit is calculated using the formula:

`currentRateLimit = min(slope * (block.timestamp - lastUpdated) + lastAmount, maxAmount)`.

The rate limit data `maxAmount` and `slope` are configurable parameters that are set and modified by Governance. The rate limit data `lastAmount` and `lastUpdated` are internal state data dynamically tracked by the Rate Limiter to perform its calculations.

Rate limits set caps on the rate of allocation to a given Instance, they do not act as a limit on the total amount that may be allocated to that Instance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule gives a concrete formula for currentRateLimit and names the configurable parameters, but the actual numeric values (maxAmount, slope) are delegated to Governance, so the operative magnitude is not stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism from the catalog or the paragraph text reaches this specific allocation rate limit rule. The mechanism is implicitly the on-chain Allocation System, but no UUID is available to cite.

assessments.title: MaxAmount
assessments.description: Defines a hard cap and rate limit mechanism for USDS allocations to specific Instances.
assessments.quote: `maxAmount` sets a hard cap on the level of allocation to an Instance at any given time. It sets the absolute rate limit regardless of how much time has passed since the last allocation. For example, if `maxAmount` is set to 1,000,000 tokens, the rate limit will increase over time at the rate determined by the `slope` until it reaches 1,000,000 tokens. At this point the rate limit will stop increasing, but it will resume increasing once an allocation to the Instance has been made.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete parameters (maxAmount, slope) and describes their dynamic behavior with an example, but it does not specify any actual numeric threshold, cap value, or deadline that a regulated party must adhere to; only the mechanism is defined.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism from the catalog or the text reaches this definitional rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication catch-all applies.

assessments.title: Inflow Rate Limits
assessments.description: Limits the speed at which liquidity and exposure can increase within a specific scope or market.
assessments.quote: Inflow rate limits constrain the rate at which allocated liquidity can increase into a scope. "Inflow" means movements that raise exposure or capital allocated to an Instance or market, such as depositing, minting, or rebalancing into a position.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph defines 'inflow' but offers no numeric threshold, formula, metric, deadline, or defined actor. The obligation is expressed qualitatively, making compliance arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No on-chain automatic enforcement is indicated, and no named penalty, review, or capital-at-risk mechanism reaches this conceptual rule. Only the generic catch-all mechanisms could apply, which are always weak.

assessments.title: Outflow Rate Limits
assessments.description: Defines and regulates the rate at which allocated liquidity or exposure can be withdrawn from a scope.
assessments.quote:
Outflow Rate Limits constrain the rate at which allocated liquidity can be withdrawn or exposure reduced from a scope. "Outflow" means movements that lower exposure or capital allocated to an Instance or market, such as withdrawals, redemptions, or unwind operations.

Outflow limits are often configured more permissively to prioritize safety and fast exits. When outflow limits are "unlimited," the rate limits contract simply does not apply a cap in that direction.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines outflow rate limits and describes their operation, but provides no numeric thresholds, formulas, or specific metrics; compliance is entirely qualitative and no concrete obligation is quantifiable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule mentions a rate limits contract that could enforce caps on-chain, but no specific enforcement mechanism UUID is provided or citable from the catalog, and the generic misalignment backstop alone is insufficient, leaving enforcement weak.

assessments.title: MaxSlippage
assessments.description: Sets a configurable decimal parameter to limit maximum allowed price impact during trades or liquidity operations.
assessments.quote: `maxSlippage` is a configurable parameter that sets the maximum allowed price impact or deviation from expected output when executing trades or liquidity operations in a pool. `maxslippage` is expressed as a decimal and must be a non-zero value. This protects against excessive price impact during volatile market conditions.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a concrete parameter (`maxSlippage`) with a numeric constraint (must be a non-zero decimal) that is objectively verifiable. However, the actual maximum allowed value is delegated to a configuration step, leaving a minor gap with no specified magnitude.
metrics: maxSlippage must be a non-zero decimal
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is mentioned; only the generic misalignment catch-all (Reports of Misalignment and Adjudication) applies, which is weak. There is no indication of on-chain automatic enforcement or any named consequence for this parameter rule.

assessments.title: Default Admin Role
assessments.description: Defines the Default Admin Role and its governance-held ownership via the Prime Agent's SubProxy.
assessments.quote: The Default Admin Role (`DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`) is the administrative role of an Instance's access-control contract, authorized to grant and revoke all other roles. It is held by Sky Governance through the Prime Agent's SubProxy. This per-Instance role is distinct from the Beacon's own `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`, which is held by the Pause Proxy.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule precisely identifies the actor (Sky Governance), the mechanism (SubProxy), and the specific permission (grant/revoke all roles). It also clearly distinguishes the Instance role from the Beacon role. The minor gap is the lack of a defined verification cadence or specific on-chain address for the SubProxy.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule operates through on-chain access control. The role's powers are governed by the Pause Proxy for the Beacon, and Emergency Spells (b8266c11) are a defined mechanism available to Sky Governance to execute emergency actions, including potentially granting or revoking roles to enforce this structure's security, providing a strong path for enforcement.

assessments.title: Controller Role
assessments.description: Defines the Controller Role's authority to move assets and update rate limits via the ALM Proxy.
assessments.quote: The Controller Role (`CONTROLLER`) is authorized to call the asset-movement functions on the ALM Proxy and to update the Rate Limits contract. It is held by the Controller contract, which dispatches operations to the relevant Facet on behalf of the Allocator Role.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies the exact actor (CONTROLLER) and concrete function scopes (call asset-movement functions on ALM Proxy, update Rate Limits contract). These are defined and verifiable, but the rule contains no numeric thresholds, formulas, or deadlines—only a qualitative authorization—so it falls into the mixed category.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No catalog enforcement mechanism directly reaches a rule about role authorization. On-chain access control may technically prevent violation, but there is no document UUID for that enforcement; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstops remain, which are weak.

assessments.title: Allocator Role
assessments.description: Defines the authorization and multisig structure for the Allocator Role via the AdministeredAgent and Relayer Multisigs.
assessments.quote: The Allocator Role (`ALLOCATOR_ROLE`) is authorized to initiate allocation operations on behalf of the ALM Proxy, through the Controller. It is held by the AdministeredAgent contract, with the Relayer Multisigs registered as its Actors, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.4 - Actor](636a39e4-5908-4fee-bae8-e0b11e0d9c55), and submitting operations through it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names exact on-chain components and roles (ALLOCATOR_ROLE, AdministeredAgent, Relayer Multisigs, ALM Proxy, Controller) and defines the authorization path, so a third party can verify compliance from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Enforcement is on-chain: the AdministeredAgent contract holds ALLOCATOR_ROLE and only registered Relayer Multisig actors can submit allocation operations through it, so unauthorized operations revert; this role/actor structure is specified in the cited Actor section.

assessments.title: Actor
assessments.description: Defines authorized addresses and multisigs permitted to submit allocation operations to the Controller.
assessments.quote: An Actor is an address registered on the AdministeredAgent that is authorized to submit allocation operations to the Controller through the Allocator Role, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.3 - Allocator Role](e7a97395-ddd5-4ae8-874f-1bb3f247446a). The Relayer Multisigs of a Prime Agent and of the Core Operator are registered as Actors.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule precisely defines an Actor as an address registered on the AdministeredAgent, authorized to submit operations via the Allocator Role. It explicitly names the specific entities (Relayer Multisigs of a Prime Agent and Core Operator) that are registered, making the condition objectively verifiable by a third party.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: While no on-chain mechanism directly prevents an unauthorized submission, the defined actors are bound by the Allocator Role's rules. Unauthorized operations by a Prime Agent, or failure to secure a Relayer Multisig, would violate the controlled processes and trigger the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) for non-compliance.

assessments.title: Revoker
assessments.description: Authorizes specific Revoker addresses to remove Actors as an emergency response measure.
assessments.quote: A Revoker is an address registered on the AdministeredAgent that is authorized to remove an Actor as a rapid-response measure, without affecting the Allocator Role held by the AdministeredAgent. The Freezer Multisig of a Prime Agent is registered as a Revoker, providing the emergency capability to remove a compromised or malicious Actor outside the standard governance process.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names specific actors (Revoker, Freezer Multisig of a Prime Agent), a location (registered on AdministeredAgent), and an action (remove an Actor), but the trigger criteria ('compromised or malicious') and timing ('rapid-response') are qualitative and no thresholds or deadlines are stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph establishes a named emergency enforcement path: the Freezer Multisig Revoker can remove an Actor outside standard governance, matching the defined escalation protocol in the Emergency Response System (1d940c6d), with removal as a concrete remedy.

assessments.title: Grantor
assessments.description: Defines the Grantor role and its authority to authorize Actors within the AdministeredAgent system.
assessments.quote: A Grantor is an address registered on the AdministeredAgent that is authorized to add an Actor, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.4 - Actor](636a39e4-5908-4fee-bae8-e0b11e0d9c55), granting it the ability to submit operations through the AdministeredAgent.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule identifies the actor (Grantor), the controlled system (AdministeredAgent), and the exact capability (add an Actor and enable operations). The authorization state is binary and verifiable on-chain, but the criteria for becoming registered/authorized are referenced elsewhere rather than stated in this paragraph.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The AdministeredAgent's on-chain access-control logic makes this self-executing: only an address registered and authorized as a Grantor can add Actors or submit operations, so unauthorized attempts fail at the contract level. The referenced Actor spec defines that access-control mechanism.

assessments.title: Administered Agent Admin
assessments.description: Defines the Administered Agent Admin role and its authority to manage specific administrative roles via Sky Governance.
assessments.quote: The Administered Agent Admin is an address registered on the AdministeredAgent with authority over its role configuration, able to add and remove the AdministeredAgent's Admins, Grantors, Actors, and Revokers. This role is distinct from the Default Admin Role, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.1 - Default Admin Role](b76195f2-7494-43a4-919e-fa823303ad06), which administers the Diamond PAU access-control contract; both are held by Sky Governance through the Prime Agent's SubProxy.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule identifies a specific role ('Administered Agent Admin') with enumerated authorities (add/remove Admins, Grantors, Actors, Revokers) and defines the actor who holds it (Sky Governance via SubProxy). However, it lacks precise operational thresholds, cadences, or verifiable conditions for exercising this authority; the scope of 'role configuration' is qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule's allocation of administrative power is plausibly subject to the Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7), where the configuration of such roles and their use by Sky Governance could be reviewed as an artifact. No quantified penalty is defined for misuse of the role itself.

assessments.title: Beacon
assessments.description: The Beacon registry restricts Diamond PAU Instances to whitelisted Facets and is controlled via the Pause Proxy.
assessments.quote: The Beacon (`Beacon`) is the registry that whitelists the Facets approved for use by Diamond PAU Instances; an Instance may only delegate calls to Facets registered on the Beacon. It is controlled by Sky Governance through the Pause Proxy. The Beacon's address on Ethereum Mainnet is `0x829dC2b7E94B1954F0764E573f2E0d45Afa28199`, and it is registered in the Chainlog under the key `PAU_BEACON`.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a binary, objectively verifiable condition: an Instance may only delegate to Facets registered on the Beacon (address provided). No numeric threshold, but the condition is exact and a third party can check compliance by inspecting the Beacon's registry.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is enforced by the Diamond proxy contract's own logic, which would revert invalid delegations, but the Atlas provides no mechanism document UUID for this on-chain enforcement, and none of the catalog entries reach this specific rule. No documented consequence path exists.

assessments.title: Facets
assessments.description: Defines the governance-controlled set of singleton Facet contracts used by Diamond PAU Instances.
assessments.quote: The documents herein define the Facets currently approved on the Beacon for use by Diamond PAU Instances. Each Facet is a singleton contract deployed at the Sky ecosystem level and shared across all such Instances. The set of approved Facets is maintained by Sky Governance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a purely descriptive statement about a governance-maintained list of Facet contracts; it imposes no obligation, threshold, metric, or verifiable condition on any actor.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No operational rule exists to trigger enforcement; the paragraph is merely informational and does not create a compliance requirement that any mechanism could reach.

assessments.title: ERC-4626 Facet
assessments.description: The ERC-4626 Facet manages vault interactions using specific share and exchange rate guards.
assessments.quote: The ERC-4626 Facet (`ERC4626Facet`) deposits, withdraws, and redeems against any ERC-4626 vault, under min-shares, min-assets, and max-exchange-rate guards. Its address on Ethereum Mainnet is `0x1dCA18608c89174181153E786778705b4A0E1a06`.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The text is a factual description of a smart contract facet and its address, with no obligation, threshold, or verifiable condition imposed on any actor. It names guard types but does not specify their values or how compliance would be checked.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism from the catalog or the document is cited or implied; the contract's internal guards are automatic but no UUID links them to any defined enforcement doc, and the paragraph itself contains no enforcement UUID.

assessments.title: Adding a Facet
assessments.description: The process for adding a Facet is deferred to a future iteration of the Atlas.

assessments.title: Removing a Facet

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a stub stating that the process will be specified in a future iteration; no operative rule, thresholds, or metrics exist.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism applies because there is no rule to enforce; only a future promise.

assessments.title: Allocator Role
assessments.description: Restricts USDS minting to addresses holding the specific Allocator Role via the Diamond PAU Controller.
assessments.quote: Only an address holding the [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.3 - Allocator Role](e7a97395-ddd5-4ae8-874f-1bb3f247446a) (`ALLOCATOR_ROLE`) may initiate a USDS mint by calling the `usds_mint` function on the Diamond PAU Controller, passing the amount of USDS to mint. The Controller dispatches the call to the USDS Facet, which performs the mint on behalf of the ALM Proxy.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a binary, objectively verifiable condition: only an address holding the Allocator Role may call the `usds_mint` function. A third party can check compliance by inspecting the role assignment and the function call on-chain.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Diamond PAU Controller's `usds_mint` function enforces the `ALLOCATOR_ROLE` check on-chain, making violation impossible; the Allocator Role document (e7a97395) defines this access control, providing strong automatic enforcement.

assessments.title: Rate Limit
assessments.description: Enforces an automatic on-chain transaction revert if USDS minting exceeds the specified rate limit.
assessments.quote: The minting of USDS is subject to the on-chain rate limit identified by `LIMIT_USDS_MINT`. This limit is enforced automatically within the call; the transaction reverts if the amount exceeds the current rate limit.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a specific parameter (`LIMIT_USDS_MINT`) and states that the transaction reverts if exceeded, so the core obligation is quantified. However, the actual numeric threshold value is not provided in the rule text; it is defined elsewhere, leaving a minor gap.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule describes on-chain automatic enforcement (transaction reverts), but the rubric requires a cited mechanism UUID from the catalog or from the text. No UUID in the catalog matches a general rate limit mechanism, and the paragraph text contains no UUID. Therefore, only the generic misalignment backstop applies, which is weak.

assessments.title: Mint USDS To ALM Proxy
assessments.description: Defines the technical process for transferring USDS from the allocator vault buffer to the ALM Proxy.
assessments.quote: The USDS Facet's `mint` function draws the specified amount of USDS from the allocator vault by calling the vault's `draw` function, then transfers that USDS from the vault's buffer to the ALM Proxy.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The text solely describes a technical process of a function's behavior, with no normative obligation, metric, threshold, or compliance requirement for any regulated party.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No obligation exists for a regulated party; thus no enforcement mechanism is relevant.

assessments.title: Allocator Role
assessments.description: Restricts USDS burning via the Diamond PAU Controller to addresses holding the ALLOCATOR_ROLE.
assessments.quote: Only an address holding the [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.3 - Allocator Role](e7a97395-ddd5-4ae8-874f-1bb3f247446a) (`ALLOCATOR_ROLE`) may initiate a USDS burn by calling the `usds_burn` function on the Diamond PAU Controller, passing the amount of USDS to burn. The Controller dispatches the call to the USDS Facet, which performs the burn on behalf of the ALM Proxy.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a fully verifiable condition: only an address holding the specific ALLOCATOR_ROLE may call the named function 'usds_burn' on the Diamond PAU Controller. A third party can objectively check compliance with the role and function signature alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is an on-chain access control rule. The Diamond PAU Controller code, as referenced, will automatically revert any transaction from an address without the ALLOCATOR_ROLE, making violation by an unauthorized actor impossible via code enforcement.

assessments.title: Rate Limit
assessments.description: Enforces an automatic on-chain rate limit on USDS burning and adjusts minting capacity accordingly.
assessments.quote: The burning of USDS is subject to the on-chain rate limit identified by `LIMIT_USDS_BURN`. This limit is enforced automatically within the call; the transaction reverts if the amount exceeds the current rate limit. The burn additionally increases the `LIMIT_USDS_MINT` rate limit by the same amount, where that rate limit is configured, restoring minting capacity.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a concrete on-chain threshold parameter `LIMIT_USDS_BURN`, an automatic revert condition if the burn amount exceeds the current limit, and a same-amount restoration formula for `LIMIT_USDS_MINT`; however, the actual rate-limit values are defined elsewhere and not quantified in this text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph describes an on-chain automatic revert, but no mechanism UUID from the catalog or paragraph text reaches this specific burn rate-limit rule; with no citable mechanism doc, the required scoring rule forces weak and none found.

assessments.title: Burn USDS From ALM Proxy
assessments.description: Defines the technical process for burning USDS from the ALM Proxy to settle allocator vault debt.
assessments.quote: The USDS Facet's `burn` function transfers the specified amount of USDS from the ALM Proxy to the allocator vault's buffer, then wipes the corresponding debt by calling the vault's `wipe` function.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies exact functions and a concrete sequence (USDS Facet burn transfers specified USDS from the ALM Proxy to the allocator vault buffer, then calls the vault's wipe function), but the operative amounts and corresponding debt are unspecified or delegated, with no numeric thresholds or cadence.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No catalogued enforcement mechanism reaches this specific burn/wipe settlement process; the on-chain liquidation penalty and PSM mechanisms do not cover this operation, and only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would remain.

assessments.title: Allocator Role
assessments.description: Restricts Aave v3 market deposits to addresses holding the ALLOCATOR_ROLE via the Diamond PAU Controller.
assessments.quote: Only an address holding the [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.3.3 - Allocator Role](e7a97395-ddd5-4ae8-874f-1bb3f247446a) (`ALLOCATOR_ROLE`) may initiate an Aave v3 market deposit by calling the `aave_deposit` function on the Diamond PAU Controller, passing the address of the aToken and the amount to deposit. The Controller dispatches the call to the Aave v3 Facet, which performs the deposit on behalf of the ALM Proxy.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule is a concrete access-control requirement: only an address holding ALLOCATOR_ROLE may call the named `aave_deposit` function on the Diamond PAU Controller, passing an aToken address and amount. A third party can verify compliance on-chain by checking the caller's role and the function invocation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Violation is made impossible by the Diamond PAU Controller's on-chain access control tied to ALLOCATOR_ROLE, as defined in the referenced Allocator Role document (e7a97395-ddd5-4ae8-874f-1bb3f247446a); unauthorized addresses cannot successfully initiate the deposit.

assessments.title: Add Liquidity To Uniswap v3 Position
assessments.description: Defines the logic for Uniswap v3 liquidity provision, including slippage checks and balance-based deposit verification.
assessments.quote: The Uniswap v3 Facet's `addLiquidity` function attempts to deposit the target amounts of the pool's two (2) tokens on behalf of the ALM Proxy. To open a new position, it calls the Uniswap v3 position manager's `mint` function. To add to an existing position, it calls the position manager's `increaseLiquidity` function instead — but only after confirming the ALM Proxy is the current owner of that position. Depositing into a tick range does not necessarily use the full target amount of both tokens; the Uniswap v3 Facet measures the amounts actually deposited by comparing the ALM Proxy's token balances before and after the call, rather than relying on the target amounts or the position manager's own return values. The deposit does not complete unless the tick bounds fall within the configured bounds for the pool. Before depositing, the Uniswap v3 Facet checks the specified minimums against expected amounts derived from the pool's time-weighted average price, not its current spot price. Those minimums must in turn satisfy the configured maximum slippage for the pool, and the deposit does not complete unless this check passes.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph defines a concrete, step-by-step process with verifiable conditions such as owner confirmation, balance-delta measurement, tick-bound checks, and TWAP-based minimum slippage checks, but all operative limits are delegated as 'configured bounds', 'configured maximum slippage', and 'specified minimums' with no numeric values or formulas in the text.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Core GovOps Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7-2f9f-454c-8add-614dff784f78) plausibly reaches implementation of this liquidity-provision logic through scheduled artifact review and penalty assessment, but the paragraph states no quantified consequence specific to this rule.

assessments.title: Remove Liquidity From Uniswap v3 Position
assessments.description: Defines the multi-step process and slippage constraints for withdrawing liquidity from Uniswap v3 positions via the ALM Proxy.
assessments.quote: The Uniswap v3 Facet's `removeLiquidity` function first confirms the ALM Proxy is the current owner of the position, then decreases the specified amount of liquidity from it. It does this by calling the Uniswap v3 position manager's `decreaseLiquidity` function. Before the decrease, the facet collects any fees the position has already accrued. The `decreaseLiquidity` call itself does not transfer any tokens to the ALM Proxy; it only credits the withdrawn amounts to the position as tokens owed. After the decrease, the facet collects again, and this second collection is what delivers the withdrawn principal to the ALM Proxy. The withdrawal does not complete unless the resulting amounts satisfy the specified minimums, and those minimums must in turn satisfy the configured maximum slippage for the pool. Unlike the deposit-side check on adding liquidity, this check is against the amounts actually withdrawn, measured after the decrease and both collections have already executed; it is not checked against an independent price reference computed before execution.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a precise step-by-step process and a verifiable post-execution check against specified minimums and configured maximum slippage, but the actual threshold values are external parameters not stated in the text.
