assessments.enforcementReasoning: Although the access control is on-chain and self-executing, the rubric requires a cited mechanism UUID from the catalog or document text; no such UUID appears in the paragraph or catalog for this specific access-control rule, so enforcement is rated weak due to lack of a citable mechanism.

assessments.title: Set Trigger For RateLimit Decrease
assessments.description: Allows the Controller role to decrease specific allocation rate limits via a smart contract function.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule is fully specified as executable smart-contract code: it names the CONTROLLER role, defines exact require guards (maxAmount > 0, amountToDecrease <= currentRateLimit), handles the unlimited case, and states the update formula for the new limit.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found: the paragraph is on-chain smart-contract code with internal require guards, but no cataloged enforcement mechanism UUID or UUID in the text reaches this rule, so under the rubric it is weak.

assessments.title: Set Trigger For RateLimit Increase
assessments.description: Allows the Controller role to increase allocation rate limits for specific keys up to a maximum amount.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule is fully specified as executable Solidity code with exact logic, role restrictions, and a formula for the new rate limit; a third party could verify compliance by inspecting the contract code.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is a code snippet that enforces itself on-chain, but no separate enforcement mechanism document is cited in the paragraph, and the rubric's catalog does not include a generic on-chain code enforcement UUID. Therefore, no citable mechanism reaches this rule; only the catch-all misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Initial Concept And Feasibility Discussions
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to document risk capital, asset liability management, and cost estimates for new yield opportunities.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent identifies a yield opportunity on a target chain that can exceed the Base Rate. The Prime Agent estimates Required Risk Capital (RRC) and Asset Liability Management requirements associated with the opportunity and evaluates options for fulfilling them. The Prime Agent also considers exchange and bridging costs, if applicable. Based on this, the Prime Agent develops a net yield target for the opportunity factoring in all of these costs. The output of this step is an internal meeting note summarizing the idea as well as estimates of Required Risk Capital, Asset Liability Management, and exchange / bridging costs.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes a sequence of activities (identify, estimate, evaluate, consider, develop, produce an internal note) but imposes no numeric thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or verifiable standards. Compliance is entirely qualitative and arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this documentation-oriented process step; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply.

assessments.title: Preliminary Required Risk Capital and Asset Liability Management Arrangement
assessments.description: Defines the process for Prime Agents to negotiate and document Junior/Senior Risk Capital and ALM transfers.
assessments.quote: If necessary, the Prime Agent reaches out to other Prime Agents that could provide Junior Risk Capital (JRC) / Senior Risk Capital (SRC) or assume Asset Liability Management obligations. The Prime Agent negotiates with these other Prime Agents and documents these potential deals. The output of this step is an informal confirmation of JRC/SRC and Asset Liability Management transfer details.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes a process (outreach, negotiation, documentation) but relies entirely on qualitative triggers like 'if necessary' and provides no numeric thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or objective verification criteria; compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism other than the weak misalignment catch-all applies to this procedural duty; no automatic, capital-at-risk, or reviewed consequence is specified or implied.

assessments.title: Prime Agent Preparation Of Capital And Operational Plan
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to submit a Capital and Operational Plan including risk capital estimates for new allocations.
assessments.quote:
The Capital and Operational Plan ("C&O Plan") articulates the Prime Agent’s strategy for a proposed new Allocation Instance or a modification to an existing Instance. In addition to articulating the Instance’s strategic objectives and operational parameters, the C&O Plan includes a pro-forma Required Risk Capital (RRC) estimate and a strategy for ensuring sufficient Total Risk Capital (TRC) coverage.

The C&O Plan is the major input into the Artifact Edit Proposal that codifies the new or modified Instance. Following the approval of such a proposal by Prime governance, the details and commitments outlined in the C&O Plan are formally integrated into the respective Instance Configuration Document of the Prime Agent’s Artifact.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires inclusion of a pro-forma RRC estimate and a TRC-coverage strategy, but no formula, numeric threshold, or metric is specified; compliance turns on qualitative judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The obligation to prepare plan contents has no explicit or structural enforcement beyond the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Pro-Forma Instance RRC Estimate
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to prepare pro-forma RRC estimates using defined risk capital models.
assessments.quote: As a critical component of the Capital & Operational Plan, the Prime Agent must prepare an initial pro-forma Instance Required Risk Capital (RRC) estimate. This estimate serves as the basis for the Prime’s capital planning prior to the availability of official RRC figures from Sky Core. The estimate must strictly adhere to the implementation of RRC-models defined in [A.3.2 - Risk Capital](55999acf-75fe-4adf-8584-9746ef50d3e4).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires preparation of a qualitative estimate with no deadline, numeric threshold, or verifiable metric. Compliance would be arguable based on the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No consequence or enforcement mechanism is specified for failing to prepare the estimate; only the generic misalignment backstop (always weak) could apply.

assessments.title: Notional Total Risk Capital (TRC) Coverage Strategy
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to define strategies for maintaining Total Risk Capital coverage for new or modified Instances.
assessments.quote:
As a critical component of the Capital & Operational Plan, the Prime Agent must articulate its strategy for ensuring its Total Risk Capital (TRC) adequately covers the pro-forma Instance RRC of a new or modified Instance and the resulting impact on its Aggregate RRC.

The Prime’s notional TRC coverage strategy must outline how this new Instance’s RRC will be notionally accounted for or supported by the Prime’s overall TRC pool. If the Prime’s current TRC is not sufficient to cover its estimated increased Aggregate RRC, the strategy should outline the Prime Agent’s intended steps for acquiring additional JRC/SRC.

For instance, this risk-capital acquisition strategy could involve:

1. Renting Junior Risk Capital (JRC)
    - Sourcing Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC) by renting it from other Primes through Ecosystem Accords.
    - Sourcing Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) from external capital providers.
2. Sourcing Senior Risk Capital (SRC):
    - Originating SRC through the Sky monthly auction.
    - Renting OSRC from other Primes through Ecosystem Accords.
3. Increasing Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC): A Prime might have plans to bolster its own IJRC through retained earnings or other internal means.
4. Decreasing exposure in an existing Instance(s) to lower Aggregate RRC.

The Prime’s capital-acquisition strategy should indicate how the Prime will remain in compliance with all relevant Atlas rules, such as sourcing ratios that constrain how much Senior Risk Capital can be "enabled" or counted toward a Prime’s Aggregate RRC. See [A.3.2.1.2.3 - Total Risk Capital Sourcing Ratios](9e99b084-f15a-4f60-b831-d6c0bd9aec04).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires a 'strategy' and 'steps' to ensure capital coverage, but the entire obligation is expressed in qualitative, procedural language ('articulate', 'outline', 'indicate'). No numeric thresholds, verifiable formulas, or specific deadlines are provided for assessing the strategy's adequacy; compliance is a matter of judgment on the submitted documentation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This rule is part of the Capital & Operational Plan, which is subject to Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) by Core GovOps. Failure to articulate a plausible strategy could result in a negative review finding and trigger penalties under the general Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12). The consequence is unquantified for this specific documentation rule, but a defined review path exists.

assessments.title: Additional Elements Of Capital And Operational Plan
assessments.description: Mandates specific operational, emergency, and risk reporting elements within the Capital and Operational Plan.
assessments.quote:
The Capital & Operational Plan includes the following additional elements:

- Operational Parameters: defines the Instance’s target chain(s), protocols, initial capital, maximum deposit sizes, and any other parameters that underpin the pro-forma RRC calculation.
- Data Submission Protocol: defines how yields, Required Risk Capital usage, ALM costs, exchange data, etc. will be reported and audited.
- Emergency Procedures: defines mechanisms to be triggered if security or risk capital thresholds are breached, such as a kill switch or partial freeze.
- Asset Liability Management (ALM) Strategy: details if the Prime will meet its ALM requirements through its own direct asset management or by transferring its obligations to another Prime Agent via the ASC Rental Primitive. If the latter, the C&O Plan must reference the governing Ecosystem Accord and its key terms.
- Performance-based Adjustments: define the conditions or KPIs that allow adjustments to Instance deposit caps or yield expansions without requiring a formal Artifact edit.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule enumerates specific sections that must be included in the Capital & Operational Plan, but provides no quantifiable thresholds, metrics, or objective criteria for the content of those sections. Compliance hinges on whether the plan contains the named elements, which a defender could argue is satisfied by any minimal placeholder definition, making it qualitative only.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Capital & Operational Plan is an artifact subject to review by Core GovOps under the Agent Artifact Review mechanism (doc UUID d4bf73e7). If required elements are missing, the review process can flag the deficiency and escalate to penalty assessment. However, no specific quantified consequence is attached to this documentation omission, so the enforcement is plausible but unquantified—mid.

assessments.title: Preliminary Informal Check With Operational GovOps
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to submit Capital and Operational Plans to Operational GovOps for review and approval.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent presents the Capital and Operational Plan for the Allocation Instance to Operational GovOps, including any associated JRC/SRC and Asset Liability Management arrangements. Operational GovOps reviews and either provides an informal greenlight or requests modifications to the Plan. The output of this step is Operational GovOps approval to proceed with a request to revise the C&O Plan, as applicable.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes a qualitative process: the Prime Agent presents a plan and Operational GovOps provides an informal greenlight or modification request. No numeric thresholds, formulas, deadlines, or verifiable criteria are defined; compliance depends on subjective judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or implied beyond the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop, which alone constitutes weak enforcement. The process step is not self-executing and carries no defined penalty.

assessments.title: Agent Inputs
assessments.description: Defines the process for a Prime Agent to draft and submit Allocation Instance updates to Powerhouse.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent drafts an update to the Prime Agent Artifact adding the Allocation Instance to the list of active Allocation Instances and including the information specified in [A.2.2.10.1.2.6 - List Of Allocation Instances](e4975062-6d19-438b-a5d5-cfc1a7fd8cb9). The Prime Agent submits the draft to the Powerhouse system. The output of this step is a draft Prime Agent Artifact update in the Powerhouse system.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes a concrete, identifiable obligation (draft and submit an update) with a defined actor (Prime Agent) and a verifiable output (a draft in Powerhouse). However, the specific content requirements are delegated to an external document, and no deadlines, metrics, or numeric thresholds are provided in this rule itself.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this process step. Only the generic misalignment backstop (c6c6f595) would apply, which is insufficient for a mid or strong rating.

assessments.title: Validation And Off-Chain Vote
assessments.description: Defines the process for reviewing proposals and conducting off-chain snapshot votes via the Operational Executor Facilitator.
assessments.quote: The Operational Executor Facilitator reviews the proposal to ensure that it is complete and aligned with the Atlas. The Operational Executor Facilitator then initiates an off-chain snapshot vote, following the quorum and majority rules in the Prime Agent Artifact. When complete, the result of the vote is recorded in the Powerhouse system. The output of this step is the snapshot vote result recorded in the Powerhouse system.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes a process with a named actor and steps, but the review criteria are entirely qualitative ('complete and aligned with the Atlas'). The quorum and majority rules are delegated to an external artifact without specifying numeric thresholds, leaving compliance arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this procedural rule. Only the generic misalignment and adjudication backstops (catch-all) could apply, which are rated weak.

assessments.title: Official Update of Artifact
assessments.description: Defines the process for finalizing allocation updates and integrating them into risk-capital monitoring systems.
assessments.quote:
If the Allocation Instance is successfully approved, the Operational Executor Facilitator finalizes and publishes the update to the Prime Agent Artifact, making it effective in the Atlas. The output of this step is an updated Prime Agent Artifact with the new Allocation Instance.

Once a new Instance is deployed, its data is integrated into risk-capital monitoring systems and its RRC will be officially determined and tracked via the Sky Core RRC Dashboard. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.1 - Sky Core Required Risk Capital (RRC) Dashboard](4eac2c9e-2718-4881-a3f1-ed10fb3f4d13). This official RRC figure supersedes the Prime-prepared pro-forma RRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the Operational Executor Facilitator and enumerates concrete steps (finalize, publish, integrate, determine RRC), but provides no quantifiable metric, threshold, or deadline to objectively verify compliance; only the occurrence of actions is regulated, not their timing or quality.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism (penalty, conservatorship, on-chain automatic, etc.) is tied to this procedural duty; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which alone is always weak.

assessments.title: Instance Setup Deployments
assessments.description: Requires Core Council Risk Advisor approval of Risk Capital estimates before updating Allocation Instance parameters.
assessments.quote:
The documents herein define how the deployment of an Allocation Instance is executed on-chain. In the short-term, an Allocation Instance may also be deployed using the process for Interim Deployments specified in [A.1.10.2.3.2.2.2 - Interim Deployments](9b3edbbf-89d1-42da-a9c3-18f858f8471f).

The Prime Agent must subsequently prepare a pro-forma Required Risk Capital estimate, which must be approved by the Core Council Risk Advisor, before the parameters of the Instance can be updated for normal operation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names an actor (Prime Agent), a required output (pro-forma Required Risk Capital estimate), an approving authority (Core Council Risk Advisor), and a condition (before Instance parameters are updated for normal operation). However, no numeric threshold, formula, or criteria for the estimate's content or approval are provided, leaving the core requirement qualitative and reliant on delegated judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Agent Artifact Review process (d4bf73e7) periodically examines procedural compliance. A Prime updating parameters without the required approval would be a detectable violation during review, potentially triggering findings and penalties via the penalty machinery. This provides a plausible but unquantified consequence.

assessments.title: Conduit Development And Testing
assessments.description: Requires GovOps to test new Allocation Instances for logic, slippage, and oracle accuracy before scaled deployment.
assessments.quote: Once formally validated, the Prime Agent implements the new Allocation Instance based on the specifications in the Prime Agent Artifact. Operational GovOps must test the Allocation Instance with minimal funds from the Prime Agent’s Central Allocation Buffer, verifying deposit / withdrawal logic, slippage constraints, and oracle checks. If this testing is successful Operational GovOps confirms that the Allocation Instance satisfies all risk constraints specified in the Prime Agent Artifact. The output of this step is validated contracts for the Allocation Instance and a green light to proceed with a scaled deployment.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule obligates Operational GovOps to test, verify, and confirm, but no quantified thresholds, metrics, or precise amounts are given. 'Minimal funds' is qualitative, and the testing scope is judgment-based, making compliance arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism cited. Neither on-chain automatic enforcement, capital-at-risk, nor a named escalation path reaches this testing requirement. Only the catch-all misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Initial Deployment and Required Risk Capital / Asset Liability Management Execution
assessments.description: Defines the process for deploying funds from the Operational Buffer into Allocation Instances using specific slippage tolerances.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent finalizes JRC/SRC and Asset Liability Management Arrangements. Operational GovOps records these arrangements in the Powerhouse interface. If Operational GovOps is charged with operationalizing an Instance, it deploys funds from the Prime Agent’s Operational Buffer into the Allocation Instance, performing any necessary DEX exchanges. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.1 - Operationalization Of Allocation Instances](989512c2-4fa1-46b8-947c-00e3c0b56024). In doing so, Operational GovOps follows instructions in the Agent Artifact regarding the amount of capital to deploy and slippage tolerances. The output of this step is a fully deployed Allocation Instance conforming to Risk Capital and Asset Liability Management requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule instructs Operational GovOps to follow Agent Artifact instructions on the amount of capital and slippage tolerances, but those values are delegated to an external artifact. No quantitative thresholds appear in the text, making compliance not fully verifiable from the rule alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule requires the output to conform to Risk Capital and Asset Liability Management requirements; violation of those requirements triggers Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and can escalate to Conservatorship (5c3dd35a), providing a strong enforcement path.

assessments.title: Operationalization Of Allocation Instances
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents using proprietary strategies to define KPIs and allows GovOps to intervene upon underperformance.
assessments.quote:
Prime Agent teams may choose to directly operationalize their Allocation System Primitive Instances ("Instances") using internal, proprietary strategies that are not defined in their Artifacts. Alternatively, Prime Agents may elect to have the Instances operationalized by their Operational Executor Agent. This constitutes an exception to the general rule that Operational Executor Agents operationalize all Sky Primitives on behalf of Prime Agents. See [A.1.14.3.4 - Agent Role Delineation](fdf32ca5-5e2e-481e-9047-4d1599547216).

For Prime Agent teams that operationalize their Instances, they will be required to formulate KPIs for their proprietary strategies; should an Instance under-perform these KPIs, Operational GovOps is authorized to step in and operationalize the Instance(s) via a back-up strategy that is defined in the Agent Artifact. Additional logic on this point will be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires Prime Agents to formulate KPIs and allows GovOps to intervene for underperformance, but 'under-perform' is not defined, no objective thresholds or measurement cadence are specified, and compliance is a matter of judgment.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule's authorization for Operational GovOps to step in lacks a defined trigger or escalation process and is not linked to any catalogued enforcement mechanism; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, and the 'future iteration' stub indicates no current actionable mechanism.

assessments.title: Sky Core Required Risk Capital (RRC) Dashboard
assessments.description: Mandates the use of the RRC Dashboard as the authoritative source for calculating required risk capital.
assessments.quote:
The Sky Core Required Risk Capital (RRC) Dashboard serves as the official system for determining and disseminating RRC figures for Prime Agents and their Allocation System Primitive Instances.

Prior to the full operational deployment of the Powerhouse system, Prime Agents must utilize the Sky Core RRC Dashboard as the authoritative source for their official Instance Total RRCs and Aggregate RRC. Data from this source is to be used for all internal TRC management, required reporting and compliance assessments.

The Sky Core RRC Dashboard is located at [https://info.skyeco.com/required-risk-capital](https://info.skyeco.com/required-risk-capital).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the actor (Prime Agents), the authoritative source (dashboard URL), and the specific data items (Instance Total RRCs, Aggregate RRC) to be used for reporting and compliance. However, it lacks numeric thresholds or formulas, making it a qualitative procedural mandate.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule's requirement to use the dashboard for compliance assessments can be enforced through the Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7), which includes penalty assessment for non-compliance. This provides a plausible enforcement path, though the consequence is not quantified for this specific rule.

assessments.title: Interim Notice Regarding RRC Dashboard Coverage
assessments.description: Requires Instance Configuration Documents to specify the RRC Framework Full Implementation status for asset types.
assessments.quote: Some Allocation System Instances displayed on the RRC Dashboard concern asset types whose risk models have not yet been fully developed. See [A.3.2.1.1.4.3 - Financial Risk Models](2af9fa64-ab25-4017-920c-f1c07dff4c06). An active Instance’s respective Instance Configuration Document will specify its `RRC Framework Full Implementation` status as either `Covered` or `Pending`.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a binary field (Covered/Pending) to be specified in an Instance Configuration Document, which is a verifiable requirement, but no criteria or metric determine when the status is Covered vs Pending — the decision is delegated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism targets compliance with this field specification; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop exists.

assessments.title: Primes' Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to manage Total Risk Capital to meet Aggregate Required Risk Capital requirements.
assessments.quote:
Prime Agent teams are responsible for managing their Total Risk Capital (TRC) to continuously meet their Aggregate Required Risk Capital (RRC). The accounting of TRC considers all on-chain holdings and any off-chain agreements, encumbrances, or conditions that may affect the immediate availability or eligibility of capital for RRC coverage. For a definition of Total Risk Capital, see [A.3.2.1.2.1 - Total Risk Capital Definition](6f6b25d6-f73c-4733-ba37-12a0a411433c).

The documents herein define requirements and standards for a Prime Agent’s internal TRC management systems.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a clear obligation to maintain TRC ≥ Aggregate RRC, which is a verifiable numeric inequality once RRC is known, but the Aggregate RRC value is not specified in this paragraph, only referenced externally. That missing parameter is a minor gap.
metrics: continuously meet their Aggregate Required Risk Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Falling below the Aggregate RRC constitutes a risk capital incident; the Risk-Capital Incident Response mechanism (12b7d480) directly activates and permits Sky Core to impose penalties up to conservatorship, a defined escalation with a named enforcer distinct from the Prime Agent.

assessments.title: Objective of Prime TRC Management
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to maintain internal TRC management systems for capital adequacy and real-time shortfall alerting.
assessments.quote:
To comply with Atlas risk capital requirements, Prime Agent teams must establish, maintain, and operate an internal system for TRC management. A Prime Agent’s internal TRC management system should enable proactive operational risk management. This entails ongoing capital adequacy assessment and strategic capital allocation planning for current and future Allocation System Primitive Instances, including the ability to perform scenario analyses for potential deployments or market stresses.

Prime Agents’ internal TRC management systems should enable them to maintain continuous sufficiency of the Prime Agent’s held TRC against its official Aggregate RRC. This requires real-time or near real-time comparison and internal alerting mechanisms to prevent and address potential shortfalls.
Primes must ensure that their internal TRC management systems maintain comprehensive, verifiable internal records of all TRC components, related transactions, and compliance activities to support internal governance and external verification processes, such as the submission of TRC Reports to Core GovOps. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.3 - Primes’ TRC Report](41ca2085-d71b-47e5-8b1a-b183b6e2b6fc).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes real obligations—establishing an internal system, capacity assessments, alerting, record-keeping—but all criteria are qualitative ('proactive', 'continuous sufficiency', 'near real-time', 'comprehensive, verifiable'). No thresholds, formulas, or verifiable metrics are given; compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is anchored to 'Atlas risk capital requirements'; if a TRC shortfall occurs and the internal system's failure contributed, the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Conservatorship (5c3dd35a) general machinery plausibly apply. Artifact review (d4bf73e7) could also surface inadequacy. Consequences are not quantified for this specific process requirement, so rating is mid.

assessments.title: Minimum Capabilities of Prime TRC Management Systems
assessments.description: Mandates Prime Agent systems track risk capital components, dynamic states, and implement shortfall response protocols.
assessments.quote:
A Prime Agent’s internal TRC management system should possess the following capabilities to meet the objectives outlined in [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.1 - Objective of Prime TRC Management](9a8120c4-0a5b-426f-97a5-283c708413f5).

1. Prime Agents’ internal TRC management systems should enable compliant sourcing and tracking of all TRC components, including Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC), Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC), Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC), and Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). Compliance in this context includes strict adherence to eligibility criteria and capital-sourcing ratios (e.g., External Per Internal, Senior Per Junior) as defined in the Atlas. See [A.3.2.1.2.3 - Total Risk Capital Sourcing Ratios](9e99b084-f15a-4f60-b831-d6c0bd9aec04).
The system must provide real-time or near real-time tracking of all held Total Risk Capital (TRC) components. This includes, for each TRC component:
    - Accurate valuation of the assets comprising each component.
    - Clear identification of the source of each component (e.g., Prime’s own SubProxy for IJRC, specific Ecosystem Accord references for rented PEJRC or OSRC, TEJRC encumbrance details, OSRC origination details).
    - Verification of each TRC component’s eligibility status according to Atlas rules. This includes tracking whether capital is “enabled” or “active” for RRC coverage purposes (e.g., based on Ecosystem Accord status, compliance with sourcing ratios, etc.).
    - Distinction between capital directly held by the Prime Agent and capital that is encumbered (e.g., PEJRC where the lending Prime retains custody but the capital is contractually committed).
2. Prime Agents' internal TRC management systems should enable dynamic-state accounting. The system must account for TRC components that are in dynamic, pending, or off-chain states, as these can impact the true risk capital available to a Prime Agent. This includes:
    - Pending transactions such as PEJRC or OSRC rental Ecosystem Accords that have been committed to by the parties, but not yet codified in the Atlas.
    - Capital in transit, e.g., assets that are committed to be IJRC, but currently moving between chains via bridges or locked in Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol (CCTP) messages awaiting finality.
    - Operational expenditures funded by TRC components (typically IJRC), such as blockchain transaction fees, oracle service fees, audit costs, and other operational overhead that reduces available risk capital. The system should track these expenditures in real-time or near real-time.
    - Any off-chain factors that could impair the immediate deployability or availability of TRC components.
3. Prime Agents' internal TRC management systems should enable continuous capital adequacy monitoring. The system must enable the near real-time comparison of the Prime Agent's internally tracked and calculated TRC against its official Aggregate RRC, as obtained from the Sky Core RRC Dashboard. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.1 - Sky Core Required Risk Capital (RRC) Dashboard](4eac2c9e-2718-4881-a3f1-ed10fb3f4d13). This core functionality is essential for the Prime Agent to proactively monitor its capital adequacy, identify potential or actual TRC shortfalls, and make timely operational and capital management decisions to maintain compliance.
4. Prime Agents' internal TRC management systems should define a RRC-incident (e.g., TRC shortfall) response protocol. The system should enable internal alerting mechanisms that detect when a Prime Agent’s TRC approaches predefined internal buffer thresholds relative to its Aggregate RRC. See [A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.1 - Encumbrance Ratio](5435f680-aaaa-461a-bcae-4056bb8964d9). The system should also detect an actual shortfall where the Prime Agent’s held TRC falls below its Aggregate RRC. Furthermore, Prime Agent teams should establish and document internal processes for responding to such alerts. Such internal processes should include: 1) internal escalation and assessment of the shortfall’s cause and magnitude; 2) formulation of potential responses or corrective actions, which may include sourcing additional TRC, reducing risk-weighted exposures, or other measures; 3) internal decision-making framework for the evaluation of potential responses and selection of the most appropriate one; and 4) notifying any pertinent parties (Operational GovOps) as needed for the purpose of planning or implementing follow-up action.

Prime Agent teams' internal decision-making framework may consider the economic trade-offs of various actions, including the strategic acceptance of penalties for a TRC shortfall where such an approach is determined to be economically advantageous compared to immediate rebalancing (e.g., avoiding excessive transaction costs or market impact).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule lists qualitative capabilities (e.g., 'real-time or near real-time tracking', 'accurate valuation', 'clear identification') with no numeric thresholds, formulas, or deadlines. Compliance is entirely judgment-based; a third party could not objectively verify whether the system 'enables' these capabilities.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule. The capabilities are internal system requirements with no direct penalty, review, or automatic consequence. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Primes’ TRC Report
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to submit periodic reports attesting to their Total Risk Capital composition and requirements.
assessments.quote: Prime Agents are required to submit periodic Total Risk Capital (TRC) Reports to provide an accurate and verifiable attestation of their TRC composition and adherence to capital requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires periodic TRC Reports but specifies no cadence, format, or quantified metrics; 'periodic' is qualitative, and attestation of 'adherence' lacks objective criteria.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Agent Artifact Review mechanism (d4bf73e7) plausibly covers TRC Reports as agent artifacts, enabling Core GovOps to review submission and accuracy, with staged findings and penalty assessment, though no specific consequence is quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Mandate and Rationale
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to submit periodic TRC reports and attestations regarding their Aggregate Required Risk Capital compliance.
assessments.quote:
Prime Agents are required to periodically submit TRC Reports to Core GovOps. This report serves a dual purpose. It provides a verifiable snapshot of the Prime Agent's TRC composition and key capital ratios as of the end of the reporting period; and second, it provides a formal attestation regarding the Prime Agent's maintenance of TRC at or above its dynamically changing Aggregate Required Risk Capital (RRC) throughout the entire reporting period. See [A.3.2.1.1.2 - Aggregate RRC](6aed5cc1-9671-4b73-88a9-fdd86ac93ece).

This comprehensive reporting, encompassing both an end-of-period statement and disclosures of any intra-period events affecting TRC, is essential. On-chain data alone (such as that captured by the planned OVRC system) cannot definitively prove the full eligibility and unimpaired availability of a Prime Agent's capital position for continuous RRC coverage, nor can it capture all off-chain factors. These factors include, but are not limited to, whether assets are subject to Prime-initiated off-chain contractual pledges, if the economic value or redeemability of its bridged assets is compromised by issues with their originating bridge, or if its assets are encumbered by derivative structures or other off-chain commitments that would impair their immediate use at any point during the period.

The TRC Report serves as an important basis for Core GovOps’ verification procedures. This entails: 1) reconciling reported end-of-period TRC components against the Sky Atlas, on-chain data, and other relevant sources to validate the period-end capital position and adherence to Atlas-defined capital requirements; and 2) reviewing Prime Agents’ attestations and disclosures regarding its TRC management and any material events throughout the reporting period to assess continuous compliance with its dynamically changing Aggregate RRC. The outcome of this validation is a critical input for the monthly settlement cycles, which latter includes the determination and retroactive application of penalties for any identified discrepancies or violations of capital requirements during the period.

The long-term vision is for the Powerhouse system to enable the automation of TRC data aggregation and verification. The Powerhouse system will have capabilities such as directly querying Prime Agent SubProxy accounts for IJRC assets, programmatically accessing and interpreting Ecosystem Accords recorded in the Atlas, interfacing with TEJRC and OSRC smart contract systems, and automatically applying Atlas-defined eligibility rules. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.3.1 - Continuous Monitoring Of On-chain Verifiable Risk Capital (OVRC)](8048bdf0-84b7-4546-8f1a-98b62d073c84). Even in this advanced state, the TRC Report, or a similar form of periodic attestation, may remain necessary to cover elements of TRC verification that are not fully able to be automated or require explicit Prime Agent declaration.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule clearly requires periodic TRC Reports with a defined snapshot and attestation, but the reporting cadence is left as 'periodically' without a fixed frequency, making the timing qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph explicitly states that validation outcomes feed monthly settlement cycles with 'retroactive application of penalties for any identified discrepancies or violations of capital requirements,' directly activating the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and escalating to Conservatorship (5c3dd35a) for breaches.

assessments.title: TRC Report Contents
assessments.description: Mandates specific TRC reporting components and attestation requirements for Prime Agents to manage allocation risk.
assessments.quote:
The Total Risk Capital (TRC) Report submitted by a Prime Agent must provide an accurate and verifiable breakdown of all TRC components held by the Prime Agent as of the end of the specified reporting period. The TRC Report should include the following essential information:

- Aggregate TRC Value As of End of Period: The total declared value in USD of all eligible TRC components held by the Prime Agent as of the end of the reporting period.
- Detailed Breakdown of TRC Components As of End of Period: For each category of TRC held, the report must detail the following values as of the end of the reporting period:
    - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC): The total amount of IJRC, a breakdown of its constituent asset types, and their respective values in USD.
    - Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC): The total amount of PEJRC. For each portion of PEJRC sourced from another Prime Agent, the report must include the amount in USD, the identifier of the counterparty Prime Agent, the expiry date of the arrangement, and a direct reference to the Ecosystem Accord that governs the PEJRC arrangement.
    - Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC): The total amount of TEJRC. For each TEJRC source, the report must include the amount in USD, the identifier of the TEJRC smart contract or facility and any relevant encumbrance identifier.
    - Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC): The total amount of OSRC. The report must specify the amount originated directly by the Prime Agent from the Total Senior Risk Capital (TSRC) pool and any amount of OSRC rented from other Prime Agents. For any rented OSRC, the report must include the amount in USD, the identifier of the counterparty Prime Agent, the expiry date, and a direct reference to the pertinent Ecosystem Accord.
    - Key Ratio Inputs and Computed Totals (Prime Internal Calculation) As Of End Of Period: Based on the component values reported above (as of the end of the reporting period), the report must include key figures used in and resulting from the Prime Agent's internal capital adequacy calculations. These figures reflect the capital structure and ratios as of the end of the reporting period and include:
        - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC)
        - External Junior Risk Capital (EJRC) generated via External Per Internal Ratio (Prime External Junior Risk Capital + Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital sourced via the EPI ratio still carries Senior Per Junior or SPJ capacity)
        - EJRC-via-SPJ (sourced by spending SPJ capacity; zero-SPJ-capacity thereafter)
        - Enabled Senior Risk Capital (SRC)
        - Total Senior Per Junior capacity
            - Allocation of SPJ capacity to 1) enable SRC; or to 2) source EJRC
        - Prime-computed eligible Total Risk Capital (IJRC + EJRC-via-EPI + EJRC-via-SPJ + enabled SRC)
        - Official Aggregate RRC
        - Capital buffer = TRC – Aggregate RRC
        - Effective ratios
            - EPI = EJRC-via-EPI ÷ IJRC
            - SPJ utilisation:
                - enabled SRC ÷ total SPJ capacity
                - EJRC-via-SPJ ÷ total SPJ capacity
- Dynamic Period Attestation and Disclosures: In addition to the end-of-period snapshot figures, the TRC Report must include an Attestation from the Prime Agent confirming it maintained TRC at or above its Aggregate RRC at all times throughout the entire reporting period. In addition, the TRC Report must include disclosure of any events, Prime-initiated off-chain contractual obligations, impairments to the value or redeemability of held assets (such as RWA backing or bridged asset viability), encumbrances, or other conditions that occurred at any point during the reporting period which materially affected its TRC, even if such conditions were temporary or not continuously visible to on-chain monitoring systems. This disclosure must include the nature of the event/condition, its precise timing and duration, and its quantified impact on the Prime Agent's TRC.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule enumerates specific data fields that must be included in the TRC Report (amounts, identifiers, expiry dates, ratios, attestation, disclosures), making the reporting obligation objectively verifiable. However, the reporting period is referenced but not defined here, and the requirement of 'accurate' is qualitative, leaving minor gaps.
metrics: Aggregate TRC Value As of End of Period
Detailed Breakdown of TRC Components (IJRC, PEJRC, TEJRC, OSRC with amounts, counterparties, expiries, accord references)

Key Ratio Inputs and Computed Totals (IJRC, EJRC-via-EPI, EJRC-via-SPJ, enabled SRC, total SPJ capacity, allocation, Prime-computed eligible TRC, Official Aggregate RRC, Capital buffer, EPI, SPJ utilisation)
Attestation confirming TRC >= Aggregate RRC at all times throughout the reporting period
Disclosure of material events with nature, timing, duration, and quantified impact
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The TRC Report is an agent artifact subject to scheduled review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7), which can lead to penalty assessment (b8ee2d12) if found non-compliant. No automatic on-chain enforcement or quantified penalty specific to this reporting rule, but the review path provides a plausible consequence.

assessments.title: Continuous Monitoring Of On-chain Verifiable Risk Capital (OVRC)
assessments.description: Requires an autonomous system to monitor OVRC and trigger pro-rata penalties for shortfalls against Aggregate RRC.
assessments.quote:
An autonomous monitoring system must be designed and implemented to enable continuous tracking of Prime Agents’ on-chain verifiable risk-capital components in near real-time. The on-chain, verifiable risk-capital components that can be tracked by such a monitoring system in real time are termed "On-chain Verifiable Risk Capital" (OVRC).

OVRC is not necessarily equivalent to Total Risk Capital (TRC). A Prime Agent’s actual TRC cannot be determined definitively without accounting for off-chain agreements, encumbrances or other relevant conditions affecting capital eligibility or availability, which conditions must be disclosed in the TRC Reports submitted by Prime Agents. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.3 - Primes’ TRC Report](41ca2085-d71b-47e5-8b1a-b183b6e2b6fc).

Where the OVRC of a Prime Agent is less than its Aggregate RRC, the shortfall will be logged and penalty accrual will commence on a pro-rata, per-second basis for the duration and magnitude of the observed shortfall, according to the penalty schedule defined in the Atlas. Thus, this on-chain monitoring system serves as an interim penalty ledger.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a clear trigger (OVRC < Aggregate RRC) and a computational method (pro-rata per-second penalty accrual), but delegates the specific penalty amounts to an external schedule, so a third party can verify shortfall and accrual direction but not exact penalty value without the schedule.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule's own text describes on-chain automatic per-second penalty accrual on any OVRC-below-Aggregate-RRC shortfall per the Atlas penalty schedule and interim penalty ledger (Penalty Mechanisms, b8ee2d12) — self-executing enforcement reaching the Prime's shortfall directly, the strongest form.

assessments.title: Validation of TRC Report In General
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to submit periodic Total Risk Capital reports to Core GovOps for validation.
assessments.quote: Prime Agents are required to submit periodic Total Risk Capital (TRC) Reports to Core GovOps. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.3 - Primes’ TRC Report](41ca2085-d71b-47e5-8b1a-b183b6e2b6fc). The protocol for validation of Primes’ TRC reports is defined in the documents herein.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires 'periodic' Total Risk Capital reports, but defines no cadence, deadline, or objective criteria for when a report is considered submitted or timely. Compliance is arguable on the same facts; a third party cannot verify it from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement consequence is linked to this reporting requirement; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is always weak. No mechanism cited here or implicitly triggered by the rule.

assessments.title: Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process
assessments.description: Mandates Core GovOps to validate Prime capital reports through on-chain reconciliation and Accord verification.
assessments.quote:
Core GovOps receives TRC Reports from Primes on a regular basis and must perform the following validation process.

Core GovOps verifies against the Atlas any Ecosystem Accord referenced in the TRC Report for sourced Prime-External Junior Risk Capital (PEJRC) or rented Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). This includes confirming the existence, current validity, and terms of such Accords as formally recorded within the Atlas.

Core GovOps validates the Prime Agent's reported IJRC by reconciling the reported IJRC amount and its constituent asset composition against the actual on-chain state of the Prime Agent’s designated SubProxy account. This involves direct on-chain verification of asset balances. Core GovOps verifies that all assets reported as IJRC and held within the SubProxy account meet the definition of "eligible assets" for IJRC as defined by the Atlas. See [A.3.2.1.2.2.1.1.1 - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC)](8728abee-0dc5-449b-b4c2-78698da16f10).

For reported Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) and Originated Senior Risk Capital directly originated by the Prime, Core GovOps validates the reported amounts and statuses by cross-referencing data from the relevant smart contract systems. This may involve querying TEJRC pool contracts, OSRC auction records, and other on-chain infrastructure to confirm the existence, ownership, and eligibility of these capital components.

Core GovOps reviews all attestations and disclosures made by the Prime Agent in the TRC Report. This review focuses on understanding the Prime Agent's TRC compliance with Aggregate RRC throughout the entire reporting period. This assessment is critical for identifying intra-period shortfalls that might not be visible to on-chain monitoring systems or reflected in the end-of-period snapshot alone. The assessment process may include requiring the Prime Agent to provide supplementary documentation, verifiable evidence, or independent third-party confirmations for material off-chain claims or attestations concerning intra-period events; and/or cross-referencing disclosed off-chain information with relevant on-chain indicators or transactions that might corroborate or contradict the attestations.

Finally, Core GovOps independently calculates and verifies the Prime Agent's compliance with all Atlas-defined capital sourcing ratios (e.g., External Per Internal (EPI), Senior Per Junior (SPJ)).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule enumerates a series of validation steps (verify accords, reconcile IJRC on-chain, review attestations, calculate ratios) but provides no numeric thresholds, deadlines, or objective pass/fail criteria. Compliance is a matter of judgment, not verifiable by a third party from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism targets Core GovOps' performance of this validation duty. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, which is insufficient for a higher rating.

assessments.title: Finalized Determination Of TRC Position And Penalties
assessments.description: Defines the process for reconciling TRC shortfalls and adjusting Prime Agent penalties based on validated reports.
assessments.quote:
After reaching a definitive accounting of Prime Agents’ capital position and TRC adequacy, penalties are finalized by Core GovOps. This involves reconciling the interim penalty ledger (derived from the OVRC system) with the definitive TRC history, which incorporates all validated information from the TRC Report including any intra-period shortfalls.

1. If the validated TRC Report indicates that the Prime Agent's TRC was below its Aggregate RRC during the reporting period, and this actual shortfall was more severe than, or not detected by, the OVRC monitoring system, then penalties will be finalized as follows: if the OVRC system had already accrued penalties, these will be adjusted upwards to match the actual shortfall; if the OVRC system had not detected a shortfall, penalties will be assessed and applied retroactively based on the full duration and magnitude of the actual shortfall.
2. If the validated TRC Report confirms that TRC shortfalls were identical in duration and magnitude to those logged by the OVRC monitoring system throughout the reporting period: the penalties accrued in the interim penalty ledger will be confirmed and finalized.
3. If the validated TRC Report confirms that TRC was higher than a misleading OVRC reading during a specific portion of the reporting period which led to an erroneously logged penalty: Core GovOps will adjust or void the penalty accordingly.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete actors (Core GovOps), metrics (TRC, Aggregate RRC, OVRC), and enumerated cases for reconciling penalties, but the adjustment magnitudes are qualitative (e.g., 'adjusted upwards to match', 'retroactively based on full duration and magnitude') without quantifying penalty rates or thresholds, making compliance only partially verifiable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph describes a penalty-finalization step for Core GovOps but provides no specific consequence for failure to perform it; only the generic misalignment reporting and adjudication catch-alls (c6c6f595, 560e1024) could reach it, which are weak.

assessments.title: Risk-Capital Incident Response
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to define incident response frameworks for Required Risk Capital within their operational artifacts.
assessments.quote:
Where a Prime Agent’s Allocation System Instances are operationalized by its Operational Executor Agent, the management of and response to Required Risk Capital (RRC)-related incidents requires a defined framework within each Prime Agent's Artifact (the Multi-Instance Coordinator Document for the Allocation System Primitive) and its associated Executor Accord.

While the Prime Agent's strategic team ("Prime Team") determines the specific rectification strategy for an RRC incident—considering its holistic portfolio, prevailing market conditions, and the potential for strategic acceptance of penalties—this discretion is exercised subject to the authority of Sky Core to impose penalties and take corrective measures, up to and including the conservatorship of a Prime Agent, to protect the ecosystem and make any losses whole.

This document will be developed further in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph explicitly states 'This document will be developed further in a future iteration of the Atlas,' making it a stub with no operative, verifiable obligations. The text lacks any quantified metrics, thresholds, deadlines, or defined verification conditions.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph directly states Sky Core's authority to impose penalties and conservatorship for RRC incidents, making violation subject to the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Conservatorship For Breach Of Capital Requirements (5c3dd35a). These are defined escalation paths with concrete remedies.

assessments.title: Instance Operational Conformance
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to define processes for monitoring and addressing operational deviations from instance configurations.
assessments.quote: Operational deviation from Artifact specifications can render an Instance’s RRC, and thus the Prime’s Aggregate RRC, invalid. Prime Agents must therefore ensure that each Allocation System Instance adheres to its respective Instance Configuration Document. Whether a Prime self-operationalizes its Allocation System or contracts with an Operational Executor Agent, its Agent Artifact must define processes for monitoring for, and addressing deviations of, Instance operational conformance. This document will be developed further in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph ends with an explicit future-iteration stub, rendering the entire provision aspirational and non-binding; no concrete, verifiable obligation exists yet.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism applies to a provision that is explicitly deferred to a future iteration; the obligation does not currently bind actors.

assessments.title: Asset Liability Management
assessments.description: Requires future definition of requirements and infrastructure for Asset Liability Management.
assessments.quote: Requirements and infrastructure related to Asset Liability Management shall be defined in a future iteration of the Atlas.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule is an explicit stub, stating only that requirements and infrastructure for Asset Liability Management will be defined in a future iteration. No current obligations, metrics, thresholds, or deadlines are provided.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule imposes no present obligations and has no defined consequence for failure to define future requirements. Only the generic misalignment backstop could theoretically apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Allocation Instance Adjustments, Scaling, And Settlement
assessments.description: Requires token holder votes for exposure changes outside specified limits and mandates retroactive penalty application for violations.
assessments.quote: On an ongoing basis, the Prime Agent team or Operational GovOps operates the Allocation Instance, scaling exposure up and down. Any change to the Allocation Instance outside of the limits specified in the Prime Agent Artifact or requiring judgment on the part of Operational GovOps (where the Allocation System Instance is operationalized by the Operational Executor Agent) requires a new vote of Prime Agent token holders. See [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.3.1 - Modification Of Existing Instances](c1b5708c-e88f-45e0-92e1-b76e68b34f13). As part of monthly and quarterly settlement cycles, Core GovOps reviews yields and obligations, applying penalties retroactively for any previously undisclosed violations. In the event of any such violations, Operational GovOps may be required to take escalatory steps based on the fallback strategy in the Prime Agent Artifact.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule obligates a new token holder vote for changes outside artifact-specified limits or requiring Operational GovOps judgment. The vote requirement is concrete, but the threshold limits are delegated to the Prime Agent Artifact without being stated here, creating a minor gap in verifiability. The retroactive penalty clause is unquantified.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph directly states that Core GovOps reviews and applies retroactive penalties for undisclosed violations. This provides a distinct enforcer (Core GovOps) and a specific penalty path, which aligns with the general Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12). The penalty amount is not specified, so the consequence is real but unquantified, making it mid-level.

assessments.title: Modification Of Existing Instances
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to initiate an Artifact Edit Proposal to modify existing Allocation System Primitive Instance parameters.
assessments.quote: When a Prime Agent wishes to modify an existing Allocation System Primitive Instance in a manner that cannot be accommodated by the existing operational parameters defined in its Agent Artifact, the Prime Agent must initiate an Artifact Edit Proposal process as detailed herein.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a qualitative trigger ('cannot be accommodated by the existing operational parameters') and a clear obligation (initiate an Artifact Edit Proposal), but provides no numeric thresholds, metrics, or verifiable criteria to determine when this trigger occurs. Compliance is arguable either way on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism specific to this procedural rule is cited or apparent. The rule does not tie to on-chain automatic enforcement, capital at risk, or any named penalty machinery. Only the generic misalignment reporting and adjudication backstop (catch-all) could apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Conditions Requiring Artifact Edit Proposal
assessments.description: Mandates an Artifact Edit Proposal for parameter changes exceeding ranges or materially altering the risk profile.
assessments.quote:
An Artifact Edit Proposal is mandatory for an Instance modification under the following conditions:

1. a desired modification to the Instance's operational parameters falls outside the pre-defined operational ranges codified in the respective Instance Configuration Document or other applicable Artifact Documents; or
2. a desired modification, even if notionally within defined ranges in the Artifact, is determined by Operational GovOps to materially alter the Instance's risk profile in a way that could invalidate the underlying Capital and Operational Plan and, consequently, the premises driving the current Required Risk Capital (RRC) for that Instance. Operational GovOps retains the discretion to require an Artifact Edit Proposal if a proposed change, regardless of its fit within existing operational ranges, is determined to pose a material change to the assessed risk.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule contains a precise condition (modification outside pre-defined operational ranges, objectively verifiable from the Instance Configuration Document) and a qualitative condition (determined by Operational GovOps to materially alter risk profile, involving discretion). This mix yields a 3.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Artifact Edit Proposal process is subject to Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7), which assesses compliance and can impose penalties. If an Instance modification is made without the required proposal, this review mechanism could detect and penalize the violation. No automatic on-chain enforcement exists.

assessments.title: Revision of Capital and Operational Plan for Instance Modification
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to update Capital and Operational Plans and risk capital estimates before modifying an Instance.
assessments.quote:
Prior to submitting an Artifact Edit Proposal for an Instance modification, the Prime Agent must revise the Capital and Operational Plan (C&O Plan) associated with that Instance to reflect the desired new state.

The revised Capital and Operational Plan for an Instance modification must include the following information:

1. Updates to the Instance's strategy and operational parameters;
2. A new pro-forma Required Risk Capital (RRC) estimate specifically calculated to reflect the Instance's proposed modified state; and
3. A revised notional Total Risk Capital (TRC) coverage strategy, detailing how the Prime Agent will manage any changes to the Instance RRC and the consequential impact on its Aggregate RRC, including plans for acquiring additional JRC or SRC if necessary.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a specific actor (Prime Agent), a trigger (before submitting an Artifact Edit Proposal), and three enumerated content requirements (strategy updates, Required Risk Capital estimate, Total Risk Capital coverage). However, the content items lack quantitative thresholds, formulas, or verification criteria; compliance with the qualitative aspects could be argued either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) would examine the Capital and Operational Plan as part of an Artifact Edit Proposal; if a Prime fails to provide the required updates, the review could lead to findings and penalty assessment, but no quantified consequence is specified for this particular planning requirement.

assessments.title: Governance Process for Instance Modification
assessments.description: Defines the multi-step governance and review process required to modify Prime Agent artifacts and operational plans.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent's revised Capital and Operational Plan forms the core of the Artifact Edit Proposal for the Instance modification. This proposal must be submitted to the Operational Executor Facilitator for review. The Facilitator assesses the proposal for completeness and general alignment. Following this review, the proposal is subjected to the Prime Agent's governance process for approval to edit the Agent Artifact, typically involving a token holder vote as defined in the Prime Agent's Root Edit Primitive.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes a process with only qualitative obligations: the Facilitator 'assesses for completeness and general alignment', and a token holder vote is 'typically' involved but not defined as a strict requirement. No quantitative metrics, deadlines, or verifiable criteria are provided; compliance would be arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule. The general misalignment reporting (c6c6f595) and adjudication (560e1024) catch-alls would be weak alone, and no on-chain, capital-at-risk, or priced incentives apply to this governance step.

assessments.title: Post-Approval Integration and RRC Update
assessments.description: Defines the process for integrating approved plan modifications and determining official Required Risk Capital via the dashboard.
assessments.quote:
If the Artifact Edit Proposal for the Instance modification is approved through the Prime Agent’s governance process, the relevant content from the revised Capital and Operational Plan is formally integrated into the respective Instance Configuration Document within the Prime Agent's Artifact.

Once the modified Instance is operational under its new, approved parameters and its data is integrated into the ecosystem’s monitoring systems, its adjusted Required Risk Capital (RRC) will be officially determined and tracked via the Sky Core RRC Dashboard. This official RRC figure then supersedes the Prime-prepared pro-forma RRC that was part of the modification proposal.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes a process (integration of approved content, determination and tracking of RRC via a dashboard) but provides no quantifiable thresholds, formulas, deadlines, or objective verification criteria. Compliance is expressed in judgment language ('formally integrated', 'officially determined') with no measurable standards, making it arguable either way.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this administrative process rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Allocation System Input Requirements
assessments.description: Mandates that all Allocation System Primitive inputs must be compliant and complete for valid deployment.
assessments.quote: The documents herein define the required inputs for a valid Invocation of the Allocation System Primitive. If any input is noncompliant or omitted, the Primitive will be invalidated and the Allocation Instance deployment will not move forward.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph merely states that inputs must be compliant and complete, but 'compliant' is qualitative and the list of required inputs is defined elsewhere—no thresholds, formulas, metrics, or deadlines are specified. A party could plausibly dispute what constitutes a noncompliant input on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule says the Primitive will be invalidated if inputs are noncompliant or omitted, but no specific enforcement mechanism from the catalog or document text reaches this declaration. Without a citable on-chain automatic enforcement doc, the only backstop is the catch-all misalignment reporting, which is weak.

assessments.title: Global Activation Status
assessments.description: Requires the Allocation System Primitive to be in a state of Global Activation.
assessments.quote: The Allocation System Primitive must be Globally Activated.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a clear obligation (Global Activation) but lacks any quantitative threshold, definition of the state, verification method, or measurable criteria. Compliance is binary but unverifiable from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is identified in the paragraph or implicitly applicable. Violation could only be pursued via the generic misalignment/adjudication catch-all processes, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Core Allocation Vault Address
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to specify their Core Allocation Vault address within the Prime Agent Artifact.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent Artifact must specify the address of the Prime Agent’s Core Allocation Vault.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires a defined actor (Prime Agent) to include a specific, objectively verifiable piece of data (the Core Allocation Vault address) in a specific artifact (the Prime Agent Artifact). Compliance can be checked by any third party simply by inspecting the artifact for a valid address; no interpretation or measurement is needed.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The artifact is subject to Core GovOps review (d4bf73e7), which can flag a missing required address and trigger the penalty machinery (b8ee2d12). However, no specific quantified consequence is defined for this particular omission, so the enforcement is mid.

assessments.title: Core Allocation Buffer Address
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to specify a Core Allocation Buffer address within their artifact.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent Artifact must specify the address of the Prime Agent’s Core Allocation Buffer.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes a concrete, binary obligation: the artifact must specify an address. A third party can easily check compliance. However, there is no numeric threshold or formula; it is a simple field requirement, making it precise but not a quantified metric.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Prime Agent Artifact is subject to scheduled review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7), which can detect a missing Core Allocation Buffer address and trigger staged findings and potential penalties. This creates a plausible enforcement path, though no automatic or quantified consequence is specific to this rule.

assessments.title: Allocation System Core Security Parameters
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to specify rate limiter addresses and parameters for vaults and buffers.
assessments.quote: The Prime Agent Artifact must specify the rate limiters for the Allocation Vault and Core Allocation Buffer, including the address and parameters for each.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires the artifact to specify rate limiter addresses and parameters, which is a concrete, verifiable checklist item. However, the content of 'parameters' is not defined, leaving the operative requirements qualitative; a party could comply with trivially uninformative parameters.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Violation (missing or inadequate specification) would be detectable via Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7), which can assess compliance and publish findings. assessments.title: Step 2: Aggregate Backstop Capital
assessments.description: Defines how Step 2 Capital is allocated to grow Aggregate Backstop Capital based on specific floor and target thresholds.
assessments.quote:
Step 1 Capital that remains after the Step 1 allocation becomes Step 2 Capital.

The allocation of Step 2 Capital depends on the level of Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)) relative to the Turbo-Fill Floor (see [A.3.5.3.2.2 - Turbo-Fill Floor](db2aaf07-4ebb-4e5d-ae5e-575717d8fbcd)) and the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.2.1 - Target Aggregate Backstop Capital](f73dda95-0b1c-4bdc-b957-469253d27281)).

When Aggregate Backstop Capital is below the Turbo-Fill Floor, fifty percent (50%) of Step 2 Capital is retained to grow Aggregate Backstop Capital. The remainder of Step 2 Capital becomes Step 3 Capital and is allocated as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121).

When Aggregate Backstop Capital is at or above the Turbo-Fill Floor and below the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital, the portion of Step 2 Capital retained to grow Aggregate Backstop Capital is calculated as fifty percent (50%) multiplied by the fill factor, where the fill factor is one (1) minus the ratio of current Aggregate Backstop Capital to the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital. The remainder of Step 2 Capital becomes Step 3 Capital and is allocated as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121).

When Aggregate Backstop Capital is at or above the Turbo-Fill Floor and at or above the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital, none of Step 2 Capital is retained; all of Step 2 Capital becomes Step 3 Capital and is allocated as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies exact percentages (50%) and a formula (fill factor = 1 - current/target) with clear conditions based on referenced thresholds, making compliance objectively verifiable.
metrics: fill factor = 1 - (current Aggregate Backstop Capital / Target Aggregate Backstop Capital)

assessments.quote: Internal Senior Risk Capital (ISRC) consists of a portion of the excess capital of the Sky Protocol that is reinvested in providing Senior Risk Capital to Prime Agents. ISRC is sourced from Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)) in two components: one hundred percent (100%) of any Aggregate Backstop Capital in excess of the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.2.1 - Target Aggregate Backstop Capital](f73dda95-0b1c-4bdc-b957-469253d27281)), plus one third (1/3) of Aggregate Backstop Capital up to the Target Aggregate Backstop Capital.

assessments.title: Allocation Modification
assessments.description: Core Council may modify capital allocations and bypass standard governance polls via executive vote.
assessments.quote:
In the short term, the Core Council may reduce the allocations of Step 1 Capital (see [A.2.3.1.2.2 - Step 1: Security And Maintenance](324e9d22-70fe-4e44-82ab-118815f5c42e)) and Step 2 Capital (see [A.2.3.1.2.3 - Step 2: Aggregate Backstop Capital](2b28d464-e683-48ba-9a66-2fee05ea0a88)) below their specified levels and restore them up to those levels, and modify the allocation of Step 3 Capital among its three specified uses (see [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121)). A reduction to the Step 1 allocation may be apportioned among its components as the Core Council determines. For Step 2 Capital, the specified level is the retention its allocation formula specifies for the current state. The Core Council exercises this authority through a public post by the Core Facilitator on the Sky Forum, confirmed by Core GovOps and the Core Council Risk Advisor.

The implementation of such modifications is authorized to proceed directly to an Executive Vote without requiring a prior Governance Poll.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete parameters (Step 1, Step 2, Step 3 allocations) and a defined procedural path (public post, confirmations, executive vote), but the magnitude of permitted reductions and the duration of 'short term' are not quantified, leaving the operative limits qualitative.

assessments.title: Operational Processes
assessments.description: Defines the monthly settlement cycle for revenue allocation, SRC origination, USDS conversions, and Smart Burn Engine updates.
assessments.quote:
The Monthly Settlement Cycle (MSC) synchronizes several key operational processes across the ecosystem, including:

1. Sky Protocol’s net revenue from the previous month is calculated and allocated through the steps of the Treasury Management Function. See [A.2.3 - Treasury Management](6c0af059-5d33-4e2b-90f1-1606957b8f85).
2. The monthly Senior Risk Capital (SRC) origination process is settled: the clearing price is established, costs are deducted from winning Prime Agents’ accounts, and their accounts are credited with Originated SRC (OSRC) for the upcoming month. See [A.3.2.2.4.3.5 - Settlement Of Origination](fff0112a-58dd-4041-97f9-7baf113b4e70).
3. Queued conversions between USDS and srUSDS within the SRC system are processed. See [A.3.2.2.4.2.2 - Deposit And Redemption Queues](38a99586-4a13-4ce3-8b2f-cee025e0c390).
4. Pioneer Incentive Pools are funded with an amount equivalent to the Sky Savings Rate multiplied by the balance of Unrewarded USDS. See [A.2.2.9.3 - Pioneer Chain Primitive](4c7be4c6-44b5-407a-94ae-3d7ca7e8039c).
5. Smart Burn Engine parameters are updated at each Monthly Settlement Cycle based on the prior month's state. See [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121) and [A.3.5.2 - Smart Burn Engine Parameters](ddb90fee-2851-4bf0-b924-f1d73e30ce7a).
6. Critical Core GovOps functions related to the operationalization of Sky Primitives are executed, including payment/reimbursement processing, compliance monitoring, and the calculation and application of retroactive penalties.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is purely descriptive, listing processes that occur during the Monthly Settlement Cycle without imposing any obligation, threshold, or verifiable condition on any actor.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific consequence attaches to this descriptive statement; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Calculation Of Applicable Balance
assessments.description: Defines the formula for calculating interest-bearing utilized USDS by subtracting specific idle and protected balances.
assessments.quote:
Interest is calculated on utilized USDS. Utilized USDS is the liquidity a Prime Agent has borrowed from Sky, less:

- USDS held idle in an ALM Proxy
- USDS held idle in a Peg Stability Module
- USDS attributable to a Sky Direct Exposure, as specified in [A.2.2.10.1.1.1.1 - Sky Direct Exposures](b3fb8653-8503-4a9e-81b2-5e9f49ad6703)
- USDS held idle in an AMM pool
- USDS supplied to a lending pool that is not borrowed from that pool
