assessments.title: Severity Of Breaches
assessments.description: Establishes a tiered penalty structure for breaches of Risk Capital requirements based on severity levels.
assessments.quote: The financial penalties for breaches of Risk Capital requirements depend on whether the breaches are Low Severity or High Severity. The documents herein define Low Severity and High Severity Breaches. The financial penalties associated with High Severity Breaches and Low Severity Breaches are defined in [A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.4 - Financial Penalties For Low Severity Breaches](f4bef3da-45a1-4575-9e38-78f2a1f95a3d) and [A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.5 - Financial Penalties For High Severity Breaches](970c1ce7-dc45-4c02-bad4-80c9f2e32eab), respectively.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph merely states that breaches are categorized as Low or High Severity and that definitions and penalties are in other documents. It contains no thresholds, metrics, or verifiable conditions; it is a structural pointer with no operative rule.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this classification statement; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply.

assessments.title: Low Severity Breach Definition
assessments.description: Defines a Low Severity Breach based on the Encumbrance Ratio threshold.
assessments.quote: A Low Severity Breach is one in which the Encumbrance Ratio is greater than or equal to 100% but less than 103%.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a Low Severity Breach with exact numeric thresholds for the Encumbrance Ratio (>=100% and <103%), making it fully quantified and objectively verifiable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The definition is part of the Penalty Mechanisms framework; a breach triggers quantified financial penalties under that mechanism (b8ee2d12), providing a specific consequence with a defined path.

assessments.title: High Severity Breach Definition
assessments.description: Defines a High Severity Breach as an Encumbrance Ratio exceeding 103%.
assessments.quote: A High Severity Breach is one in which the Encumbrance Ratio is greater than 103%.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a single numeric threshold: Encumbrance Ratio greater than 103%. It is fully quantified and objectively verifiable; a third party could check compliance from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The definition triggers the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and escalates to conservatorship (5c3dd35a) for breach of capital requirements, providing a specific, defined path with concrete remedies.

assessments.title: Length Of Breaches
assessments.description: Defines the methodology for calculating the duration of severity-level breaches for penalty mechanism application.
assessments.quote:
The length of a breach refers to the duration measured between its defined start and end points, which depend on the specific aspect of the breach being considered.

If a breach is initially a Low Severity Breach and subsequently becomes a High Severity Breach, then (1) the length of the Low Severity Breach is the duration from when it became a Low Severity Breach until it became a High Severity Breach; and (2) the length of the High Severity Breach is the duration from when it became a High Severity Breach until that high-severity period concludes (e.g., upon final resolution of the breach or a transition to a different severity level).

Likewise, if a breach is initially a High Severity Breach and subsequently becomes a Low Severity Breach, then (1) the length of the High Severity Breach is the duration from when it became a High Severity Breach until it became a Low Severity Breach; and (2) the length of the Low Severity Breach is the duration from when it became a Low Severity Breach until that low-severity period concludes (e.g., upon final resolution of the breach or a transition to a different severity level).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a clear methodology for splitting breach duration when severity transitions occur, but the exact start and end points of a breach are delegated to 'the specific aspect of the breach being considered' without enumeration, leaving a minor gap.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule directly supports the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12), which impose quantified financial penalties for breaches; the duration calculation is integral to penalty application, making enforcement strong.

assessments.title: Financial Penalties For First 30 Minutes
assessments.description: Applies a 500% APY penalty on risk capital shortfalls during the first 30 minutes of a breach.
assessments.quote: For the first 30 minutes of a Low Severity Breach, the financial penalty is equal to a 500% annual percentage yield on the difference between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a fully quantified penalty: 500% APY on the shortfall for the first 30 minutes of a Low Severity Breach. All elements are numeric and verifiable.
metrics: difference between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The penalty is directly imposed by the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12), which defines quantified financial penalties for risk capital breaches. This is a specific, strong enforcement path.

assessments.title: Financial Penalties For Subsequent 30 Minutes
assessments.description: Applies a 1,000% APY penalty on Risk Capital shortfalls during subsequent low severity breaches.
assessments.quote: For the next 30 minutes of a Low Severity Breach after the expiration of the duration specified in [A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.4.1 - Financial Penalties For First 30 Minutes](32750a35-acf3-4248-a5f0-6787a7fc0cd7), the financial penalty is equal to a 1,000% annual percentage yield on the difference between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a fully quantified penalty: 1,000% APY on the shortfall between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital for a defined 30-minute window. All elements are numeric and verifiable.
metrics: difference between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The penalty is a direct application of the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12), which provide a defined institutional path for imposing quantified financial penalties on Primes for Risk Capital breaches.

assessments.title: Financial Penalties After 60 Minutes
assessments.description: Imposes a 1,500% APY penalty on Risk Capital shortfalls after a 60-minute breach window.
assessments.quote: After the first 60 minutes of a Low Severity Breach, the financial penalty is equal to a 1,500% annual percentage yield on the difference between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a fully quantified penalty: 1,500% APY on the shortfall after 60 minutes of a Low Severity Breach. The formula, threshold, and timing are explicit and verifiable.
metrics: difference between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is a specific penalty under the Penalty Mechanisms framework (b8ee2d12), which provides quantified financial penalties for Risk Capital shortfalls. The penalty is directly defined and enforceable via that mechanism.

assessments.title: Financial Penalties For First 15 Minutes
assessments.description: Sets a 1,500% APY penalty for Risk Capital shortfalls during the first 15 minutes of a breach.
assessments.quote: For the first 15 minutes of a High Severity Breach, the financial penalty is equal to a 1,500% annual percentage yield on the difference between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a fully quantified penalty: 1,500% APY on a defined capital shortfall for exactly 15 minutes. All terms are numeric or refer to defined capital aggregates, making compliance objectively verifiable.
metrics: difference between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is a direct specification under the Penalty Mechanisms (A.3.2.2.7.2), which empowers Sky Core to impose quantified financial penalties for Risk Capital breaches. The penalty is precisely defined and enforceable via that mechanism.

assessments.title: Financial Penalties For Subsequent 15 Minutes
assessments.description: Applies a 2,000% APY penalty on Risk Capital shortfalls during high severity breaches.
assessments.quote: For the next 15 minutes of a High Severity Breach after the expiration of the duration specified in [A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.5.1 - Financial Penalties For First 15 Minutes](b9bfd816-925e-4403-a4c2-fda647a2c59a), the financial penalty is equal to a 2,000% annual percentage yield on the difference between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a precise formula: a 2,000% APY penalty on the shortfall between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital for a specific 15-minute window. All terms are defined or quantifiable, making compliance objectively verifiable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The penalty is a direct application of the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12), which establishes quantified financial penalties for Risk Capital breaches. This mechanism provides a defined enforcement path with concrete consequences.

assessments.title: Financial Penalties For Subsequent 30 Minutes
assessments.description: Sets a 2,500% APY penalty for Risk Capital shortfalls during high severity breaches.
assessments.quote: For the next 30 minutes of a High Severity Breach after the expiration of the duration specified in [A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.5.2 - Financial Penalties For Subsequent 15 Minutes](7d3dc8ba-d12c-4583-91eb-9a6d29dffd8d), the financial penalty is equal to a 2,500% annual percentage yield on the difference between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a fully quantified penalty: 2,500% APY on the shortfall between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital, applied for a specific 30-minute window during a High Severity Breach. All inputs are numeric or defined elsewhere, making compliance objectively verifiable.
metrics: difference between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is a direct financial penalty within the Penalty Mechanisms framework (b8ee2d12), which explicitly provides quantified penalties for Risk Capital shortfalls. The penalty is defined and enforceable, creating a strong incentive to comply.

assessments.title: Financial Penalties After 60 Minutes
assessments.description: Applies a 3,000% APY penalty on Risk Capital shortfalls after a 60-minute breach window.
assessments.quote: After the first 60 minutes of a High Severity Breach, the financial penalty is equal to a 3,000% annual percentage yield on the difference between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a fully quantified penalty formula: 3,000% APY on the shortfall after 60 minutes of a High Severity Breach. The inputs (breach status, capital amounts) are defined elsewhere, but the penalty itself is objectively verifiable from the text alone.
metrics: difference between Aggregate Required Risk Capital and Total Risk Capital
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is a quantified financial penalty, directly enforced through the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) that impose such penalties on Primes for Risk Capital shortfalls. This is a specific consequence with a defined path.

assessments.title: Collection Of Penalties
assessments.description: Defines the calculation and transfer process for penalties from Prime Agent accounts to Sky.
assessments.quote: Penalties are calculated by the Core Executor Agents as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. See [A.2.4 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle](6f8d5065-d6ff-4add-9a28-eadeffa7ed1a). Once calculated, penalties are transferred from the Prime Agent’s SubProxy Account to Sky by Sky Governance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies who calculates penalties (Core Executor Agents), when (as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle), and who transfers them (Sky Governance). The process is fully defined with named actors and a clear cadence; the only minor gap is that the calculation method is delegated to a referenced document, but the collection obligation itself is precise.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism targets the collection process itself. Failure to calculate or transfer penalties would only be reachable through the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop, which is weak.

assessments.title: Alternative Enforcement Mechanisms
assessments.description: Defines alternative penalty collection methods if a Prime Agent's Risk Capital falls below required levels.
assessments.quote:
In the event that the Prime Agent’s Total Risk Capital is less than its Required Risk Capital at the time of the Monthly Settlement Cycle, or the collection of the penalty would cause the Prime Agent’s Total Risk Capital to fall below its Required Risk Capital, then Sky may exercise the alternative enforcement mechanism described below.

In this instance Sky, at its discretion, may issue additional tokens of the Prime Agent and sell them on the open market until it has collected proceeds equal to the calculated penalty. Any proceeds above the calculated penalty shall be refunded to the Prime Agent SubProxy account.

Alternatively, Sky may convert the penalty into a debt owed by the Prime Agent to Sky Core at terms mutually agreed between Sky Core and the Prime Agent.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger condition is precisely defined with a numeric comparison (Total Risk Capital < Required Risk Capital) and a specific time (Monthly Settlement Cycle). The first alternative enforcement action (token issuance and sale until proceeds equal the penalty) is clear, but the second alternative (debt conversion at mutually agreed terms) introduces a qualitative gap.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule grants Sky discretionary power to use alternative enforcement; there is no consequence for Sky failing to exercise it. Only the generic misalignment backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Short-Term Exemption
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to maintain an Encumbrance Ratio of 90% or less during the interim phase.
assessments.quote: While the Risk Framework undergoes refinement, penalties for any Prime Agent breaches of Required Risk Capital will be calculated by Core GovOps once the infrastructure is in place to do so. This calculation serves the purposes of system monitoring, data gathering, and framework calibration. However, throughout this interim phase, such calculated penalties will not be formally assessed against Prime Agents, and consequently, Prime Agents will not be required to make payment for these penalties. Notwithstanding this temporary exemption from penalty payment, Prime Agents are expected to maintain a Encumbrance Ratio of less than or equal to 90%. See [A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.1 - Encumbrance Ratio](5435f680-aaaa-461a-bcae-4056bb8964d9).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a numeric threshold (Encumbrance Ratio ≤ 90%) but uses 'expected to' rather than a mandatory obligation, making compliance arguable; a defender could claim the rule is not binding.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph explicitly suspends penalty assessment and payment during the interim phase, so the penalty mechanisms do not apply. No other enforcement mechanism is specified; only the generic misalignment backstop remains, which is weak.

assessments.title: Additional Token Issuance For Breach Of Capital Requirements
assessments.description: Core GovOps may mandate Prime Agents to issue and sell additional tokens to remedy capital shortfalls.
assessments.quote: In the event that financial penalties are not sufficient to address the shortfall because payment of the penalties would exacerbate an existing capital shortfall, Core GovOps may require the Prime Agent to issue additional tokens and sell them to the extent it deems necessary. Operational GovOps will assist Core GovOps in executing any such transaction. Future iterations of the Risk Capital framework will specify a more detailed methodology for required token issuance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule grants Core GovOps discretion to require token issuance 'to the extent it deems necessary,' with no quantitative thresholds, formulas, or metrics. The methodology is explicitly deferred to future iterations, making compliance arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Non-compliance with a Core GovOps directive to issue tokens would constitute a breach of capital requirements, triggering the conservatorship process (5c3dd35a) where Core GovOps escalates to an Executive Vote and Sky Core Facilitator takes control, providing a defined and strong consequence.

assessments.title: Restrictions On Investments For Breach Of Capital Requirement
assessments.description: Core GovOps may restrict Prime Agents from using specific Instances or limit their exposure to them.
assessments.quote: Core GovOps may impose whatever restrictions it deems necessary on the usage of the Allocation System Primitive by the Prime Agent, including limiting the Prime Agent’s exposure to certain Instances (conduits) or prohibiting the Prime Agent from using certain Instances. These restrictions may extend for a period of time that Core GovOps deems fit.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule grants Core GovOps complete discretion ('whatever restrictions it deems necessary', 'for a period of time that Core GovOps deems fit') with no numeric thresholds, formulas, metrics, or objective criteria. A third party cannot verify compliance from the text alone; the obligation is entirely qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is embedded in the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Conservatorship (5c3dd35a) framework. A Prime Agent's violation of restrictions imposed under this rule would constitute a breach of the penalty mechanism, plausibly triggering financial penalties or escalation to conservatorship. However, the consequence is unquantified for this specific rule and requires Core GovOps to initiate enforcement.

assessments.title: Conservatorship For Breach Of Capital Requirements
assessments.description: Defines the conservatorship process and expedited governance vote required to take control of a defaulting Prime Agent.
assessments.quote: In the event that less extreme measures are not adequate to address the capital shortfall, Core GovOps may seek to put the Prime Agent into conservatorship, in which case the Sky Core Facilitator takes direct control of the Prime Agent to maximize value for Sky and other Prime Agent stakeholders. Seeking to put a Prime Agent into conservatorship requires immediate escalation to Sky Core Governance and requires an expedited Executive Vote as specified in [A.1.9.1.5.4.1 - Known And Uncontentious Remedies](3f5f79fa-698c-42db-a941-ead5a5d0aa48).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names actors and a condition ('less extreme measures are not adequate to address the capital shortfall'), but the trigger is entirely qualitative with no numeric thresholds, metrics, or verifiable criteria; compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific consequence attaches to violating this rule; it is a permissive procedural step. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak. No on-chain, capital-at-risk, or named enforcement mechanism reaches this rule.

assessments.title: Financial Penalties For Operational Executor Agents
assessments.description: Establishes future requirements for Operational Executor Agents to provide collateral to insure Prime Agent risk capital breaches.
assessments.quote: In the near term there are no penalties for Operational Executor Agents for failure of the Prime Agents they supervise to maintain appropriate levels of capital. In future iterations of the Risk Framework, Operational Executor Agents will be required to put up collateral and act as "insurers" of all activities by the Prime Agents they supervise with regard to the Sky Primitives. At that point Core GovOps will be able to seize this collateral in the event of failure to obtain compensation for breaches of the Risk Capital requirement by the Prime Agent.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph explicitly states there are no penalties in the near term and that requirements will be specified in future iterations; no current obligation exists for Operational Executor Agents.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No current rule exists to enforce; the described collateral seizure mechanism is only planned for future iterations and not active today.

assessments.title: Termination Of Executor Accord
assessments.description: Defines termination and replacement procedures for Executor Accords if supervision of Prime Agents fails.
assessments.quote: In the event that Core GovOps determines that the Operational Executor Agent is not appropriately supervising the activities of the Prime Agent, Core GovOps may terminate the respective Executor Accord. This requires an immediate escalation to Sky Governance and requires an expedited Executive Vote as specified in [A.1.9.1.5.4.1 - Known And Uncontentious Remedies](3f5f79fa-698c-42db-a941-ead5a5d0aa48). Core GovOps must arrange for another Operational Executor Agent to stand in until the Prime Agent can Invoke the Executor Accord Primitive to enter into a new Executor Accord. The Prime Agent must suspend all operations until a new Executor Accord is voted on and formally integrated into the Agent’s Artifact.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The trigger condition 'not appropriately supervising' is entirely qualitative with no metrics, thresholds, or verifiable criteria. The rule defines actors and a process, but compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is a discretionary power of Core GovOps, not an obligation. No mechanism compels its exercise or penalizes inaction; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply.

assessments.title: Triggers For Escalation
assessments.description: Mandates Sky Governance escalation for Risk Capital penalty disputes and extraordinary remedies like conservatorship or termination.
assessments.quote: In the event of a disagreement regarding the penalties for a violation of Risk Capital requirements, either party may escalate the matter to Sky Governance. In addition, the extraordinary remedies of Prime Agent Conservatorship and Executor Accord Termination must always be escalated to a Sky Governance Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a qualitative trigger (disagreement) and a mandatory escalation path for extraordinary remedies, but contains no numeric thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or verifiable conditions; compliance is arguable based on whether a disagreement exists.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this procedural rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Sky Governance Process
assessments.description: Defines the escalation and resolution process for matters brought to Sky Governance.
assessments.quote: Once a matter has been escalated to Sky Governance, the Sky Core Facilitator may request any information they deem necessary from Core GovOps, Operational GovOps, and the Prime Agent. Sky Governance then acts through a Governance Poll to determine its resolution of the matter.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule enumerates steps (escalation, information request, Governance Poll) but provides no criteria, thresholds, or deadlines for the resolution; the obligation to hold a poll is verifiable, but the substance is qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this procedural governance rule; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Asset Liability Management
assessments.description: Establishes universal rules for Prime Agents to manage collateral allocation and maintain USDS peg stability.
assessments.quote: The Asset Liability Management framework establishes universal rules for Prime Agents deploying Sky’s Collateral Portfolio to maintain the stability of the USDS peg through highly liquid assets. The Asset Liability Management framework governs collateral allocation across all Agents, via the Allocation System Primitive, and replaces Sky Core’s historical Asset Liability Management mechanisms which will be offboarded entirely or transitioned to Prime Agents.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph describes the framework's purpose and scope but contains no operative rule, threshold, metric, or verifiable condition. It is purely descriptive and aspirational, with nothing a third party could check for compliance.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific obligation is imposed, so no enforcement mechanism applies. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would be available, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Minimum Demand Absorption Buffer
assessments.description: Requires a percentage of the Sky Collateral Portfolio to be held in a liquid Demand Absorption Buffer.
assessments.quote: The Asset Liability Management also ensures that a certain percentage of the Sky Collateral Portfolio is invested in a Demand Absorption Buffer, highly liquid market making USDS assets that trade for close to 1 USD per USDS. In this way, if there is ever upward pressure on the price of USDS these assets can be used to sell USDS to maintain the peg.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states an obligation to hold 'a certain percentage' in a Demand Absorption Buffer, but no numeric threshold, formula, or measurement cadence is provided. The obligation is qualitative and compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule. The buffer's purpose is peg maintenance, but no automatic on-chain enforcement, penalty, or named enforcer is defined for the buffer size requirement. Only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Application To Prime Agents
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to maintain specific percentages of Actively Stabilizing Collateral and Demand Absorption Buffer.
assessments.quote: Each Prime Agent investing a portion of the Sky Collateral Portfolio must maintain, with respect to its portion of same, the percentage of Actively Stabilizing Collateral and Demand Absorption Buffer specified in [A.3.3.2.2 - Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral](475fe222-9e4a-4e9d-9be6-a7a424ce02f8). By ensuring that every Prime Agent maintains these levels, Sky as a whole remains compliant with the required thresholds of Actively Stabilizing Collateral and Demand Absorption Buffer.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule clearly obligates each Prime Agent to maintain the percentage of Actively Stabilizing Collateral and Demand Absorption Buffer specified in A.3.3.2.2. The threshold is defined in that referenced section, so the core obligation is quantified, but the numeric value is not repeated in this paragraph, creating a minor gap.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Violation of the percentage requirement could be identified through Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) and penalized via the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12). No on-chain automatic enforcement or quantified consequence specific to this rule exists, so enforcement is mid.

assessments.title: Application To Sky Core
assessments.description: Sky Core manages and allocates the Sky Core Collateral Portfolio to Actively Stabilizing Collateral during transition.
assessments.quote: While its legacy ALM infrastructure is being transferred to Prime Agents, Sky Core manages the portion of the Sky Collateral Portfolio not deployed by Prime Agents ("Sky Core Collateral Portfolio"). During this transitional period, Sky Core allocates the Sky Core Collateral Portfolio to Actively Stabilizing Collateral as specified in [A.3.3.2.6 - Sky Core Asset Liability Management Rules](8135523a-dd5f-482d-b522-ec4227746eaf).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph assigns Sky Core to manage and allocate the Sky Core Collateral Portfolio to Actively Stabilizing Collateral as specified in a referenced section, but provides no numeric thresholds, formulas, or verifiable metrics within this text; it is a qualitative delegation to another document.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this transitional allocation rule for Sky Core itself; only the generic misalignment backstop (catch-all) would apply, which is weak. No on-chain automatic enforcement, capital-at-risk, or named penalty path targets this internal directive.

assessments.title: Peg Defense Event
assessments.description: Mandates Prime Agent responsibilities and collateral requirements during extraordinary peg stability threats.
assessments.quote: In addition to the requirement for Prime Agents to hold a certain percentage of their Collateral Portfolio in Actively Stabilizing Collateral and the Demand Absorption Buffer, Prime Agents have special responsibilities in extraordinary situations where the stability of the peg is threatened. The definition of these events and the obligations for Prime Agents are specified in the implementation of the framework. See [A.3.3.2 - Implementation](bf1a1991-1c2b-457c-b1ca-6147049e93c5).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states that Prime Agents have special responsibilities during peg defense events, but the events and obligations are not defined here; they are deferred to the implementation section. No thresholds, metrics, or verifiable conditions are provided, making it a stub.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The paragraph contains no operative obligations; it merely references future implementation. No enforcement mechanism applies to this placeholder text. Only the generic misalignment backstop could theoretically apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Asset Liability Management Rental
assessments.description: Permits Prime Agents to trade Asset Liability Management obligations via a rental primitive to optimize collateral distribution.
assessments.quote: To allow the Asset Liability Management obligation of Prime Agents to be satisfied in the most efficient way possible, Prime Agents may enter into Asset Liability Management Rentals between each other, as specified in the Asset Liability Management Rental Primitive. This allows one Prime Agent to hold a greater amount of Actively Stabilizing Collateral to offset another Prime Agent holding a lesser amount. Thus, the overall level of Actively Stabilizing Collateral is unaffected but the Actively Stabilizing Collateral can be held by a Prime Agent that is able to more efficiently hold it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph merely permits Prime Agents to enter into Asset Liability Management Rentals, referencing an external primitive for specification. It contains no numeric thresholds, formulas, deadlines, or verifiable obligations; compliance is not checkable from this text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is a permissive statement, not an obligation; there is no violation mode to enforce. No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule, and the generic misalignment backstop alone is weak.

assessments.title: All Asset Liability Management Obligations Are Rented Together
assessments.description: Mandates that all asset liability management obligations must be transferred as a single package when rented.
assessments.quote: When Asset Liability Management obligations are rented, the associated obligations with regard to Actively Stabilizing Collateral, Demand Absorption Buffer, and Peg Defense Events are all transferred together.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a qualitative obligation: when ALM obligations are rented, the associated obligations (ASC, DAB, Peg Defense Events) must be transferred together. No metrics, thresholds, formulas, deadlines, or verifiable conditions are provided; compliance is a binary judgment but lacks quantified criteria.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) includes periodic reviews of Agent artifacts for Atlas compliance and can lead to penalty assessment. This plausibly reaches a violation of the bundling rule, though the penalty is unquantified for this specific rule.

assessments.title: Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to maintain at least 5% of their collateral portfolio in Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.quote: Prime Agents must maintain at least 5% of their Collateral Portfolio in Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a numeric threshold (5%), a defined actor (Prime Agents), and a verifiable metric (Collateral Portfolio share in Actively Stabilizing Collateral). A third party could check compliance from the text alone.
metrics: at least 5% of their Collateral Portfolio in Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) plausibly reach a violation, but no consequence is quantified for this specific rule, making enforcement mid.

assessments.title: Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.description: Requires Actively Stabilizing Collateral to provide buy support at a minimum price of 0.999 USD per USDS.
assessments.quote: Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must provide buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS (10bps downside spread). Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral includes Cash Stablecoins in PSMs or decentralized exchanges (e.g., Curve), other stablecoins, crypto assets, or off-chain Real World Asset (RWA) loans to market makers, provided they meet the specified redemption price and transparency requirements.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a fully quantified numeric threshold: buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS. A third party could verify compliance by checking the market or PSM price. The definition of eligible collateral types is enumerated, though the referenced 'specified redemption price and transparency requirements' are not defined here, the core obligation is objectively verifiable.
metrics: buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Failure to meet this definition means the collateral does not qualify as Actively Stabilizing Collateral, which could cause a Prime to breach the Minimum ASC requirement (A.3.3.2.2). That breach is subject to Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) and Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12). No direct on-chain automatic penalty exists for this definitional rule alone.

assessments.title: Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations
assessments.description: Defines the specific components used to calculate Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule provides a fully quantified formula: Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral is the sum of specific, verifiable on-chain components (USDC in named pools, Cash Stablecoins in specific DEX pairs). A third party could compute the value from the text alone.
metrics: USDC in the PSM3 on Base, Arbitrum, Unichain, Optimism
Cash Stablecoins in Curve (paired with USDS)
Cash Stablecoins in Uniswap (paired with USDS)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is a definitional calculation, not an obligation; no enforcement mechanism applies to a formula. Only the generic misalignment backstop could be invoked, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.description: Defines requirements for assets to qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.quote:
Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral consists of Cash Stablecoins that do not qualify as Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral but can be converted to Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may include Cash Stablecoins deposited into lending protocols, Cash Stablecoins used to provide liquidity to decentralized exchanges, or liquid staking derivatives of cash stablecoins.

Assets must satisfy the following requirements to qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral:

1. The assets must be verifiable onchain or through reputable APIs or oracles;
2. The assets must be able to be converted into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral within 15 minutes under normal market conditions; and
3. The process to convert the assets into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must be fully automated and triggered automatically when ASC falls below specified levels.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a concrete time limit (15 minutes) and requires automation, but the trigger levels for conversion are delegated to 'specified levels' elsewhere, and the verifiability requirement is qualitative ('reputable APIs or oracles'). The obligation is clear but the operative magnitude for the trigger is missing.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Misclassification of assets as Latent ASC would be detected during Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7) and could lead to penalties under the Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12), but no specific consequence is quantified for this eligibility rule alone.

assessments.title: Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations
assessments.description: Defines Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral components and allows agents to limit exposure to specific protocols or pools.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a fully quantified and objectively verifiable formula: Latent ASC is the sum of Cash Stablecoins in six explicitly named protocols/pools. A third party could check compliance from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The calculation is used to determine compliance with the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement (A.3.3.2.2), which is subject to artifact review (d4bf73e7) and penalty mechanisms (b8ee2d12). Incorrect calculation could lead to a violation of that requirement, triggering those enforcement paths.

assessments.title: Maximum Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.description: Limits latent actively stabilizing collateral to a maximum of 25% of total actively stabilizing collateral.
assessments.quote: Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may not exceed 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a clear numeric threshold (25%) and a verifiable ratio (Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral / Actively Stabilizing Collateral). A third party could check compliance from the text alone.
metrics: Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may not exceed 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is a Prime-level collateral composition limit. Violation can be detected through artifact review (d4bf73e7) and penalized via the penalty mechanisms (b8ee2d12), but no quantified consequence is specified for this specific rule, making enforcement mid.

assessments.title: Penalties For Failing To Satisfy Actively Stabilizing Collateral Requirement
assessments.description: Defines the current absence of penalties for failing to maintain Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirements.
assessments.quote: In the near term there will be no penalties for Prime Agents for failing to maintain the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Instead, failures to maintain the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral will be detected and reported as specified in [A.3.3.2.2.2.1 - Reporting Of Failures To Satisfy Actively Stabilizing Collateral Requirement](b74ba49a-de9e-4c4c-866c-b04d9dd208f7).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states that there are no penalties and that failures will be detected and reported, but provides no quantitative thresholds, metrics, or deadlines. It is a qualitative obligation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule explicitly disclaims penalties and only provides for detection and reporting. No specific enforcement mechanism is cited; only the generic misalignment backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Reporting Of Failures To Satisfy Actively Stabilizing Collateral Requirement
assessments.description: Mandates automatic detection and 24-hour reporting of collateral requirement violations to specific stakeholders.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a concrete obligation (develop an automatic detection tool) with a timing requirement (24 hours), and enumerates the exact reporting parties. However, it lacks a quantified metric for 'failures' or 'violation' beyond a cross-reference, contains the qualitative qualifier 'near term' which weakens immediate verifiability, and delegates action to a specific role rather than establishing a direct, self-executing standard.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited for a failure to develop the detection tool or report violations. Only the generic misalignment backstop could apply, which is insufficient; no on-chain, capital-at-risk, explicit penalty, or named enforcer path exists for this particular duty.

assessments.title: Near Term Exemption For Keel
assessments.description: Grants Keel a temporary exemption from Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirements due to infrastructure limitations.
assessments.quote: In the near term, due to limitations in the infrastructure on Solana, Keel is exempt from the requirement to maintain the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral. This exemption will be removed in a future iteration of the Asset Liability Management Framework.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule clearly exempts Keel from the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement, but the duration is qualitative ('near term', 'future iteration') with no quantified deadline or metric.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is an exemption, so no violation can occur; no enforcement mechanism is needed or provided. The catch-all misalignment process would be the only backstop, which is weak.

assessments.title: Calculation
assessments.description: Defines the per-block formula for calculating the Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive.
assessments.quote:
The Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive is calculated on a per block basis as follows:

`Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive = Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral * (Base Rate - SOFR)`

The parameters of this formula are defined in [A.3.3.2.2.4.1.1 - Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral](e0b95f42-2021-44ab-a979-491a113ccbc1), and SOFR is specified in [A.3.3.2.2.4.1.3 - Secured Overnight Financing Rate](2edd1333-6ca6-4c10-9d71-80b85d4a4265).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states an exact per-block formula with defined inputs for Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral and SOFR referenced to specific paragraphs, but the parameter values themselves are defined elsewhere and Base Rate is not explicitly sourced in this text.
metrics: Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive = Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral * (Base Rate - SOFR)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No citable enforcement mechanism reaches this calculation rule; the paragraph only defines a formula and references parameter definitions. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral
assessments.description: Defines the calculation for Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral based on Prime Agent holdings and minimum requirements.
assessments.quote: The Eligible Actively Stabilizing Collateral is the lesser of (1) the Prime Agent’s Actively Stabilizing Collateral and (2) the Prime Agent’s Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral specified in [A.3.3.2.2 - Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral](475fe222-9e4a-4e9d-9be6-a7a424ce02f8).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a precise formula (lesser of two quantities) but the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral value is defined in another section, so a third party cannot verify the result from this text alone without cross-referencing.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: This is a definitional rule with no direct compliance obligation; no enforcement mechanism applies to a calculation formula. Only the generic misalignment backstop could theoretically reach it, which is weak.

assessments.title: Payment
assessments.description: Defines the monthly payment frequency for the Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive.
assessments.quote: The Actively Stabilizing Collateral Incentive is paid on a monthly basis as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a monthly payment frequency, which is a quantifiable cadence, but it does not name the actor responsible for making the payment, leaving a minor gap in verifiability.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism is specified or implicitly reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Minimum Demand Absorption Buffer
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to maintain a Demand Absorption Buffer of 25% of required Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.quote: Every Prime Agent must maintain a Demand Absorption Buffer equal to 25% of their required Actively Stabilizing Collateral.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a numeric threshold (25% of required Actively Stabilizing Collateral) for a named actor (Prime Agent), making compliance objectively verifiable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Artifact review (d4bf73e7) can detect buffer shortfalls, and penalty mechanisms (b8ee2d12) can impose financial penalties, but no specific consequence is quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Demand Absorption Buffer
assessments.description: Requires Prime Agents to maintain a USDS or DAI buffer for sale at a maximum price of 1.001.
assessments.quote: To further stabilize USDS during periods of excess supply, Prime Agents must maintain a Demand Absorption Buffer (DAB), a subset of ASC consisting of USDS that is for sale for at most 1.001 USD per USDS. The Demand Absorption Buffer includes USDS or DAI in PSMs. The Demand Absorption Buffer can also be fulfilled by autonomous systems that generate USDS dynamically through the allocation as needed.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a concrete obligation (maintain a DAB) and a numeric price cap (1.001 USD per USDS), but the required size of the buffer is not quantified, leaving the core magnitude qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or implicitly reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Penalties For Failing To Satisfy Demand Absorption Buffer Requirement
assessments.description: Specifies that penalties for failing to maintain the Minimum Demand Absorption Buffer will be defined in future iterations.
assessments.quote: Penalties for failing to maintain the Minimum Demand Absorption Buffer will be specified in a future iteration of the Asset Liability Management framework.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a stub that explicitly defers specification of penalties to a future iteration; it contains no operative obligation, threshold, metric, or verifiable condition.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No rule exists to enforce; the paragraph merely states that penalties will be defined later, so no enforcement mechanism applies.

assessments.title: Peg Defense Event Alert Tool
assessments.description: Mandates the development of a real-time DEX price calculation and notification tool for Peg Defense Events.
assessments.quote: The Core Council Risk Advisor, in consultation with Core GovOps, will develop a tool that calculates the average price of USDS on DEXes that are connected via LayerZero in real time. This tool must be made available to all Prime Agents and functionality must be developed that notifies Sky and Prime Agents in real time when a Peg Defense Event has been triggered.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule mandates development of a tool with described functionality (real-time price calculation, notification) but provides no quantified thresholds, deadlines, performance metrics, or verifiable criteria. Compliance is arguable on the same facts (e.g., what constitutes 'real time' is undefined).
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this development obligation. The Core Council Risk Advisor is not subject to artifact review, penalty mechanisms, or capital-at-risk rules. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is weak.

assessments.title: Peg Defense Obligations
assessments.description: Mandates Prime Agents to purchase USDS at specific intervals during a Peg Defense Event.
assessments.quote: In a Peg Defense Event, all Prime Agents must immediately begin to buy USDS at a rate of at least 6.25% of their Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement every six (6) hours. The six (6) hour periods run consecutively from the onset of the Peg Defense Event, and the Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement is measured as of the start of each period. Each Prime Agent is responsible for monitoring its Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement and maintaining sufficient capacity to satisfy this obligation for the duration of the Peg Defense Event.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names all Prime Agents and specifies a numeric purchase obligation: at least 6.25% of their Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement every six hours, with periods measured consecutively from Peg Defense Event onset and the requirement measured as of each period start. Remaining terms such as Peg Defense Event and ASC requirement are defined elsewhere but do not undermine verifiability.
metrics: at least 6.25% of their Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement every six (6) hours
six (6) hour periods run consecutively from the onset of the Peg Defense Event
Actively Stabilizing Collateral requirement is measured as of the start of each period
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Agent Artifact Review by Core GovOps (d4bf73e7) plausibly reach a Prime Agent's failure to execute the required USDS purchases, but no quantified penalty or automatic enforcement is specified for this specific peg-defense obligation.

assessments.title: Alternatives For Satisfying Peg Defense Obligations
assessments.description: Defines methods for performing peg defense using collateral sales or USDS-backed borrowing.
assessments.quote: Peg Defense can be performed through a combination of (1) selling other types of collateral for USDS, or (2) by using USDS, or generating new USDS via the Allocation System, that is then used as collateral to borrow other types of assets (e.g. USDC or USDT on Aave) and buy USDS with it.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes permissible methods for peg defense without any quantified thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or defined actors. It is purely qualitative and imposes no verifiable obligation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism is applicable because the rule is permissive and imposes no requirement; only the generic misalignment backstop could theoretically apply, but that is always weak and there is no obligation to enforce.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph is a cross-reference to another document and contains no operative requirements, thresholds, or verifiable conditions. It is a stub with nothing to comply with.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states an obligation for Sky Core to allocate capital to the Lite PSM, but provides no metrics, thresholds, formulas, or verifiable conditions; it is purely qualitative.

assessments.title: Lite Peg Stability Module
assessments.description: Defines the transition of Lite PSM control from Sky Core to Grove.
assessments.quote: Control of the Lite PSM is being transitioned to Grove. Until this transition is complete, the Lite PSM continues to be controlled by Sky Core, subject to the requirements specified in [A.3.3.2.6 - Sky Core Asset Liability Management Rules](8135523a-dd5f-482d-b522-ec4227746eaf). Post-transition, Grove will manage the Lite PSM as an ASC asset pursuant to the rules defined in this Article.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a transition of control and references external requirements, but provides no metrics, thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable conditions; it is purely qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism is specified or implied for this transitional statement; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Lite Peg Stability Module Parameter Values
assessments.description: Defines specific parameter values for the Lite Peg Stability Module and DC-IAM mechanisms.
assessments.quote:
The current values of the Lite Peg Stability Module parameters are:

- `tin`: 0%
- `tout`: 0%
- DC-IAM `line`: 10,000,000,000 DAI
- DC-IAM `gap`: 800,000,000 DAI
- DC-IAM `ttl`: 43,200 seconds
- `buf`: 800,000,000 DAI
- Authorized Parties: None
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule lists exact numeric parameter values (percentages, DAI amounts, seconds) and a defined actor state ('Authorized Parties: None'). All values are fully quantified and objectively verifiable from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Lite PSM parameters are enforced on-chain by the Peg Stability Module contract; the fixed-rate swap mechanism and debt ceiling parameters are self-executing, making violation impossible without a governance change.

assessments.title: Lite Peg Stability Module Parameter Modification
assessments.description: Defines the process for recommending and voting on Lite Peg Stability Module parameter changes.
assessments.quote: The Core Facilitator, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, may recommend changes to any of the parameters specified in the subdocuments of [A.3.3.2.7.1.1.1 - Lite Peg Stability Module Parameter Definitions](9196786a-18b6-4dea-b4e2-852090371dd7). These changes will be subject to an Executive Vote through the Operational Weekly Governance Cycle.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a permissive process (who may recommend parameter changes and the governance vote) but imposes no measurable obligation, threshold, or deadline. It is purely qualitative and lacks any verifiable compliance criteria.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak. The rule is permissive, so violation is unlikely and no consequence is defined.

assessments.title: Andromeda
assessments.description: Regulates the transition of Andromeda RWA management from Sky Core to Grove and its subsequent collateral management.
assessments.quote: Historically, Andromeda balanced Sky Core’s Cash Stablecoin liquidity by allocating excess into low-risk treasury strategies and replenishing shortages. Control of the Andromeda RWA Arranged Structure is currently being transitioned to Grove. Until the transition to Grove is complete, Andromeda continues to be controlled by Sky Core, subject to the requirements defined in [A.3.3.2.6 - Sky Core Asset Liability Management Rules](8135523a-dd5f-482d-b522-ec4227746eaf). Post-transition, Grove will manage Andromeda as a non-ASC asset within its Collateral Portfolio, subject to JRC requirements. Andromeda is not currently operational and its debt ceiling has been reduced to zero.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph describes a transition and references external rules (A.3.3.2.6 and JRC requirements) but imposes no new quantifiable thresholds, metrics, or deadlines. It states a current state (debt ceiling zero) but provides no verifiable compliance obligation beyond cross-references.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is attached to this paragraph; it merely points to other rules that have their own enforcement. Only the generic misalignment backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Other RWA Offboarding
assessments.description: Mandates winding down legacy RWA exposure and allows direct Executive Votes for offboarding processes.
assessments.quote: Other than Andromeda, all old RWA exposure that was added before Endgame must stay for as long as necessary, and optimized for yield if possible. When it is possible, the Core Facilitator should take action to wind down and offboard all such Legacy RWA. Governance actions related to optimizations, wind down and offboardings can be done directly in Executive Votes with no prior Governance Poll needed.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes a qualitative obligation to wind down legacy RWA 'when it is possible' and optimize yield 'if possible', with no thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or verifiable conditions; compliance is entirely judgment-based.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Agent Owner For Arranged Structures
assessments.description: Requires Arranged Structures to have an Agent owner to manage instructions and access.
assessments.quote: Arranged Structures must have an Agent owner. The Agent owner assigns instructions to the Arranged Structure on behalf of Sky, and determines if and how other Agents can access the Conduit of the Arranged Structure.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a concrete obligation ('must have an Agent owner') and defines the owner's role, but provides no quantifiable metric, threshold, deadline, or verification cadence. Compliance is binary but not numerically specified.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is attached to this rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is weak. No on-chain automatic enforcement, capital-at-risk incentive, or named penalty path reaches this requirement.

assessments.title: Arrangers
assessments.description: Requires every Arranged Structure to have a designated Arranger responsible for ongoing reporting.
assessments.quote: This Section defines procedures related to Arrangers, Ecosystem Actors that assist in the design and operation of Arranged Structures. Every Arranged Structure must have a designated Arranger responsible for conducting ongoing reporting. All aspects of this relationship, including the Arranger's duties, must be defined in this Section.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states that every Arranged Structure must have a designated Arranger responsible for ongoing reporting, but all aspects of the relationship and duties 'must be defined in this Section' — they are not yet defined. The obligation is a stub with no concrete metrics, thresholds, or verifiable conditions.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is mentioned or implicitly reaches this rule. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstops (c6c6f595, 560e1024) could apply, which are always weak.

assessments.title: Introduction
assessments.description: Requires Arrangers to be SKY voter approved and prohibits them from influencing asset operations after allocation.
assessments.quote:
Arrangers are Ecosystem Actors who specialize in sourcing, negotiating, structuring, and reporting on Real World Assets, as well as maintaining and monitoring the underlying Arranged Structures used by the Sky Protocol. The Arrangers manage a restricted function on the Arranged Structure Conduit that allows them to send assets onwards to the predetermined blockchain account of the Arranged Structure.

Arrangers are generally prohibited from occupying any position where they could cause damage or loss to the Sky Ecoystem, notwithstanding delays or inconveniences.

After the Arranged Structures are established and assets are allocated, Arrangers must not have the capability to operate or influence the legal and operational structure’s asset operations in any manner that could cause significant harm or losses to the stability of USDS.

Arrangers are directly approved by SKY voters, and all LRA collateral exposure must be structured by an approved Arranger.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule contains a concrete, verifiable requirement ('all LRA collateral exposure must be structured by an approved Arranger') but the other prohibitions rely on qualitative judgments ('could cause damage or loss', 'significant harm or losses') with no numeric thresholds, metrics, or deadlines. The approval process is delegated to SKY voters without stated criteria.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Agent Artifact Review process (d4bf73e7) plausibly reaches Arranger compliance with these prohibitions and the approval requirement, providing a scheduled review and penalty assessment path, though consequences are unquantified for this specific rule.

assessments.title: Onboarding And Offboarding of Arrangers
assessments.description: The Core Facilitator may initiate governance polls to onboard or offboard Arrangers.
assessments.quote: When they deem it necessary, the Core Facilitator may initiate a Governance Poll to onboard or offboard Arrangers. The list of current active Arrangers is maintained in [A.3.4.3.2.1 - List Of Active Arrangers](b8791aaa-84b7-4012-8a4f-053595ec232a).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule grants the Core Facilitator discretion to initiate a Governance Poll 'when they deem it necessary,' with no criteria, thresholds, or verifiable conditions. It is a real process but entirely qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is permissive and imposes no mandatory obligation; no specific enforcement mechanism is defined. Only the generic misalignment backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Reporting And Stress Test Requirements
assessments.description: Requires Arrangers to provide monthly reports and semi-annual stress tests for arranged structures.
assessments.quote:
Arrangers must publish monthly reporting on each Arranged Structure they have arranged.

Every six (6) months, Arrangers are also required to publish a stress test analysis that demonstrates how the structures would perform under historical financial crisis scenarios and other hypothetical scenarios.

The Core Facilitator must periodically fund independent Ecosystem Actors to review and verify the quality and the results of the stress tests. Should an independent review produce an unfavorable result, the Core Facilitator must propose a Governance Poll for warning, temporarily deactivating, or permanently offboarding the Arranger and/or the Asset Managers connected to the discovered issue.

To be considered compliant, Arrangers’ monthly reports must satisfy the requirements of one of the following documents:

- [A.3.4.3.3.1 - Monthly Arranger Report Requirements](7b902bb1-68b4-477d-a575-29aaa02e9e7b)
- [A.3.4.3.3.2 - Access To Accounts](47eedd39-5bb9-492f-a4aa-9405bb5d196f)
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies monthly reporting and semi-annual stress tests with clear cadences, and defines compliance by reference to specific documents. The stress test scenarios are described qualitatively ('historical financial crisis scenarios and other hypothetical scenarios'), leaving some judgment, but the core obligations are quantified.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule mandates independent review of stress tests, and if unfavorable, the Core Facilitator must propose a Governance Poll for offboarding. This is a specific consequence path with a named enforcer and concrete remedies, consistent with the artifact review and penalty assessment mechanism (A.1.14.2.10).

assessments.title: Monthly Arranger Report Requirements
assessments.description: Mandates specific data points and verification steps for monthly Arranger reports regarding RWA holdings and cash flows.
assessments.quote:
The following information must be included in the monthly Arranger report. Each item must be reported for at least the start and end date of the reporting period. If these dates fall on days when markets are closed, the first business day after the start date and the last business day before the end date may be used instead.

- Cash balance.
- Cash income over the reporting period. Any income over $20,000 in value should be broken out as its own line item, and an explanation provided for any non-recurring or non-ordinary expenses.
- Cash expenses over the reporting period. Any expense over $20,000 in value should be broken out as its own line item, and an explanation provided for any non-recurring or non-ordinary expenses.
- Market value of publicly traded equities, ETFs, and mutual funds.
- Market value (the closing price) of publicly traded debt securities. Debt securities that are investment grade and less than 12 months from maturity may alternatively be reported at cost basis + linearly recognizing scheduled interest income.
- A valuation for illiquid or privately traded assets. This should utilize a valuation from a reputable third party with relevant expertise or follow a well-defined methodology that is explained in detail in the report.
- CUSIPs, date of purchase, date of maturity, coupon, cost basis, and face value of all publicly traded debt securities in the portfolio for the last day of the reporting period.
- USDS inflows from the Sky Protocol during the reporting period.
- Total repayments on-chain to the Sky Protocol either to a vault or for surplus. If repayments are derived from multiple sources, they should be broken out into line items for each source.
- Vault debt to the Sky Protocol.
- Copies of original statements for all bank, brokerage, exchange, custodial, or other accounts. The Arranger may redact the names for non-Arranger service providers if and only if that is a requirement of confidentiality agreements with the non-Arranger service providers.

The Core Facilitator must publicly confirm on the Sky Forum that they have reviewed the original account documentation and verified that it supports the Arranger’s summary.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a monthly cadence, a $20,000 threshold for income/expense breakdown, exact data points, and a verification step by the Core Facilitator. However, the valuation of illiquid assets relies on qualitative criteria ('reputable third party', 'well-defined methodology'), leaving a minor gap in full objectivity.
metrics: start and end date of the reporting period
first business day after the start date and the last business day before the end date
cost basis + linearly recognizing scheduled interest income
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Arranger's monthly report is an artifact subject to Core GovOps review (d4bf73e7), and non-compliance could trigger penalty mechanisms (b8ee2d12) for Primes/Operational Agents, though no specific consequence is quantified for this rule.

assessments.title: Access To Accounts
assessments.description: Allows Arrangers to meet reporting requirements via public read-only account access and dashboard availability.
assessments.quote:
As an alternative to the requirements set out in [A.3.4.3.3.1 - Monthly Arranger Report Requirements](7b902bb1-68b4-477d-a575-29aaa02e9e7b), the Arranger can provide the following information through public read-only access to all accounts:

- All asset balances
- All transaction amounts (non-Arranger service provider names may be redacted)
- Hold-to-maturity yields (for assets with maturity) or current yield (for assets with no maturity)

In addition, Makerburn.com ([https://makerburn.com/#/](https://makerburn.com/#/)), Daistats.com ([https://daistats.com/#/](https://daistats.com/#/)), or another dashboard must be publicly available to summarize USDS inflows and outflows from the Sky vault.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule lists specific information items (all asset balances, all transaction amounts, yields) and requires a specific dashboard, making compliance verifiable, but it does not specify a measurement cadence or numeric thresholds, leaving minor gaps.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Agent Artifact Review mechanism (d4bf73e7) provides scheduled review of agent compliance, which could detect failure to provide the required read-only access; however, no specific penalty is quantified for this rule, making enforcement mid-level.

assessments.title: Modification
assessments.description: Defines modification procedures and governance requirements for Smart Burn Engine parameters via Executive Vote or SBE-BEAM.
assessments.quote:
The Core Facilitator, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, can modify the `kbump` and `hop` parameters of the Smart Burn Engine. LSEV2-SKY-A-USDS rewardsDuration should always match the value of the `hop` parameter without requiring prior governance authorization. Changes to other parameters require a Governance Poll followed by an Executive Vote.

The Smart Burn Engine parameters must be updated as necessary to implement the allocation specified in [A.2.3.1.2.4 - Step 3: Smart Burn Engine](5ce73730-4d5d-479c-b01e-40e87f072121). Such updates can be executed either through an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll, or through the SBE-BEAM within its bounds.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The text names the actor (Core Facilitator with Core Council Risk Advisor) and parameters (`kbump`, `hop`, `LSEV2-SKY-A-USDS rewardsDuration`) and specifies routes and ordering (Operational Weekly Cycle Executive Vote without prior poll, SBE-BEAM within its bounds, Governance Poll then Executive Vote for other parameters). The `rewardsDuration` = `hop` relation is verifiable, but the SBE-BEAM bounds and Step 3 allocation are defined in referenced docs rather than stated here.

assessments.title: Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module
assessments.description: Defines parameter bounds and governance-whitelisted operator permissions for the Smart Burn Engine's accumulation rate.
assessments.quote:
The Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module (SBE-BEAM) enables a designated, Governance-whitelisted Operator to adjust the Kicker Lot Size (`kbump`), the SKY Accumulation Percentage (`burn`), and the Splitter Interval (`hop`) parameters of the Smart Burn Engine, as specified in [A.3.5.2.2.1.2 - Kicker Lot Size Parameter](fc9cece1-84bf-4133-a2ef-ef2182a23a35), [A.3.5.2.1.1.2 - SKY Accumulation Percentage Parameter](e16d6215-c2f1-4140-affd-30e52a17fd43), and [A.3.5.2.1.1.1 - Splitter Interval Parameter](39a67e65-33f0-4f2c-917d-efff544cf5ab). Adjustments are governed by the SBE-BEAM smart contract logic and specific parameters set by Sky Governance.

The SBE-BEAM Operator can raise or lower these parameters freely within the bounds set by Sky Governance. Those bounds are one-sided guardrails on the rate of accumulation: the Kicker Lot Size cannot be set above `maxKbump`, the Splitter Interval cannot be set below `minHop`, and the combined throughput, expressed as the Kicker Lot Size divided by the Splitter Interval, cannot exceed `maxRate`. The rate of accumulation therefore cannot be raised beyond the maximum that Sky Governance has sanctioned, while no corresponding bound limits reductions to it. The SKY Accumulation Percentage (`burn`) can be set to any value between 0% and 100%. The `tau` parameter separately requires a minimum interval between operations, applying to any operation regardless of whether it raises or lowers the parameters. The SBE-BEAM holds the following bounding parameters: (i) `maxKbump`, (ii) `minHop`, (iii) `maxRate`, and (iv) `tau`.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule fully quantifies the operator's permissions with named parameters (`maxKbump`, `minHop`, `maxRate`, `tau`) and explicit bounds (e.g., 'cannot be set above', 'cannot be set below', 'any value between 0% and 100%'). A third party could verify compliance from the text alone, assuming the specific numeric values for the bounding parameters are set by governance.
metrics: Kicker Lot Size cannot be set above `maxKbump`
Splitter Interval cannot be set below `minHop`
combined throughput (Kicker Lot Size / Splitter Interval) cannot exceed `maxRate`
SKY Accumulation Percentage (`burn`) can be set to any value between 0% and 100%
`tau` parameter requires a minimum interval between operations
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule states adjustments are 'governed by the SBE-BEAM smart contract logic', making the parameter bounds on-chain and automatically enforced. A violation (e.g., setting a parameter outside its bound) is impossible by the contract's design. If a vulnerability were exploited, the Emergency Spells mechanism (b8266c11-3a84-4bbe-abe2-de9474f74ffd) provides a pre-authorized path to freeze or pause the module.

assessments.title: Max Kbump Definition

This is captured within the Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine mechanism.

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a clear actor (SBE-BEAM), a precise operation (set `hop`), and a mathematically verifiable boundary condition (`hop` >= `minHop`). Compliance is binary and objectively determinable from the operation parameters.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The SBE-BEAM is an on-chain contract module whose code must explicitly enforce the `hop` >= `minHop` constraint, making violation impossible at the protocol level. This is an implicit programmatic enforcement of the parameter boundary within the Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine system (`3eb6f099`).

assessments.title: Tau Definition
assessments.description: Defines a mandatory minimum time interval between consecutive Smart Burn Engine operations.
assessments.quote:
The `tau` parameter defines the minimum time interval, in seconds, that must elapse between consecutive uses or operations of the SBE-BEAM.

A SBE-BEAM operation may adjust one or more parameters. Once a SBE-BEAM operation is executed, the `tau` duration must expire before any subsequent SBE-BEAM operation can be performed. This interval applies to every operation regardless of whether it raises or lowers the affected parameters.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph names a concrete parameter (tau) and a clear operational rule (a minimum interval in seconds must elapse between SBE-BEAM operations), but it does not state the actual numeric tau value, so the operative magnitude is not verifiable from this text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The tau interval is an on-chain timelock on SBE-BEAM operations: the Smart Burn Engine bounded external access module makes a subsequent operation impossible until tau has elapsed, so violation is automatically prevented. This is part of the Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine mechanism (A.3.5, UUID 3eb6f099-2736-4f62-9cb8-096a8fcca757).

- The value of the `minHop` parameter is 550 seconds.
- The value of the `maxRate` parameter is 350,000,000 USDS per year.
- The value of the `tau` parameter is 1,800 seconds.

assessments.title: Technical Limitations
assessments.description: Enforces hard-coded parameter limits on the Smart Burn Engine to prevent protocol halts and precision errors.
assessments.quote:
The SBE-BEAM enforces technical limitations, including the following, that apply independently of the bounding parameters set by Sky Governance. An attempt to use the SBE-BEAM in a manner that exceeds these limitations will revert.

The `hop` parameter cannot be set higher than five (5) years. This limitation prevents the Smart Burn Engine from being placed in a state in which its reward stream — the staking rewards funded by the non-burned portion of surplus and streamed out over the Splitter Interval — can no longer be revived through the SBE-BEAM.

The `burn` parameter cannot be set higher than 100%, the point at which the entire surplus is directed to SKY accumulation. A higher value would cause the Smart Burn Engine to halt.

The `kbump` parameter must be set to a whole multiple of `RAY` (10²⁷). A value that is not an exact multiple of `RAY` will revert, ensuring the Kicker Lot Size is always expressed in the protocol's standard fixed-point precision.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states explicit numeric thresholds: hop ≤ 5 years, burn ≤ 100%, and kbump must be a multiple of 10^27. These are fully quantified and verifiable; a third party could check compliance from the text alone.
metrics: kbump must be a whole multiple of 10²⁷ (RAY)
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism from the catalog reaches this rule, and no UUID appears in the paragraph text. The on-chain revert is a technological constraint but not covered by any listed mechanism doc; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Operators
assessments.description: Defines parameter limits and governance controls for the Smart Burn Engine Bounded External Access Module operator.
assessments.quote: The SBE-BEAM Operator is a Governance-whitelisted entity that can use the SBE-BEAM to alter the three Smart Burn Engine parameters within its control — the Kicker Lot Size (`kbump`), the SKY Accumulation Percentage (`burn`), and the Splitter Interval (`hop`). Changes to the `kbump` and `hop` parameters, and to their combined throughput, are limited by the `maxKbump`, `minHop`, and `maxRate` parameters, and every change is subject to the `tau` cadence. The `burn` parameter is not subject to the `maxKbump`, `minHop`, or `maxRate` bounds, which limit only the rate of accumulation, and is constrained only by the technical maximum specified in [A.3.5.2.4.4 - Technical Limitations](42ea8a7b-fb28-455e-8038-5fcf25250f17). The Operator can be changed by an Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the SBE-BEAM Operator, the three controlled parameters (`kbump`, `burn`, `hop`), the bounding parameters (`maxKbump`, `minHop`, `maxRate`), and the `tau` cadence, but gives no numeric values or cadence length in this paragraph; those magnitudes are delegated elsewhere.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: On-chain automatic enforcement: the SBE-BEAM is a bounded external access module whose contract code enforces the maxKbump/minHop/maxRate limits and tau cadence, blocking out-of-bound or too-frequent changes; the technical limitations referenced in the paragraph (42ea8a7b) document those bounds.
