assessments.title: Agreement By Core Facilitator
assessments.description: Requires the Core Facilitator to post agreement to the Sky Forum before executing recommended changes.
assessments.quote: Before a recommended change is executed, the Core Facilitator must post to the Sky Forum to indicate its agreement with the recommendation.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a specific actor (Core Facilitator), action (post to the Sky Forum), and objective sequencing condition (before execution), so compliance is verifiable; however, the trigger 'recommended change' and execution are defined elsewhere and no numeric metric or cadence is stated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: None found. The paragraph only imposes an off-chain posting step and does not attach a penalty, on-chain check, or named enforcer to noncompliance; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, which alone is weak.

assessments.title: Execution By Operator
assessments.description: Defines the process for the Operator to prepare and execute changes via the SBE-BEAM.
assessments.quote: Once the Core Facilitator has agreed to a recommended change, the Operator prepares and executes the change through the SBE-BEAM. Preparation can include the creation of transaction simulations to verify inputs.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule identifies an actor (Operator) and a process step (prepare and execute a change), but the obligation is entirely qualitative. There are no metrics, thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable criteria for what constitutes adequate 'preparation' or a valid 'execution'.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or structurally implied for this procedural step. The Operator's compliance is self-enforced. Only the generic misalignment backstops (c6c6f595, 560e1024) could theoretically apply, which alone are always weak.

assessments.title: Public Communication
assessments.description: Requires the Operator to publicly communicate all SBE-BEAM executions via forum posts or informational dashboards.
assessments.quote: Once a change has been executed through the SBE-BEAM, the Operator must publicly communicate the execution to the Sky Ecosystem. This communication may take the form of either (1) a post to the Sky Forum or (2) the inclusion of the execution in an informational dashboard that allows community members to see each change executed through the SBE-BEAM.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the Operator, the trigger (after execution), and two specific communication methods, but provides no deadline, cadence, or quantitative metric, leaving timing and completeness unquantified.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this transparency rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is weak.

assessments.title: Target Aggregate Backstop Capital
assessments.description: Sets the target aggregate backstop capital at 1.5% of the total USDS supply.
assessments.quote: The Target Aggregate Backstop Capital is one and one half percent (1.5%) of the total supply of USDS.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a precise numeric target (1.5% of total USDS supply) but does not specify an actor, measurement cadence, or any obligation; it is a definitional parameter rather than an actionable requirement.
metrics: 1.5% of the total supply of USDS
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism is specified; the target is a parameter for the Surplus Buffer, but there is no consequence for failing to meet it. Only the generic misalignment backstop exists, which is weak.

assessments.title: Turbo-Fill Floor
assessments.description: Sets the 150 million USDS threshold for accelerated Aggregate Backstop Capital retention.
assessments.quote: The current Turbo-Fill Floor for the Aggregate Backstop Capital is 150 million USDS. The Turbo-Fill Floor is the level below which an accelerated retention rate applies, as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.3 - Step 2: Aggregate Backstop Capital](2b28d464-e683-48ba-9a66-2fee05ea0a88).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a specific numeric threshold (150 million USDS) and a clear condition (below this floor, accelerated retention applies). A third party can verify compliance from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Surplus Buffer and Smart Burn Engine (3eb6f099) is an on-chain automatic mechanism; the Turbo-Fill Floor parameter is enforced by the smart contract, which automatically applies the accelerated retention rate when the condition is met, making violation impossible.

assessments.title: Capital Retention To Achieve Target Aggregate Backstop Capital
assessments.description: Retains Step 2 Capital to increase Aggregate Backstop Capital when below target levels.
assessments.quote: When Aggregate Backstop Capital is below Target Aggregate Backstop Capital, a portion of Step 2 Capital is retained to grow Aggregate Backstop Capital, as specified in [A.2.3.1.2.3 - Step 2: Aggregate Backstop Capital](2b28d464-e683-48ba-9a66-2fee05ea0a88).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a condition (Aggregate Backstop Capital below target) but the action 'a portion of Step 2 Capital is retained' is qualitative with no specified portion, formula, or threshold. Compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific consequence or enforcement mechanism is stated or implied for failing to retain capital; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply.

assessments.title: SKY Backstop
assessments.description: Defines the automatic minting and selling of SKY to recapitalize the system during undercollateralization events.
assessments.quote: This Article governs the SKY Backstop. If the USDS Stablecoin becomes undercollateralized, the Sky Protocol will automatically generate and sell SKY to recapitalize the system. The period when the recapitalization mechanism is actively minting and selling SKY to close the shortfall is termed a "SKY Backstop Event."
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a condition ('undercollateralized') but provides no metric, threshold, or formula to determine when that condition is met. The obligation is qualitative, making compliance arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule itself is an on-chain automatic mechanism that mints and sells SKY to recapitalize the system when undercollateralized, making violation impossible and self-executing. This is strong enforcement.

assessments.title: Emission Rate
assessments.description: Requires the definition and continuous assessment of an emissions rate for the SKY backstop function.
assessments.quote: An emissions rate for the SKY backstop function that prevents risk of sudden failure must be defined. This must be continuously assessed and improved to maximize stability of the system in worst case scenarios.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires defining and continuously assessing an emissions rate, but provides no quantitative thresholds, formulas, metrics, or verifiable criteria; compliance is entirely qualitative and arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is weak.

assessments.title: Limitless
assessments.description: The SKY Backstop emission rate is currently set to be unlimited.
assessments.quote: The SKY Backstop is temporarily limitless.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule is a qualitative statement that the backstop is temporarily limitless, with no numeric threshold, deadline, or condition for when it ceases to be limitless. It imposes no verifiable obligation on any actor.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism applies; the rule is a descriptive parameter, not an obligation, and no consequence is defined for violation.

assessments.title: Maximum Level Of Emission
assessments.description: Requires defining and continuously assessing a maximum SKY emission limit per undercollateralization event.
assessments.quote: A maximum level of SKY emission per undercollateralization event must be defined. This must be continuously assessed and improved to maximize stability of the system in worst-case scenarios.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires defining a maximum emission level and continuously assessing it, but provides no numeric threshold, formula, or verifiable criteria. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism targets this rule; only the generic misalignment backstop (c6c6f595) could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Override Mechanism
assessments.description: Requires a governance override mechanism for SKY emissions and defines necessary research processes for its safe use.
assessments.quote: The Protocol must include an override mechanism that allows Sky Governance to continue emitting SKY beyond the maximum level. This Section must specify research processes and principles to guide when and how the override mechanism can be safely used.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states that the Protocol must include an override mechanism and that the Section must specify research processes and principles, but it provides no concrete thresholds, metrics, deadlines, or verifiable conditions. It is a directive to create something, not a rule with measurable compliance criteria — effectively a stub.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule. The SKY Backstop mechanism (4d8b0d82) is about the backstop's economic function, not about enforcing the requirement to include an override. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is weak.

assessments.title: Halt Mechanism
assessments.description: Requires a mechanism to immediately halt the SKY backstop during severe risk of total failure.
assessments.quote: The Protocol must contain a SKY backstop halt mechanism that immediately halts the backstop event in case of severe risk of total failure.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule requires a halt mechanism for 'severe risk of total failure' but provides no quantitative thresholds, metrics, or defined criteria for what constitutes such risk; compliance is entirely judgment-based.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or implied; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Mitigate Worst Case Scenario
assessments.description: Defines a haircut mechanism for USDS target price to settle bad debt when backstops fail.
assessments.quote: In case the backstop limit is reached and not overridden, or in case the backstop is halted during the event, the USDS target price receives a haircut to settle the remaining bad debt of the system. This Section must define elements and infrastructure to address this worst-case scenario, including research concerning ways to mitigate damage.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph states that a haircut will occur under certain conditions but provides no quantitative parameters, thresholds, or defined actors. The second sentence is a directive to define elements in the future, making it a stub.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism is specified; the haircut is a system event, not a rule with consequences for non-compliance. Only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Relation To Genesis Capital Backstop
assessments.description: Requires the Genesis Capital Backstop to be applied before invoking the SKY Backstop.
assessments.quote: The SKY Backstop may not be invoked unless the Genesis Capital Backstop (see [A.3.7.1.6 - Genesis Capital Backstop](a9965d58-8cda-49fc-8a7f-f8cc2e0d6b98)) has been applied and USDS remains undercollateralized.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states two concrete conditions (Genesis Capital Backstop applied, USDS undercollateralized) that are objectively verifiable in principle, but the operative criteria for 'applied' and 'undercollateralized' are delegated to other sections without numeric thresholds or formulas in this paragraph.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is attached to this condition; violation would be prevented only by governance voting or the generic misalignment backstop, both of which are weak.

assessments.title: Native Vault Engine
assessments.description: Mandates limited collateral types and risk parameters for Core Vaults during the transition to SparkLend.
assessments.quote: The Sky Core Vaults are gradually being deprecated over time to incentivize users to migrate to SparkLend and other borrowing platforms offered by Prime Agents (see [A.3.7.1.1.2.3 - Stability Fee](0257a420-e92e-4942-b794-a559f299365f)). During the transition period, the Core Vaults will have a limited set of collateral types and risk parameters that Core GovOps, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, must implement according to the following subdocuments.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a concrete obligation (Core GovOps must implement a limited set of collateral types and risk parameters) and references subdocuments, but the actual parameters, thresholds, or deadlines are not stated in this text; they are delegated.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this directive; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Liquidation Ratio
assessments.description: Defines the minimum collateral ratio required to prevent vault liquidation and the process for changing it.
assessments.quote:
The Liquidation Ratio parameter limits the maximum amount of Dai debt that a vault user can draw from their vault given the value of their collateral locked in that vault. In practice, it expresses the minimum collateral in percentage terms that can support a given Dai debt. If the ratio of a Vault user's collateral to their debt drops below this value, their vault can be liquidated. Each vault type has its own Liquidation Ratio. The Liquidation Ratio for each vault type is expressed as a percentage value of the collateral that must be present in the vault to support its debt.

Changes to the Liquidation Ratio are subject to the Operational Weekly Cycle, requiring a Governance Poll followed by an Executive Vote.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines the Liquidation Ratio conceptually but provides no numeric threshold or specific value. It states that each vault type has its own ratio expressed as a percentage, but no actual percentages are given. Thus, it is qualitative and lacks verifiable criteria; a third party could not determine compliance from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The liquidation ratio is enforced by the on-chain liquidation mechanism: if a vault's collateral ratio falls below the set ratio, the vault is automatically liquidated, incurring a liquidation penalty (bce9331b). This is a strong, contract-enforced consequence.

assessments.title: Debt Ceiling Limit
assessments.description: Establishes a maximum debt ceiling and a rate-limiting module to mitigate rapid exposure increases.
assessments.quote:
The Debt Ceiling Limit is numerically provided and acts as an upper limit. Core GovOps, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, can propose changes within this limit.

Debt Ceiling Limit = Unlimited is defined as large enough to avoid being reached in the near future.

The DC-IAM methodology contained in [A.3.7.1.1.2.4 - Debt Ceiling Instant Access Module (DC-IAM)](93c9f662-4e0d-477e-8fc9-e3726877e842) acts as a risk mitigation tool. It limits the rate at which exposure can increase in a short period of time in the event of an unexpected emergency.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a debt ceiling exists and can be changed by Core GovOps, but provides no numeric threshold, formula, or verifiable condition; the Unlimited definition ('large enough to avoid being reached in the near future') is qualitative.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No catalogued mechanism or UUID in the paragraph directly reaches a violation of the absolute debt ceiling. On-chain enforcement of the ceiling is implicit but cannot be tied to any listed UUID, so it defaults to weak.

assessments.title: Stability Fee
assessments.description: Defines Stability Fee mechanics, surplus buffer transfers, and modification methods via governance or external modules.
assessments.quote:
The Stability Fee parameter is an annual percentage fee charged on the Dai generated on Vaults. It is expressed as an annual percentage yield but it is charged on a per-block basis in Dai. The Dai from this fee is minted, added to the Dai debt for the vault, and then transferred into the Surplus Buffer which is under the control of Sky Governance. Each vault type has its own Stability Fee that can be adjusted independently.

The Stability Fees can be modified through either Executive Votes or the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module. See [A.3.7.1.3 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module](47b8b035-8abd-42e6-86b8-33f852fa953a).

The Stability Fees must be gradually increased over time to incentivize users to migrate to SparkLend and other borrowing platforms offered by Prime Agents.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes an obligation to 'gradually increase' Stability Fees, but provides no numeric threshold, formula, cadence, or deadline; compliance is entirely judgment-based.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this rule; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies, which is weak.

assessments.title: Maximum Debt Ceiling (line)
assessments.description: Defines the mechanism and parameter for setting maximum debt ceilings via the DC-IAM.
assessments.quote:
The `line` parameter refers to the maximum value for the Debt Ceiling that the DC-IAM will allow in the given vault type. When using the DC-IAM to manage the Debt Ceiling of a vault type, the `line` parameter essentially replaces the Debt Ceiling parameter for that vault type. Rather than Sky Governance setting the Debt Ceiling directly, they will need to set the Maximum Debt Ceiling `line` in the DC-IAM. The `line` parameter is defined in Dai.

The Maximum Debt Ceiling is defined in [A.3.7.1.1.2.2 - Debt Ceiling Limit](b490d4d0-8eb8-4dc6-9ef3-c85d357f1f4b) and is currently unlimited.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines the `line` parameter and states that Sky Governance must set it, but provides no numeric threshold, formula, deadline, or verifiable condition. It is a qualitative description of a parameter's role, not a precise obligation.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The DC-IAM is an on-chain contract that automatically enforces the `line` as the maximum debt ceiling; violation (exceeding the line) is impossible because the contract code prevents it. The referenced section A.3.7.1.1.2.2 (UUID b490d4d0-8eb8-4dc6-9ef3-c85d357f1f4b) defines the debt ceiling limit and its on-chain enforcement.

assessments.title: Ceiling Increase Cooldown (ttl)
assessments.description: The ttl parameter limits the frequency of Debt Ceiling increases to control the rate of debt growth.
assessments.quote: The Ceiling Increase Cooldown (`ttl`) parameter controls how frequently the Debt Ceiling can be increased by the DC-IAM. If a user attempts to use the DC-IAM to increase the Debt Ceiling of a vault type before this time expires, the transaction will fail to execute and the Debt Ceiling will remain unchanged. The `ttl` parameter in combination with the `gap` parameter enforces a maximum rate at which debt usage can increase over time using a given vault type. These parameters should be set such that the maximum increase over time can accommodate all reasonable usage of the vault type in question. The `ttl` parameter is defined in seconds.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes the ttl parameter's function and states a qualitative guideline ('should be set such that the maximum increase over time can accommodate all reasonable usage'), but provides no numeric threshold, formula, or verifiable condition. Compliance is entirely judgment-based.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches the obligation to set the parameter appropriately. The on-chain cooldown enforces the parameter's effect, not the rule's qualitative requirement. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop applies.

assessments.title: Auction Parameters
assessments.description: Defines the approval process and emergency bypass authority for modifying auction risk parameters.
assessments.quote: A clear justification and analysis must be provided to validate any proposed changes to the parameters specified in this document. Before these changes are added to an Executive Vote, Core GovOps, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, must obtain approval through a Governance Poll. However, in an emergency, Core GovOps, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, has the authority to bypass the Governance Poll and add the proposed parameters directly to an Executive Vote. The parameters contained herein must be regularly monitored and updated if needed.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names specific actors (Core GovOps, Core Council Risk Advisor) and process steps (Governance Poll, Executive Vote) but leaves key operative conditions qualitative: 'clear justification', 'emergency', 'regularly monitored' without thresholds, cadence, or criteria.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific consequence is stated for violating the process; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak. No on-chain or institutional enforcement mechanism reaches this rule.

assessments.title: Auction Price Function (calc)
assessments.description: Defines the mathematical function and parameters used to determine collateral price decay during auctions.
assessments.quote:
The Auction Price Function is the mathematical function that determines how the collateral price changes over time during a collateral auction. Collateral auctions use a falling price auction, where the price starts high and decreases according to the function defined in this parameter.

The Exponential Stair Step function contains two key parameters, `cut` and `step`, defined in [A.3.7.1.1.2.5.1.1 - Auction Price Function (cut)](1ff3ceac-abd0-4195-9a60-a4aaf48c3d31) and [A.3.7.1.1.2.5.1.2 - Auction Price Function (step)](4b46633c-4d6c-4a9c-9be0-93d242ce9db9), respectively.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes the auction price function qualitatively, naming the Exponential Stair Step function and its two parameters, but provides no numeric thresholds, formulas, or exact parameter values; those are delegated to sub-paragraphs. A third party cannot verify compliance from this text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or implied; the rule is a definitional parameter with no actor obligation, so only the generic misalignment backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Auction Price Function (step)
assessments.description: Defines the time interval parameter for auction price adjustments during liquidation processes.
assessments.quote: The `step` parameter controls the length of time between price drops. A smaller step means a smoother line; a large one means more pronounced steps. The `step` parameter is defined in seconds.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph defines a parameter's role and unit but states no numeric threshold, formula, or compliance obligation; it is purely descriptive and imposes no verifiable requirement.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No obligation exists to enforce; no mechanism reaches this descriptive text.

assessments.title: Auction Price Multiplier (buf)
assessments.description: Defines the auction price multiplier parameter used to set starting prices for collateral liquidations.
assessments.quote: The `buf` parameter is a multiplier that is applied to the starting price of a collateral auction. Each vault type has its own Auction Price Multiplier that can be adjusted by Sky Governance separately. This multiplier is intended to be greater than 1.0x because Liquidations 2.0 uses falling price auctions. This means that it is generally preferable for the auction price to begin above the market price and then fall to the correct value over some amount of time. The `buf` parameter is defined as a multiplicative factor.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a parameter and states an intention (greater than 1.0x) but provides no numeric threshold, formula, or verifiable obligation. Compliance is arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is mentioned; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Max Auction Duration (tail)
assessments.description: Sets the maximum time allowed for a vault auction to settle before a mandatory reset occurs.
assessments.quote:
The Max Auction Duration parameter sets the maximum time that can elapse before an auction needs to reset for a particular vault type. Expressed in seconds, this parameter determines when an auction can no longer settle and must be reset.

The Max Auction Duration parameter overlaps with the Max Auction Drawdown parameter in that an auction will need to be reset once either maximum is exceeded.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph defines a parameter but provides no numeric threshold or specific value; it merely describes what the parameter does. No verifiable obligation exists.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific consequence or enforcement mechanism is attached to this definitional text; there is no rule to violate.

assessments.title: Proportional Kick Incentive (chip)
assessments.description: Defines the Dai reward percentage paid to keepers for triggering vault liquidation auctions.
assessments.quote: The Proportional Kick Incentive parameter represents a reward in Dai paid to the keepers that trigger collateral liquidation auctions in the Sky Protocol. The Proportional Kick Incentive is set as a percentage and represents a portion of Dai based on the debt of the vault that is being liquidated. The Dai is rewarded for each liquidation auction at the point the auction is triggered. Each vault type has its own Proportional Kick Incentive that may be adjusted separately by Sky Governance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines the Proportional Kick Incentive as a percentage of vault debt, but no specific percentage value is stated. It is a qualitative description of a parameter; a third party cannot verify compliance from this text alone because the actual magnitude is delegated to governance.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The incentive is paid automatically by the on-chain liquidation contract when a keeper triggers an auction, making the rule self-executing. The liquidation penalty mechanism (bce9331b) enforces liquidation-related parameters on-chain, including the kick incentive.

assessments.title: Flat Kick Incentive (tip)
assessments.description: Defines a fixed Dai reward for keepers triggering collateral liquidation auctions per vault type.
assessments.quote: The Flat Kick Incentive parameter represents a reward in Dai paid to the keepers that trigger collateral liquidation auctions in the Sky Protocol. The Flat Kick Incentive is a fixed amount of Dai that is rewarded for each liquidation auction at the point the auction is triggered. Each vault type has its own Flat Kick Incentive that may be adjusted separately by Sky Governance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The text defines a parameter but provides no numeric value, threshold, or formula; it merely states that a fixed amount exists and is set per vault type by governance. No compliance obligation is stated, so it's essentially a definition with no verifiable condition.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No rule to enforce; the parameter is descriptive. Only the generic misalignment backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Liquidation Penalty (chop)
assessments.description: Defines the liquidation penalty fee and the requirement for collateral auctions to cover debt and penalties.
assessments.quote: The Liquidation Penalty parameter controls the fee vault owners must pay when their position is liquidated due to insufficient collateral. For a vault holder to receive any collateral back from the liquidations process, the debt and Liquidation Penalty must be covered by the collateral auction. Each vault type has its own Liquidation Penalty that can be adjusted by Sky Governance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule describes the liquidation penalty parameter and its role, but provides no numeric threshold, formula, or specific value; it only states that a penalty exists and is adjustable by governance, making compliance unverifiable from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The liquidation penalty is enforced on-chain automatically by the smart contract when a vault is liquidated, as described in the Liquidation Penalty mechanism (bce9331b).

assessments.title: Local Liquidation Limit (hole)
assessments.description: Limits the maximum concurrent Dai debt auctions allowed for a specific vault type.
assessments.quote: The Local Liquidation Limit sets the maximum amount of Dai debt for which collateral auctions can be active at any one time within a particular vault type. When the total Dai value of auctions exceeds this maximum for a particular vault type, no more collateral can be auctioned using that vault type until others are completed. Each vault type has a separate Local Liquidation Limit.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names a concrete parameter (Local Liquidation Limit) and describes its effect (capping concurrent auctions, blocking new ones when exceeded), but the actual numeric threshold is not stated; it is delegated to per-vault-type setting. The operative magnitude is missing.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The limit is enforced automatically by on-chain smart contract logic, but no mechanism UUID in the provided catalog or in the paragraph text covers this specific on-chain enforcement. Without a citable mechanism, the rating defaults to weak.

assessments.title: Debt Floor (dust)
assessments.description: Sets minimum minting and repayment thresholds for individual vaults via the Debt Floor parameter.
assessments.quote: The Debt Floor parameter controls the minimum amount of Dai that can be minted using a specific vault type for an individual vault. If a user tries to mint Dai and the amount of Dai minted would not put the vault's amount of Dai minted above its Debt Floor, the transaction will fail and no DAi will be minted. Likewise, if a user attempts to pay back debt such that their debt will equal less than the Debt Floor and greater than zero, the transaction will fail and no Dai will be paid back. Each vault type has its own Debt Floor that can be adjusted by Sky Governance.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines the Debt Floor parameter and the exact condition for transaction failure (minting or repaying that would leave debt below the floor and above zero), but the actual numeric threshold is not stated; it is adjustable by governance. A third party cannot verify compliance without knowing the current parameter value.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is enforced automatically on-chain (transactions fail), but no mechanism UUID from the rubric's catalog or the paragraph text can be cited to support a strong rating; therefore enforcement is rated weak per rubric constraints.

assessments.title: Oracles
assessments.description: Mandates the use of Chronicle v3 oracles for specific collateral types until January 2026.
assessments.quote:
The Native Vault Engine collateral types of ETH, STETH, WBTC will specifically use the Chronicle v3 oracle solution, until at least January 1st 2026. The Native Vault Engine collateral types must be migrated to the new version of the Chronicle v3 oracle when it is feasible to do so.

Other oracle solutions, including diversified oracles, will only be considered until January 1st, 2026, and only if there are unresolvable security concerns with the Chronicle v3 oracles.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies exact collateral types (ETH, STETH, WBTC), a named oracle solution (Chronicle v3), and a clear deadline (until at least January 1st 2026). Compliance is objectively verifiable by checking the Native Vault Engine's oracle configuration on-chain.

assessments.title: Tau Definition
assessments.description: Enforces a minimum time interval between consecutive operations of the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module.
assessments.quote:

assessments.title: Legacy Context
assessments.description: Defines best-effort information dissemination procedures for upcoming collateral and vault type offboarding.
assessments.quote:
Periodically, collateral and vault types (ilks) are re-evaluated, which sometimes results in an offboarding of that collateral or vault type.

There have been several instances where users entered official Sky forums/chats to understand why they had been suddenly liquidated, despite historically comfortable collateralization ratios ([https://forum.skyeco.com/t/an-assessment-first-hand-experience-and-recommendations-from-the-aave-offboarding/11836](https://forum.skyeco.com/t/an-assessment-first-hand-experience-and-recommendations-from-the-aave-offboarding/11836)). This is, understandably, a poor user experience.

Even with liquidation penalties set to 0%, the forced unwinding of levered positions conceivably can result in user losses, as well as potentially taxable events.

This Section defines procedures concerning the dissemination of information about upcoming collateral offboarding on a best-effort basis. The objective is to minimize the number of users who are unaware of the offboarding prior to getting their positions liquidated.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a best-effort objective to disseminate information about offboarding, but provides no quantified metrics, thresholds, deadlines, or verifiable conditions; compliance is entirely qualitative and arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is cited or implied; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, which is weak.

assessments.description: Defines communication and bypass protocols for the collateral offboarding process.
assessments.quote:
Specific Goals:

1. Codify a series of good-faith communication efforts.
2. Provide an easy-to-follow process for Sky contributors to follow without significant burden.
3. Minimize the number of users unaware of a collateral offboarding.
4. Provide a method to bypass these requirements in the event a collateral is being offboarded due to serious security or solvency concerns.

assessments.title: Immediate Actions
assessments.description: Defines the technical process and communication requirements for offboarding collateral or vault types.
assessments.quote:
Upon approval by Sky Governance to offboard a permissionless collateral type or vault type, the following actions are taken as soon as is practicable:

- Set debt ceiling to zero (0) Dai or USDS.
- Make an initial public announcement on all communication channels listed in [A.3.7.1.5.3.0.6.1 - Communication Channels And Media Assets Listing](9ac8a70b-8b6a-4825-a5e0-5e9019e50bc4).
- Make a second public announcement on all communication channels in the above cited document no later than 14 calendar days after the initial public announcement.
- Once the second public announcements have been made, set the liquidation penalty to 0%.

However, the actor responsible is not defined, and the initial steps are qualified by 'as soon as is practicable', introducing minor ambiguity.

second public announcement no later than 14 calendar days after the initial public announcement

assessments.title: Communication Channels And Media Assets Listing
assessments.description: Defines the mandatory communication sequence and channels for notifying stakeholders of collateral offboarding processes.
assessments.quote:
The following channels should be used for initial and second public announcements of collateral offboarding. The order of announcement publication is as follows:

1. The author of the collateral offboarding notice shall post to the Sky Forum detailing the recommended offboarding. This forum thread is used to inform downstream announcements on other channels.
2. Core GovOps publishes the associated notices to:
    - All public Sky Calendars
    - The Sky Official Discord’s Announcement channel.
    - The official Sky subreddit.
3. Partner Relationship Leads from relevant Ecosystem Actors reach out to:
    - Affected collateral partners (e.g., Aave)
    - Affected frontend service providers (e.g., Oasis, DeFi Saver)

Additionally, outreach may be done to cover more channels not listed here. These may include other Ecosystem Actor or Facilitator owned Twitter accounts, communication channels, and platforms.

Unless otherwise noted in [A.3.7.1.5 - Offboarding Process](3da8a0fd-952c-4f80-b674-f60c9a293cb9) and its subdocuments, Core GovOps will take the lead in coordinating channels announcements.

assessments.title: Requirements
assessments.description: Defines requirements for expedited offboarding of collateral types that threaten protocol security or solvency.

When a collateral type threatens the security or solvency of the Sky Protocol, an expedited offboarding is in order. Expedited offboardings override the timeline specified in [A.3.7.1.5.2 - Technical Process](305e2bd6-a594-4aec-8713-adbe7bc87120) and allow the immediate modification of all relevant parameters.

Expedited offboardings must proceed pursuant to the following requirements:

- The Offboarding Proposal must state that the offboarding should be expedited due to an emergency or urgent concern, as defined in [A.1.9.1.1 - Definition Of Emergency Situations](5eafb29e-84a0-4a53-a798-3f958c880225)**.**
- The Offboarding Proposal must explicitly reference this Atlas document.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule imposes a real obligation (expedited offboarding when a collateral type threatens security or solvency) and lists procedural requirements for the proposal, but the trigger condition is entirely qualitative ('threatens the security or solvency') with no metric, threshold, or verifiable criteria. Compliance is arguable on the same facts.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is stated or implied. The rule only defines proposal content; failure to comply would at most lead to governance rejection, which is not a defined penalty path. Only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop could apply, which is weak.

These announcements must also state that the offboarding is being expedited and explain the reasons for this accelerated process.

The rule only requires announcements; failure to comply would at most fall under the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop, which is always weak. assessments.title: Genesis Capital Backstop
assessments.description: Defines a pro-rata haircut process for Genesis Agents to cover losses exceeding Prime Agent capital and buffers.
assessments.quote: If losses exceed a Prime Agent’s capital and cannot be absorbed by the Sky Surplus Buffer, the Sky Protocol must apply a pro‑rata haircut across each Genesis Agent’s Genesis Capital, implemented as a transfer of eligible assets from each Agent to the Sky Surplus Buffer. The haircut must be sized to cover the portion of the loss that exceeds what the Prime Agent’s capital and the Sky Surplus Buffer can absorb, up to a maximum of the Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a clear trigger (losses exceed Prime capital and buffer), a pro-rata haircut formula, a cap (Aggregate Backstop Capital), and an implementation (transfer of eligible assets). However, 'losses' and 'eligible assets' are not defined in this paragraph, leaving minor gaps in full verifiability.

The Surplus Buffer mechanism (3eb6f099) is the economic backstop that receives the assets, and the protocol's code enforces the transfer, making violation impossible.

A solution must be developed to allow these transfers to be accomplished on an automated basis without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay (see [A.1.10.3 - Governance Security Delay Requirements](c5f0e955-0441-42e0-a6fc-eab875bba568)).

assessments.title: Post Backstop Settlement
assessments.description: Defines the sequential activation of the SKY Backstop and USDS price adjustment to cover residual losses.
assessments.quote: If, after the haircut, losses still exceed the combined capacity of the Prime Agent’s capital and Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)), the SKY Backstop (see [A.3.6 - SKY Backstop](4d8b0d82-97da-4041-b185-4b98c2779cbe)) is activated. The SKY mint must be sized to cover the remaining loss. If losses still exceed what the SKY Backstop can absorb, Sky will adjust the USDS target price below $1 to the extent necessary to settle the remaining deficit; Sky will then distribute 24 billion SKY to USDS holders via an airdrop.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a clear sequence of conditions and actions with specific numeric thresholds and formulas: losses exceeding defined capacities trigger SKY mint sized to cover the remaining loss, then if losses still exceed SKY Backstop capacity, USDS target price is adjusted to cover the deficit, and a fixed 24 billion SKY airdrop occurs. All conditions are objectively verifiable given the referenced capacity definitions.
metrics: losses still exceed the combined capacity of the Prime Agent’s capital and Aggregate Backstop Capital

distribute 24 billion SKY to USDS holders via an airdrop

assessments.title: Genesis Capital

assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule provides a fully quantified formula: Genesis Capital = min(Eligible Genesis Capital, total capital), with Eligible Genesis Capital defined as contributed capital minus phased-out capital. Given the referenced input values, the calculation is objectively verifiable.

assessments.title: Genesis Capital Phase-Out

As the ecosystem matures and Aggregate Backstop Capital (see [A.3.5.3.1.2 - Aggregate Backstop Capital](6dbead44-5ac4-4c5b-be3c-64eddd004e5c)) reaches a sufficient level, Genesis Capital will phase out. The documents herein define the eligibility conditions and phase-out amounts.

Phase-out is effected by increasing an Agent's Phased-Out Genesis Capital (see [A.3.7.1.6.6.2.3 - Phased-Out Genesis Capital](8f813186-1317-41b1-86d1-47fce7f42af5)), which reduces the Agent's Eligible Genesis Capital and therefore its Genesis Capital, progressively reducing the Genesis Capital subject to the Genesis Capital Backstop (see [A.3.7.1.6 - Genesis Capital Backstop](a9965d58-8cda-49fc-8a7f-f8cc2e0d6b98)). Phase-out does not involve any repayment or transfer of capital from the Genesis Agents to Sky.

assessments.title: Usage Standards
assessments.description: Defines the authority and consultation process for the Freezer Multisig to freeze the Spark Liquidity Layer.
assessments.quote:
The signers of the Freezer Multisig should exercise their authority to freeze the Spark Liquidity Layer in the event that Spark is not complying with rules regarding Risk Capital or Asset Liability Management, or in the event of another emergency. The signers should consult with Operational GovOps Soter Labs before exercising such authority, unless such consultation would cause a delay that could result in a loss of user funds or harm to Sky or Spark. Operational GovOps Soter Labs may also ask the signers to exercise the Freezer Multisig in an emergency. The signers will work with Operational GovOps Soter Labs and, if necessary, other Ecosystem Actors, in good faith in determining whether to exercise their authority based on such request.

Each action executed by the Freezer Multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines an actor (Freezer Multisig signers) and a process (consultation, reporting) but the triggers are qualitative ('not complying with rules', 'another emergency', 'reasonable time frame') with no numeric thresholds or verifiable criteria, making compliance arguable.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is attached to the signers' exercise of authority; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak. No on-chain automatic enforcement, capital at risk, or named penalty path reaches this rule.

assessments.title: Modification
assessments.description: Defines governance procedures and emergency response for modifying Freezer Multisig signers.
assessments.quote:
Modification of the signers of the Freezer Multisig must be approved through a Governance Poll; no Executive Vote is required.

The only exceptions to this are if: 1) a signer self-reports a loss of access to their private key due to any reason; or 2) a signer explicitly expresses their wish to be removed as a signer. In both cases, the signer is required to communicate the loss of access to their private key, or the wish to be removed as a signer, in the form of a public Sky Forum post. The specific signer should be replaced as soon as possible, which does not require a Governance Poll.

Any changes to the multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious. Where malicious activity is suspected, the Core Facilitator must prepare an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the multisig.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies concrete steps: Governance Poll for modifications, exceptions for self-reported key loss or removal wish via public forum post, and an expedited Executive Vote for unauthorized changes. However, no numeric thresholds or deadlines are provided; 'as soon as possible' is qualitative, making the timing ambiguous.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule directly defines a consequence for violation: unauthorized signer changes are treated as malicious, and the Core Facilitator must prepare an expedited Executive Vote to remove external security access. This is a specific, defined escalation path with a named enforcer and concrete remedy, aligning with the Emergency Response System (1d940c6d).

assessments.title: Approve PSM Spend
assessments.description: Requires operator approval for the PSM to spend DAI for USDC swaps.
assessments.quote:
The operator must approve the PSM to spend the newly acquired DAI. The approval is needed for the PSM to be able to `swap` DAI for USDC.

```
proxy.doCall(
    address(dai),
    abi.encodeCall(dai.approve, (address(psm), usdsAmount))
);
```
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies the exact on-chain action ('approve the PSM to spend the newly acquired DAI'), the control mechanism (`dai.approve` for `usdsAmount`), and the direct objective (enabling `swap` DAI for USDC). It is fully quantified and executable by the operator as a mandatory step, leaving no room for interpretation.
metrics: approve the PSM to spend the newly acquired DAI
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is structurally enforced on-chain; without this approval, the Peg Stability Module (PSM) smart contract's `swap` function would revert, making violation technically impossible. The PSM's fixed-rate swap mechanism is documented in 0082c12d.

assessments.title: Calculate Swap Limit
assessments.description: Defines the formula for calculating the maximum USDC to DAI swap limit based on PSM DAI balance.
assessments.quote:
The operator must calculate the `swap` `limit` per transaction. The maximum amount of USDC that can be swapped to DAI in one transaction is calculated based on the DAI balance held by the PSM. `psmTo18ConversionFactor` converts DAI’s 18 token decimals to USDC’s 6 token decimals.

`uint256 limit = dai.balanceOf(address(psm)) / psmTo18ConversionFactor;`
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule provides a fully quantified, verifiable formula in code (`uint256 limit = dai.balanceOf(address(psm)) / psmTo18ConversionFactor;`) with defined inputs (DAI balance of the PSM, a conversion factor) and a clear output (the maximum USDC swap limit per transaction). A third party could check compliance from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule defines a limit for a swap involving the Peg Stability Module (PSM). The PSM's on-chain contract code enforces this limit automatically, making a violation impossible at the contract level. This is cited via the Peg Stability Module mechanism (0082c12d-f1a7-46ff-a4aa-5fe42ece1a4d).

assessments.title: Split Into Multiple Swaps If Limit Exceeded
assessments.description: Mandates a specific multi-step process for splitting large USDC swaps to respect PSM limits.
assessments.quote:
If the `usdcAmount` exceeds the limit, the operator must split the swap into multiple smaller swaps as follows.

1. The operator must refill the PSM with DAI by calling `psm.fill()`.
2. The operator must recalculate the limit to see how much USDC can be swapped after the refill.
3. The operator must swap the maximum possible USDC amount that doesn't exceed the limit.
4. The operator must update `remainingUsdcToSwap` by subtracting the amount just swapped.
5. The operator must repeat the process until the full `usdcAmount` is swapped.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies a precise algorithm with defined steps and function calls, but the 'limit' threshold is an input defined elsewhere, leaving a minor gap in full self-contained quantification.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The Peg Stability Module (PSM) enforces swap limits on-chain; attempting to swap more than the limit would revert, making violation impossible and automatically enforcing the need to split swaps as described.

assessments.title: SparkLend Risk Parameters Cap Automators
assessments.description: Defines parameters and authorization for dynamically adjusting Supply and Borrow Caps via Cap Automators.
assessments.quote:

The cap automator is defined in terms of three parameters:

1. `gap` - the target available exposure
2. `ttl` - the cooldown period for cap increases
3. `max` - the absolute maximum exposure

Authorized parties can update a covered Supply Cap or Borrow Cap so the available exposure is equal to the target, as long as the resulting exposure does not exceed the specified maximum limit and the cooldown period has elapsed in the case of increases to the Supply Cap or Borrow Cap.

assessments.title: Conditions For The Pre-launch Token Rewards
assessments.description: Defines the formula and allocation percentages for Spark pre-launch token rewards based on platform usage.
assessments.quote:
Spark has a pre-launch token rewards program based on the usage of its lending platform. Users of the platform will receive an airdrop of SPK tokens, depending on how much and how long they have used the platform during the pre-launch token reward period. These rewards are only for users on Ethereum Mainnet.

There are two seasons of the Spark pre-launch token rewards: Season 1 and Season 2.

Season 1 of pre-launch token rewards was active from August 20 2023 and lasted for nine months, ending on May 20 2024. 130,434,783 SPK tokens were allocated in this period.

In Season 2 14,478,261 SPK will be rewarded per month to SparkLend users who qualify for the airdrop.

Season 2 is an additional pre-farming period, which runs until the Spark Agent launches as part of Sky Endgame launch season.

The monthly SPK rewards are allocated as follows:

- 80 % is allocated to users borrowing DAI and/or USDS
- 20 % is allocated to users supplying ETH

The proposed full anti-cheat SPK Airdrop for SparkLend is calculated using the following formula:

`Airdrop = 80% * (DAI Borrows + USDS Borrows - sDAI Supplies * sDAI Liquidation Threshold - sUSDS Supplies * sUSDS Liquidation Threshold) + 20% * (ETH Supplies - ETH Borrows / ETH Liquidation Threshold)`

All supplies and borrows are denominated in USD based on the on-chain oracle price at that block to determine the conversion.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The paragraph describes a rewards program but imposes no verifiable obligation on any regulated party; it lacks 'must' or requirement language, making it a descriptive statement rather than a rule. A defender could plausibly argue it is not binding.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No enforcement mechanism applies because the paragraph does not establish a binding rule; only the generic misalignment backstop would be available, which is weak.

assessments.title: Definition
assessments.description: Requires Spark to maintain an Encumbrance Ratio below a specified Target Risk Tolerance Ratio.
assessments.quote: The Encumbrance Ratio is defined as the ratio of Spark's Required Risk Capital (RRC) to Total Risk Capital (TRC), as these terms are defined in the Sky Atlas Stability Scope ([A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.1 - Encumbrance Ratio](5435f680-aaaa-461a-bcae-4056bb8964d9)). Spark will seek to maintain a Encumbrance Ratio not greater than the Target Risk Tolerance Ratio specified in [A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.1.3 - Parameters](d65a06a6-1426-4af2-978c-cd4f7bac79b7).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The obligation is expressed qualitatively as 'seek to maintain' rather than a hard threshold, and the target ratio is delegated to another document. A defender could plausibly argue compliance even if the ratio exceeds the target, as Spark could claim it is seeking to maintain it.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is tied to this soft target; only the generic misalignment backstop applies, which is always weak.

assessments.title: Operational Process
assessments.description: Requires Spark to reduce the Encumbrance Ratio via risk capital or allocation system actions when exceeding targets.
assessments.quote:
Spark governance and contributors must take immediate action to reduce the Encumbrance Ratio when it exceeds the Target Encumbrance Ratio level. These actions may fall into two categories, risk capital actions or allocation system actions.

Risk capital actions are actions Spark takes to increase Total Risk Capital, including increasing Internal Junior Risk Capital, sourcing External Junior Risk Capital from other Prime Agents or tokenized sources, or sourcing External Senior Risk Capital from Sky or tokenized sources.

Allocation system actions involve adjusting the capital allocations within the Spark instance of the Allocation System to reduce Required Risk Capital, such as unwinding or disposing of assets requiring higher levels of risk capital as a percent of exposure.

The operational processes implemented at Spark will meet or exceed the requirements specified in the Sky Atlas at [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2 - Primes' Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management](3af8a3a2-25e5-44b3-87a4-7df1f2712685).
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete metrics (Encumbrance Ratio, Target Encumbrance Ratio) and enumerates two action categories, but the target value is not stated, 'immediate' is unquantified, and the required actions are described qualitatively without specific thresholds or deadlines.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Failure to take action could lead to a sustained breach of the Encumbrance Ratio target, which is a capital requirement violation. The Penalty Mechanisms (b8ee2d12) and Conservatorship (5c3dd35a) plausibly reach such a breach, but no consequence is quantified for this specific operational process rule, making enforcement mid.

assessments.description: Defines a fixed USDS backstop to cover risk exposures not addressed by Required Risk Capital.
assessments.quote: The Spark Product Backstop is a fixed value of USDS, updated from time to time by Spark governance via the Spark SubDAO Proxy Policy Changes process ([A.6.1.1.1.3.4.1.1 - Spark SubDAO Proxy Policy Changes](90240e75-6e5f-4a54-8999-ee430cfcf20d)), meant to cover the anticipated risk exposures to Spark products that are not covered under Sky’s Required Risk Capital framework.

assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism is mentioned or implied; only the generic misalignment/adjudication backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Evaluation Method
assessments.description: Defines the formula for computing Target SubDAO Proxy Value using risk capital, backstops, and expense reserves.
assessments.quote:
Target SubDAO Proxy Value is computed as the greater of Required Risk Capital (RRC) plus Spark Product Backstop, or Operational Expense Reserve.

RRC is calculated as the higher of current RRC or highest RRC incurred within the RRC Lookback Period, divided by Risk Tolerance Ratio ([A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.1 - Encumbrance Ratio](9995ba51-1de7-4b32-8b76-a71462dc4c5b)).

Spark Product Backstop is set manually by Spark governance per [A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.2.1.3 - Spark Product Backstop Definition](ac10196b-18b2-4bc4-8627-0cacac8a3524).

Operational expense reserve is calculated as the higher of past month’s operating expenses multiplied by Target Runway (in months), or total operating expenses incurred in trailing period equal to Target Runway.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a formula for Target SubDAO Proxy Value with concrete steps, but the Spark Product Backstop is set manually by governance, and other parameters (Risk Tolerance Ratio, RRC Lookback Period, Target Runway) are defined elsewhere without values, making the overall obligation mixed.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: No specific enforcement mechanism reaches this definitional rule; only the generic misalignment backstop applies.

assessments.title: Operational Process
assessments.description: Multisigs manage vault liquidity via taker roles and rate limits to maintain target liquidity configurations.
assessments.quote:
The Spark Prime Relayer Multisig will execute transactions to ensure liquidity within Spark Savings vaults is aligned with the Target Liquidity configurations specified in Target Liquidity Current Configuration, up to the total amount of user deposits in a given Spark Savings vault. This will be implemented via control of the taker role in the vault and transferAsset rate limit from Spark Liquidity Layer ALM Proxy to the vault.

In normal conditions, this will be automated via the ALM Planner software. If the Prime Relayer Multisig fails to maintain Spark Savings vault liquidity in alignment with the Target Liquidity configurations, the Core Operator Relayer Multisig is empowered to effectuate transactions to achieve this.

No numeric threshold, formula, or cadence is provided.

assessments.title: Counterparty Requirements
assessments.description: Mandates borrower registration, sanction compliance, and solvency requirements for loans funded via Arkis Infrastructure.
assessments.quote:
Borrowers funded via Arkis Infrastructure must be duly registered by competent authorities in their primary jurisdiction, and must not be subject to sanctions by the US, UK, EU, or UN. Responsibility for verifying KYC/KYB and meeting related compliance requirements is handled by Arkis during the borrower onboarding process.

Borrowers must not be insolvent at the time of loan origination or renewal. Borrowers will self-certify their solvency as part of loan agreements. If a borrower becomes insolvent or enters administration while having an active loan, the entire loan amount becomes due and payable and Arkis may immediately liquidate collateral to recover the loan balance.

assessments.title: Permitted Actions
assessments.description: Defines authorized actions for contributors regarding smart contract deployment, multisig establishment, and asset movement constraints.
assessments.quote:
Designated Contributors are permitted to take any actions reasonably necessary to facilitate the deployment, configuration, testing, maintenance, and operational readiness of a Confidential Strategic Integration and Deployment. Such actions may include deployment and configuration of smart contracts, establishment of multisigs or administrative control systems, deployment and configuration of Spark Savings or Morpho vault infrastructure, operation of relayer or frontend infrastructure, and related implementation activities.

Confidential Strategic Integrations and Deployments may remain undisclosed while applicable confidentiality obligations remain in effect, provided that the governance acceptance and disclosure requirements set forth in this section are satisfied.

For the avoidance of doubt, this authorization does not permit deployment or allocation of Spark treasury assets, Spark Liquidity Layer assets, governance-controlled capital, or other protocol-owned funds, except as otherwise expressly authorized through Spark governance processes. Nothing herein prohibits the movement or allocation of assets voluntarily deposited by users into a Confidential Strategic Partnership and Deployment through preconfigured product functionality established prior to public launch, provided that such functionality remains subject to the limitations and governance acceptance requirements set forth in this section.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names the actor ('Designated Contributors'), enumerates permitted activity categories (smart contract deployment, multisig establishment, Spark Savings/Morpho vault infrastructure, relayer/frontend operation), and states a specific prohibition on deploying or allocating Spark treasury, liquidity layer, governance-controlled, or other protocol-owned funds except through Spark governance. However, the operative permission standard is qualitative ('reasonably necessary'), and governance acceptance/disclosure requirements are referenced but not specified with numeric thresholds, formulas, or deadlines.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: Because this rule is part of the Spark Agent Artifacts, Core GovOps Agent Artifact Review (d4bf73e7-2f9f-454c-8add-614dff784f78) plausibly reaches violations such as unauthorized deployment/allocation of protocol-owned funds or actions outside the permitted scope through scheduled review, published outcomes, and penalty assessment; however, no consequence is quantified for this specific rule, so enforcement is mid.

Spark protocol coverage will only be conveyed if Spark governance explicitly votes to extend coverage to a specific deployment or products after public launch and full disclosure of the deployment or product details.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule names concrete parameters (Confidential Strategic Integrations and Deployments framework, Spark governance vote, public launch, full disclosure) and states a clear binary condition for insurance coverage, but the criteria for 'full disclosure' and 'public launch' are qualitative and no numeric thresholds or metrics are provided.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is a disclaimer defining the scope of insurance coverage, not an obligation on any actor. No violation can occur, so no enforcement mechanism reaches it; only the generic misalignment backstop would apply, which is weak.

assessments.title: Modification
assessments.description: Requires Atlas Edit Proposals for multisig signer changes except for specific self-reported access loss or removal requests.
assessments.quote:
Modification of the signers of the Freezer Multisig must be approved through an Atlas Edit Proposal.

The only exceptions to this are if: 1) a signer self-reports a loss of access to their private key due to any reason; or 2) a signer explicitly expresses their wish to be removed as a signer. In both cases, the signer is required to communicate the loss of access to their private key, or the wish to be removed as a signer, in the form of a public Sky Forum post. The specific signer should be replaced as soon as possible.

Any changes to the Multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious. Where malicious activity is suspected, the Core Facilitator must prepare an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the Multisig.
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule defines a clear primary obligation (Atlas Edit Proposal approval) and enumerated exceptions with a required communication method (Sky Forum post). assessments.title: Tokenized Treasury Owner Role
assessments.description: Defines OWNER_ROLE authority over fees and roles, managed via a TimelockController with specific executor and canceller roles.
assessments.quote: The `OWNER_ROLE` on a Tokenized Treasury Instance is authorized to set purchase and redemption fee rates within bounds established by the `MANAGER_ADMIN_ROLE`, and to grant or revoke any role in the contract. The `OWNER_ROLE` is held by an OpenZeppelin `TimelockController` operated by the credit token issuer. The operator, acting as a Relayer, calls `depositPSM` to deposit `amount` of `asset` from the ALM Proxy into the PSM, receiving the corresponding PSM `shares` in return. ```

assessments.title: Call swapUSDSToUSDC Function
assessments.description: Defines the relayer-only process and technical requirements for swapping USDS to USDC via the PSM.
assessments.quote:
Only an operator with the relayer role can swap USDS to USDC via the PSM. To do so, they must call the swapUSDSToUSDC function on the Controller contract on mainnet, providing the usdcAmount (denominated in 1e6 precision to match PSM USDC handling). The operation will only succeed if the ALM Proxy holds at least the equivalent amount of USDS for the swap; otherwise, the transaction will revert. The rate limit configuration serves as whitelisting for swaps. Calling this function will carry out the following actions:

- The contract will confirm the relayer status of the operator. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert.
- The contract will ensure the swap amount is within the allowed rate limit (LIMIT_USDS_TO_USDC) for the PSM.
- The contract will convert the USDC amount to an 18-decimal format using psmTo18ConversionFactor.
- The contract will approve the daiUsds contract to spend the converted amount from the ALM Proxy.
- The contract will swap USDS to DAI at a 1:1 ratio via daiUsds, sending DAI to the proxy.
- The contract will approve the PSM to spend the DAI.
- The contract will swap DAI to USDC at a 1:1 ratio with no fee via psm.buyGemNoFee, sending USDC to the proxy.

The function call is as follows:

`function swapUSDSToUSDC(uint256 usdcAmount) external`
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies an exact function name, parameter (usdcAmount in 1e6 precision), a complete sequence of on-chain actions, and clearly defined verifiable conditions (relayer role, rate limit, USDS balance). All elements are objectively checkable from the text alone.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The function's on-chain checks—relayer role, rate limit, and USDS balance—cause an automatic revert if violated. This self-executing enforcement is a core property of the Peg Stability Module (0082c12d), which maintains peg integrity through contract-enforced swap conditions.

assessments.title: Call swapUSDCToUSDS Function
assessments.description: Defines the operational logic and role requirements for swapping USDC to USDS via the PSM.
assessments.quote:
Only an operator with the relayer role can swap USDC to USDS via the PSM. To do so, they must call the `swapUSDCToUSDS` function on the Controller contract on mainnet, providing the usdcAmount (denominated in 1e6 precision to match PSM USDC handling). The operation will only succeed if the ALM Proxy holds at least the amount of USDC specified for the swap; otherwise, the transaction will revert. The rate limit configuration serves as whitelisting for swaps. Calling this function will carry out the following actions:

- The contract will confirm the relayer status of the operator. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert.
- The contract will ensure the swap amount is within the allowed rate limit (LIMIT_USDC_TO_USDS) for the PSM.
- The contract will approve the PSM to spend the USDC from the ALM Proxy.
- The contract will calculate the swap limit per transaction based on the DAI balance held by the PSM, converting with psmTo18ConversionFactor.
- If the usdcAmount is less than or equal to the limit, the contract will perform a direct swap of USDC to DAI.
- If the usdcAmount exceeds the limit, the contract will split the swap into multiple smaller swaps: refill the PSM with DAI via psm.fill, recalculate the limit, swap the maximum allowed amount, update the remaining amount, and repeat until complete (reverting with "DssLitePsm/nothing-to-fill" if PSM cannot be filled).
- The contract will convert the USDC amount to a DAI amount, accounting for token decimal differences.
- The contract will approve the daiUsds contract to spend the DAI amount from the ALM Proxy.
- The contract will swap DAI to USDS at a 1:1 ratio via daiUsds, sending USDS to the proxy.

The function call is as follows:

`function swapUSDCToUSDS(uint256 usdcAmount) external`
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule precisely defines the function's behavior, including the caller role, input precision, revert conditions, and step-by-step logic. However, the rate limit value (LIMIT_USDC_TO_USDS) and conversion factor (psmTo18ConversionFactor) are named but not numerically specified, leaving minor gaps.

assessments.title: Call swapUSDSToUSDC Function
assessments.description: Defines the relayer-only process and technical constraints for swapping USDS to USDC via the PSM.
assessments.quote:
Only an operator with the relayer role can swap USDS to USDC via the PSM. To do so, they must call the `swapUSDSToUSDC` function on the Controller contract on mainnet, providing the usdcAmount (denominated in 1e6 precision to match PSM USDC handling). The operation will only succeed if the ALM Proxy holds at least the equivalent amount of USDS for the swap; otherwise, the transaction will revert. The rate limit configuration serves as whitelisting for swaps. Calling this function will carry out the following actions:

- The contract will confirm the relayer status of the operator. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert.
- The contract will ensure the swap amount is within the allowed rate limit (LIMIT_USDS_TO_USDC) for the PSM.
- The contract will convert the USDC amount to an 18-decimal format using psmTo18ConversionFactor.
- The contract will approve the daiUsds contract to spend the converted amount from the ALM Proxy.
- The contract will swap USDS to Dai at a 1:1 ratio via daiUsds, sending Dai to the proxy.
- The contract will approve the PSM to spend the Dai.
- The contract will swap Dai to USDC at a 1:1 ratio with no fee via psm.buyGemNoFee, sending USDC to the proxy.

The function call is as follows:

`function swapUSDSToUSDC(uint256 usdcAmount) external`
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule specifies the exact actor (relayer role), function name, contract, parameter precision (1e6), success conditions (ALM Proxy USDS balance, rate limit), and step-by-step actions. All conditions are objectively verifiable on-chain.
metrics: ALM Proxy holds at least the equivalent amount of USDS
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The function call is enforced on-chain: the contract automatically reverts if the caller lacks the relayer role, the swap exceeds the rate limit, or the ALM Proxy has insufficient USDS. This is self-executing via the Peg Stability Module (UUID 0082c12d...), which governs the PSM.

assessments.title: Call swapUSDCToUSDS Function
assessments.description: Defines the operational logic and role requirements for swapping USDC to USDS via the PSM.
assessments.quote:
Only an operator with the relayer role can swap USDC to USDS via the PSM. To do so, they must call the `swapUSDCToUSDS` function on the Controller contract on mainnet, providing the usdcAmount (denominated in 1e6 precision to match PSM USDC handling). The operation will only succeed if the ALM Proxy holds at least the amount of USDC specified for the swap; otherwise, the transaction will revert. The rate limit configuration serves as whitelisting for swaps. Calling this function will carry out the following actions:

- The contract will confirm the relayer status of the operator. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert.
- The contract will ensure the swap amount is within the allowed rate limit (LIMIT_USDC_TO_USDS) for the PSM.
- The contract will approve the PSM to spend the USDC from the ALM Proxy.
- The contract will calculate the swap limit per transaction based on the Dai balance held by the PSM, converting with psmTo18ConversionFactor.
- If the usdcAmount is less than or equal to the limit, the contract will perform a direct swap of USDC to Dai.
- If the usdcAmount exceeds the limit, the contract will split the swap into multiple smaller swaps: refill the PSM with Dai via psm.fill, recalculate the limit, swap the maximum allowed amount, update the remaining amount, and repeat until complete (reverting with "DssLitePsm/nothing-to-fill" if PSM cannot be filled).
- The contract will convert the USDC amount to a Dai amount, accounting for token decimal differences.
- The contract will approve the daiUsds contract to spend the Dai amount from the ALM Proxy.
- The contract will swap Dai to USDS at a 1:1 ratio via daiUsds, sending USDS to the proxy.

The function call is as follows:

`function swapUSDCToUSDS(uint256 usdcAmount) external`
assessments.precisenessReasoning: The rule states a clear, binary condition: only an operator with the relayer role can call the function. The function's behavior and failure conditions are fully specified, making compliance objectively verifiable on-chain.
assessments.enforcementReasoning: The rule is self-enforcing via smart contract code (transaction reverts if caller lacks relayer role), but no mechanism doc from the catalog or the text covers this on-chain access control; without a citable UUID, enforcement is rated weak per rubric.
